reviews.comment: She's caring and stuff but she explains things so confusingly. It could be the most straight forward assignment and somehow everyone is confused because she used 10 pages to explain it. Even the syllabus is SEVENTY THREE pages long. She literally confuses everyone. Even though I got a good grade I felt like I was going insane reading instructions

She's a good professor, but for being a half-online class, it is the most work I have ever done. It's just busy work, but it gets annoying doing it every week. It's all group work, so it's not that difficult in class. If you miss class, you have to do alternative work, which is much harder than the in-person work, so you should just show up.

She is decent. I personally never had a love for the topic so I didn't find the class that enteraining.
Its all group work so being in class is a must you get 3 skips for the semester
The group work isnt bad its just sometimes annoying to do when you have alot of other schoolwork to do
Mostly it is in class work though, final needs is done outside

Professor Bierema is a very nice lady, but I genuinely would not recommend taking this class in person if it is a requirement. Her D2L is terribly organized and the instructions for assignments are overwhelming. No examples are given, and she generally gives overly detailed explanations that make understanding worse. Not content.

Bierema is kind and clearly cares about the wellbeing of her students. She's easy to reach out to and gives lots of reminders about due dates and homework. D2L-wise, this is the most organized class I've ever had. There is a lot of work in this class, but it's super easy and Bierema is an easy grader.  Show up to class, look at the checklist, easy.

She's a really nice professor. The class I took was only once a week, and you definitely had to go to receive credit for the in class assignments. But the in class assignments were so easy and you got to do them with ur table ur assigned. I never felt like the class was too difficult or stressful.

She is the kindest professor I've ever had. She cares about her students and not deadlines & grades. The second I told her I was have a mental health episode, she immediately created a plan with me to get back on my feet and didnt question or shame me in any way. If I could take her course again I would. The class is easy just a lot, stay organized
She's a nice lady but the workload is CRAZY for a gen Ed class. It's like she wants you to fail with how confusing her assignments are.

Dr. Bierema is a really personable professor. My class was hybrid, once a week. She had lots of Packbacks each week but the structure was really simple in her class. One presentation for the whole semester with a group. Seems super caring and biomed was scaring me but her course was really simple. Would take her again. Easy 4.0 if u stay on task.

Professor Bierema was very nice, but the course material was extremely confusing. The book you have to read has little to nothing to do with what you learn or do in the class and is only relevant to some of the homework. If you don't like working in randomly assigned groups, this class is not for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you want to take a class where you use 4 different sites to do things that can be accomplished on D2L here you go. Grading criteria ranges from clear for the final project to impressively vague. It really seems like she does the least possible work while giving her students a massive amount. The textbook is extremely odd and uncomfortable.

She's a nice person, but she gives so much unnecessary "busy work". It's a big class, but she doesn't lecture much, the class is heavily based on group work and there is not much individual work. She makes the content understandable, but at times it is uncomfortable and weird. Overall, she's very understanding but I would not take the class again.
She's nice, big classroom

Please please please if you have her as an option to take, do it. This was the easiest class I've taken and she was super super nice and an easy 4.0. She barely gives homework maybe two things a week and there's never a test or quiz. The majority of your grade is graded based off completion and not even correctness.

Mrs. Bierema was literally the sweetest. She is an amazing professor and the class isn't difficult at all. Highly suggest taking it if you need credit. There are quizzes and class activities so make sure you go to class but usually its only one day a week.

Professor Bierema was the easiest professor Ive had this semester. Isb 204 is a hybrid course but once you get the hang of the weekly routine its nothing. I HIGHLY recommend you take advantage of all the extra credit she offers cuz it helps boost your grade. But overall, easy 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really bad class.
Really unprepared professor. Nonsensical tasks
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Allen. She has a wonderful personality and seems to care about student's well-being. She also cares about the deeper meaning behind what she teaches. Class work is a lot, but if you set some time aside to do the work, read instructions, and ask questions, this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She treats students like children and does not care about them, uses jingles to get their attention and does pointless exercises that actually stifle creativity. She tries to be all sunshine and roses but you can tell she doesn't want to be there because she is treating it like free association. One of the worst classes I have ever been in.

Probably one of the most lackluster classes I have ever taken. I have no idea how this syllabus has been approved. It is all over the place and the professor talks about being progressive but does not offer accommodations if you experience an emergency. Truly performative in the lectures and in practice.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The hw is not difficult, but it is EXTREMELY time consuming. It's only 2 hours, but it somehow manages to feel like the longest 2 hours of your life. The students are often treated like children; with name tags and jinglebells to get our attention. If I can save one poor soul from this class, then my mission is complete.
JeanaDee Allen means well, but for a level 100 class I do more work in some of my 300/400 combine. If at all take another CAS class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Allen is awesome. The assignments may take a long time, but she is incredibly understanding and wants the best for her students. I highly recommend taking this class and the lectures are always worth going to. Professor Allen gives out a ton of extra credit, but you will get an easy 4.0 in this class.
lot's of workload and she played ecco2k in class

This professor was professional and responsive, making the online asynchronous CAS 110 class engaging. The course included quizzes, activities, and assignments, but for a 100-level class, the workload felt time-consuming. Graded on a 1000-point scale for a 4.0, the class was fun, useful, and covered a unique topic that changes every semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This asynchronous course featured creative assignments, weekly quizzes, and a midterm interview that emphasized experiential learning. The professor was fantastic—always approachable and ready to help with questions, providing great support. Perfect for students seeking a well-structured course that fosters creativity and critical thinking!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: allen is a nice lady but eccentric and IMO annoying. she does genuinely care though. this class is an introvert's worst nightmare; when u meet, u are forced to talk to everyone in the class. work is fairly easy and the assignments can actually be fun. no tests or reading. light work. only complaint is that her grading seems very random

A great professor and I enjoyed the class. There are a few homework assignments but nothing hard to complete. My class was hybrid so the times we met once a month in class were important because it's a big part of grading. Overall, it was a good class and easy to complete.

The topics is interesting, but the quality of instruction is fairly poor. The exams are incredibly difficult and not much help from the provided study guide. The instructors only read off the slides and expect us to know what's happening when we evaluate in the barns. Would not recommend the class if you don't have to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Garmyn is a fun professor and for FSC433 there are a lot of lectures and ton of content, but the labs make it fun. The final group project is graded on if you put in work and learned something rather than how well it turned out. Exams are long, but manageable if you study. She is very relaxed with grading and looks for effort over correctness.

Haven't finished the class yet, but professor Garmyn is great for an easy 3.5-4.0 class to boost your GPA! While the only thing I disliked was that she didn't answer or take questions till after class, whatever thought you wanted to ask, save it till the end. Reads off Powerpoint slides, exams are easy, same for homework and quizzes, Iclicker grade
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I dont know why students had issues with her. She was amazing and her class was very easy. Yes lectures were just her reading off slides but that made this class easy. Exams matched the homework and quizzes.  I enjoyed this class she was very clear with expectations and easy to get ahold of.

She was decent. Her lectures mainly consisted of her reading off of lecture slides the whole time but at least the class was short. Homework is graded off completion and quizzes are questions right from the homework so that wasn't too bad. Exams are a bit hard but if you study the homework and quizzes it isn't awful. Overall an okay professor.

Her class is pretty boring and I barely listened in class but all of her assignments are pretty easy and she mainly grades them for completion. Her exams were kind of hard but studying the homework assignments really helped.

Most boring prof Ive ever had. Attendance is mandatory, because if it werent people wouldnt bother to show up. The whole class period is her reading off PowerPoint slides. Every Day. Three times a week. For the whole semester. The class itself isnt very difficult but unless you REALLY care about meat, dont plan staying awake in this class.
She left for 5 weeks mid semester for a trip and had 2 TA's running class and barely knew how.
Professor never answers email and disappears for weeks at a time.

To be honest her class is pretty easy. There are in class questions you must answer for attendance/grade, but class material is pretty easy. Exams are half multiple choice half written but again not hard. She is gone doing research a lot so will have canceled classes/ TA ran classes which is nice. My downfall was not paying attention in class

Dr. Peters is super nice! She taught half of the lectures, and Dr. Peacor taught the other half. I think that she had simpler topics, so it was easier to understand her. The rest of the class was quite difficult outside of her lectures. Something that made things a bit difficult was her lack of study materials for exams.
I love Dr. Peters. She genuinely cares about her students, and I love the way she teaches her classes. I recommend every student take her class.

I loved Dr. Peters! I enjoyed taking her Great Lakes Bio class. It wasn't a ton of work and the quizzes felt fair. This semester, she offered that if you had over a 90% in the class you didn't have to take the final exam so make sure you attend class! There were no attendance drops but a few chances for extra credit.

Dr. Peters is a great professor! She obviously knows what she's talking about and welcomes any questions or comments on the material. She makes an effort to get to know the class and lectures are engaging and interesting. Attendance is not required but participation matters! Exams are written response but easy if you go to class and participate.

Dr. Peters is a good professor and she is obviously very knowledgeable in her field. However, her grading is weird sometimes and her quizzes/tests are all short answer. I would take her class again, but be prepared for it to be slightly unorganized and for her to be gone several lectures.

Dr. Peters cares a lot about her students and works hard to know everyones name. She makes a fairly large class feel close knit. The assignments are varying and cater to many different types of learners. She is readily available to help whenever. I hope I can go with her on the study abroad this summer! She's overall just a great person.
Good teacher easy course
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof, super nice, forgiving on missing pts on assignments/exams. Just show up to class, and if u can't email them and u can get points back. Not too much homework, exams were very fair, and lectures were engaging that helped prepare for the exams. Need more profs like her

Dr. Peters is a funny person and makes lectures fun. She rarely assigns homework (BS162) and grades very forgivingly on exams. The ONLY downside of taking her/BS162 is attendance is mandatory and if you miss one day, it takes your participation grade down about 3%, which is annoying but other than that I would recommend her to anyone who asked!

Peters is a great professor. The main reason I liked her class was because the practice exams matched up to the actual exams very well. You never had to worry about not knowing what was going to be on the exam. The amount of homework was very fair and when we did have homework it was not very difficult or time consuming at all.

BS 162 was a lot easier than BS 161. Everything you need to know for the exams Dr. Peters goes over in class. All tests are free response but they are really similar to the practice tests. Attendance is not mandatory technically but there is a google form you have to fill out each class. If you attend most lectures you will get a good grade.

absolutely NO amber slander.  science does not come easy to me. but ive gained SO much confidence in this class. Amber is approachable, shes funny, and shes inspiring. class material is easy to digest yet difficult too. but if you pay attention, ask questions, and do the practice exams  common homework, you'll be fine.

I loved Dr. Peters! She tries her hardest to make the class easy for her students. 35% of our final grade was based on homework (most of them being in-class activities), so make sure you do those. The exams are spaced out well and they are not too hard as long as you pay attention the lectures and do the Common Homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Honestly, I thought this class was so annoying. The class material is boring, not sure why any pre-med would want to learn it. Tests are all short answers which is so annoying, make it multiple choice like any normal class come on. Also, they take 3 weeks to grade your exams which is absolutely ridiculous. Should consider changing class format.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Peters is great! Her lectures make a lot of sense and her in-class questions really help the material "stick." Peppy and approachable, making the best of online classes. Her tests and homework are fair, just pay attention in class and you'll do fine. Stuff takes a while to get graded though.

One major problem I had with this class was how LONG it took to find out grades for exams, like a good 3 weeks even though theres 5 TAs and lecture is only about 150 people so that bothers me. Other than that, her exams are very easy and Amber relates a lot of her lectures to everyday life and her own life and was a great teacher and person.
Very cool teacher. She was super straight forward and the tests were exactly what we learned in class. However, all tests included short answer!

she is so unorganized and the pickiest grader ever on exams its so ridiculous. exams are all free response. the material isnt hard but shes so picky on grading that in the end she has to curve the class. shes a really nice lady and the final is group which is nice. but still, shes just so freaking picky on grading
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Amber Peter's class. You form a group to work with at the beginning of the year. The final is taken with your group. She gives a lot of study materials for the class. One thing I would complain about is that she posts homework and other useful documents very last minute. Overall great class and much better than BS161.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amber is super nice! There is homework every week and it is posted over weekend, kinda inconvenient but the homework was usually really easy, I usually did Btwn classes. Exams are straight to the point with great study guides. The group work is nothing to worry about, its mostly discussion with each other in class 4 particp, no agonizing projects.

Lectures are kind of long, the class was a bit disorganized, and in-class group assignments got a bit tedious, but the work was fairly simple and the exams/tests/quizzes were near mirrored to practices.

To begin with, Amber has an extremely annoying voice and her voice makes it hard to sit through a 2 hour lecture. She is also very disorganized. If we have a homework assignment due on Tuesday, don't expect it to be posted before Sunday. Everyday in class there is an in class assignment and it can get a little annoying.

For better or for worse, there's not much that I can go into detail about Amber. This course, like most ISP courses, was one I, speaking on behalf of most of the students in the class, was not eager about taking. With all negative remarks and low expectations aside, she elaborated fairly succinctly on the causes and effects of climate change.

This is the most ridiculous class I've ever had the displeasure of taking.  Prof and TAs are rampantly disorganized, the material covered belongs in a high school classroom, and there is a ridiculous amount of busywork assigned.  I become physically ill during labs due to the utter stupidity of the tasks we are told to undertake.  Avoid.
She is an effective, helpful instructor. Her class format was quite good. She's very/too nice. Note to other students: SHUT UP while she is lecturing. No one is paying to listen to you!

Absolutely loved him, he's very nice and helpful. He will stop lecture and explain everything if you missed something, and if you get a chance to talk to him after/outside of class, he is super helpful and very nice. Would definitely recommend and if I could, I would have him teach all of my math courses!

Not the best professor you can have for Calc 3, but he is very good, thoroughly explains the content and goes step by step to complete complex problems. If you go to his lectures without fail and understand the concepts, you're gonna succeed in his class.
Little cousin jokes made learning calc 2 bearable

Similar to the majority of my peers, I quickly stopped attending Calculus II lectures. Instead I watched the videos/self taught. His accent, handwriting, and lecture pacing made in person lectures difficult to comprehend. Quizzes are weekly and can be difficult. MTH 133 is a rigorous course, the average final exam grade this semester was a 43% GLHF

If you don't watch the video lectures ahead of class (which I don't recall ever being told to do, I just did it because I was super lost) then the in-person lecture is useless because he does a lot of proofs. Just do the homework and you're fine.

Nice guy, makes jokes in class. I can see why some wouldn't like his fast-paced lectures, but I found them helpful because he then had time for lots of example problems. Lectures are not required and there are videos of it on D2L.

A lot of people complain about his lectures but I actually found them very useful and digestible. I understand peoples' complaints but his lecture style reflects "different strokes for different folks." He goes through the theorems and concepts very quickly, but he provides many examples after which I find more helpful. Take notes and go to lecture
All I can say is, meh.

I love Abbas, his lectures are thorough and well explained. Even if you don't like his lectures, you can always not attend lectures and instead watch videos on D2L from professor Maccombs, who is also an amazing professor. Overall the class is difficult but you have many options on how you want to approach the material.

Very bad lectures that would be a waste of my time. I never learned anything from him and had to spend many hours trying to learn to succeed in this class. Not helpful at all though he makes funny jokes.

Nice guy, but his lectures move way too fast to take notes on, much less understand. We had only three 50 minute sessions a week and yet he would speed through his notes and let us out 5-10 minutes early despite the intensity and volume of the material. I found Calc III to be easier than Calc II but I would not recommend taking it with Prof. Abbas.
The professor himself is fine. Nice, explains things well, and is very approachable. However, the class itself is just hard. No other way around it.

Great guy who cares and knows what he's talking about but has so flaws in his lectures. He can be fast with his notes and has a lot of words/explanations/theorems. Other than that, I can't blame the guy, the class is hard in general. The quizzes and exams have T/F questions that would screw me over. 100% on the written part but 60% at the end.

He was such a nice professor, and would answer any questions you brought to him, but about half way through the semester, his lectures didn't make sense. He didn't explain much to us, he just re wrote his notes for us to copy down. We normally did a couple example problems in class, but he didn't explain the steps he just did them.
Horrible Handwriting, would leave lectures without understanding anything, he proceeds really fast and its hard to grasp all the topics hes teaching

He will consistently bring up thought-provoking philosophical questions such as why people so universally conform to silly naming conventions such as "u substitution" and "p-series."  He realizes not all students will need to use Calc II in life.  So, he gives them philosophical wisdom instead.  This is what sets his lectures apart Ryan's videos.

Casim is just a huge meme between me and my friends. With his little jokes about the Stone Age to the caveman method, he got funny little jokes. He lectures quite well but his handwriting is not very easy to read at all. As a professor in any other class I would take him again, but as the professor for Calc 2 again, it depends on how you learn.
Not Casim's fault, but this class was super hard. He made the lectures almost enjoyable to attend. Ask questions, do the homework, and put in the time and you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy, so incredibly funny. His lectures were clear and useful for WebWork. Just make sure you go to recitation and take the quizzes. The exams are not bad if you study using the old exams that they provide. 10/10 recommend this guy, he's a gem

What a guy. Abbas is a German genius mathematician with a slick accent. He's always cracking little jokes, bringing a little light to a very dull and stale topic. The class is stone cold. But that's not gonna change with a different prof. Plus lectures aren't mandatory because he posts his notes online. Go to recitation for the quizzes.

I love Abbas with all my heart! Having him as a prof is like having a genius grandpa teach you math; super approachable &clearly cares for students. Explains ideas well&can offer alternative explanations. Writes down everything he says and posts online; this can be annoying in class but makes it easy to miss class, but don't skip- he's super funny!
Loved the guy. Interesting despite the topic and always cracks jokes. Easy grader and throws a huge curve at the end of the semester.
It's not an easy class, but he definitely helps. The homework problems are very similar to those on the quizzes and tests.
I love this guy, really cool!

Funny guy, really smart.  If you're naturally good at math this class won't be too bad.  I would avoid skipping as he covers about a section a lecture.  Homework is tough, but the quizzes and exams are quite easy.

Sharp guy, expects a lot from his students--sometimes I think he confuses us with his grad students. He doesn't always work out solutions to the homework problems before he assigns them, which can turn into long and grueling homework sessions. Homework took roughly ten hours a week, often more. However, it was definitely worth being in his class.
Homework due twice a week- very hard. Tests (2 exams and a final) were easier than the homework. Quizzes once a week. Difficult class, but some interesting proofs. Funny guy
This professor was terrible.
The class was hard, but not beyond what someone in an Honors math class should be able to manage. He gave up his own time for a problem session, and was helpful with office hours. Highly recommended

Very very difficult, even for an honors course. Not impossible though: a good challenge for someone looking to do well in a math career. He explains well, but the material can be so murky that it is still takes time to sift through. Gave up his own time to give us an unofficial recitation session: I highly recommend him.
Great teacher, commited to helping students understand Calculus and do well in the class.
excellent communications ability
hes hilarious, i liked the lectures
He's a really good professor and does a lot of examples to help you understand.  I would definitely recommend him.
Abbas is the****.
I like him because I understand him when he teaches me in class.
Abbas is hilarious!!!
He's not a great prof, but he's a damn genius and he's really funny.

The quizzes are worded in ways that try to trick you. The module are assignments are so much for no reason. She is a strict grader, and half of the assignments ask questions that were never discussed in the lecture or readings. I watched every lecture video, did every reading, took in-depth notes for both, and still struggled on the assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Sarkissian had a lecture everyday about the content we read for class. Throughout the slides, she would include iClicker questions that counted for attendance and participation. They were often easy, and she would pause to review. The exams were easy if you paid attention in class and there were many opportunities to earn full credit.

This is a 300-level course, which is upper-level in the PLS department, so expect a lot of reading (4 texts) and writing. Prof. Sarkissian is great, but you cannot wing this class. This is a discussion-based course, so you are expected to participate. There is a participation grade, discussion posts, three essay exams, and a book report.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly avoid taking this class if you're looking to 4.0. The content and course itself is very simple and easy, as it should be for an introductory level class. However, the exams are purposely worded in a way to trick you. Also note that an A in this class is a 93-100.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: 4 Exams, lowest is dropped and the other points come from participation points that come from attending lectures, answering pop questions via iclicker, easy enough if you do the reading and pay minimal attention to lecture. Issue is in the exams, multi-choice questions feel completely random, rubric for essay is there but not applied to grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tough test grader despite simple material. Does Iclicker quizzes with lots of dumb/poorly worded/trick questions. Only missed 1-2 classes the whole semester but got a 75% attendance grade because the clicker quizzes were so dumb. Not an unbearable class but frustrating at times.

Professor Sarkissian is extremely knowledgeable about political science. The course itself is pretty straightforward but exam questions can be tricky sometimes. I really enjoyed this class and I appreciate her answering my questions on politics inside and outside the class. Participation portion is easy to achieve points. No extra credit options.

Extremely hard grader on exams, homework, and even in-class participation. Hours of homework per night. Lectures are based solely on homework discussion questions, isn't really teaching you anything, just talking about the book. Very blunt, says she doesn't understand your thinking and doesn't offer any suggestions to do better. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this Professor's lectures. This was my first political science class I took. At first I was hesitant about poli sci but this professor made me truly consider continuing to study political science. She really knows what she's talking about and I believe she loves teaching comparative politics. She is also really nice and friendly.

Very kind, understanding & inspirational. She knows that Poli Sci has got some confusing concepts sometimes & will absolutely make time to help you. She loves answering questions & makes sure students don't hesitate to ask. Ask her about any current political events you are curious about too! It actually really helps you connect course concepts!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Sarkissian is a very good professor and very funny. She clearly cares about her students and our wellbeing, inside and outside the classroom. Very little homework besides reading the textbook, which is $1 per chapter, and you only need 11 chapters. Very clear and good at explaining things in lecture with good conversations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Sarkissian was not only a very effective lecturer, but was very engaging as well. Her depth of knowledge with comparative politics is inspiring and I had fun with learning the materials. Her exams require you to understand the lectures/textbook readings well and encourages you to consistently analyze the context around what we're learning.

This professor was one of my better online instructors. Her lectures were clear and very easy to follow. The textbook was only $11. Criteria of assignments was very specific. The only downside is that tests could be a bit tricky, I never scored higher than an 80% but grades can be made up with other assignments.

No feedback on exams (makes it impossible to tell what did you get wrong since you can't even access the blank exam afterwards). Posts some video lectures the day before the exam. Midterm 2 is a cumulative exam which makes no sense. Lots of extra credit so people tend to like him.

The best chemistry professor I have had in my 4 years here. Lecture isn't required but I would recommend still going because he explains things in ways that make it so much easier to understand. Quizzes and exams are open note/you get a cheat sheet and it's basically impossible to fail this class.

Bazgir is an amazing professor, and is truly the only reason I did so well in Orgo. With every lecture, he made them entertaining and engaged with the class, always making sure that you understand the material before moving on. If you have the chance, take Ayoob Bazgir!
Very interesting class. Professor is chill and relaxed, and content material is very easy. Would definitely recommend!
Great professor! explains organic chemistry in a simple way that allows everyone to understand! gives a lot of extra credit!

He makes chemistry so easy with his comparisons to real-world analysis. He truly wants all his students to see how complex concepts can be broken down in simple ways. He allows students to engage during lectures free of shame. He makes funny jokes and does call-and-responses so we all stay engaged. 10% EC boost to your grade. Everyone loves him

I would go to war for him
- gives a lot of extra credit
- extra tries on the hw if you ask
- he will help on quizzes and tests
- he wants you to pass

Great prof, lots of opportunities for extra credits, I got a OK Exams and quizzes but bcs I did all the hws and extra credits, which you got tons of time for btw, and I got a 4.0. If you miss his lectures, the video lecture are still great and they are not too long. Most lectures he also lets you leave early which is great. great prof, good man.

Professor Bazgir is very knowledgeable and offers many resources to for you to succeed in his class. Although I would still recommend studying with peers outside of class often. His grading is forgiving, since he allows retakes for many quizzes and takes your highest grade out of the two attempts.

Dr. Bazgir is an excellent professor. His lectures are very engaging and full of examples to help solidify content understanding. Apart from his office hours, he is also always happy to accommodate if you have questions or want to meet in-person. Lots of opportunities for extra credit. Overall, a great experience.

He is very kind and curves grades/gives extra credit based off of the class's needs. I had around a 75% in the class but ended up with a 100% because of how much extra credit he gave out. His lectures are engaging and he provides the lectures online as well. The subject itself is hard but Dr. Bazgir helped me understand a lot about orgo chem.

I was super scared to take orgo, but Ayoob made it so easy. He explains everything clearly and reviews past content at the beginning of lectures. 8am lectures with attendance not required, but I still went.  Activ takes a while to get the hang of, but there's also 10% (or more) extra credit offered. Needed 24% on the final to 4.0. Highly recommend!
Incredible

He explained things really well and made it so easy to be able to learn from. If you miss a lecture he has them all recorded and posted on D2L so you don't miss anything. He gives so much practice and help, especially with recitations as well. You also get extra credit options! Super helpful professor and good at teaching.

He's the goat, lecture is worth going to even though the slides are posted. There are so many resources available to practice and the class is structured to be very forgiving with make up quizzes and EC, will be taking him again for Orgo 2

Prof. Bazgir is a great professor and clearly wants his students to succeed. While his accent at times makes it difficult to understand lectures, he is always happy to take questions during lecture and even helps during quizzes. I am not a good chemistry student so the multiple extra credit opportunities and easy homework was a grade-saver.

Prof. Bazgir is a great professor and clearly knows the material and wants to see his students succeed. The homework and extra credit assignments saved my grades. I am not a good chemistry student and I was very surprised at the amount of care Bazgir puts into answering students' questions, even during quizzes or after exams.
Lecture can be a bit fast but he posts video lectures online so you can go over it. Overall if you try somewhat the class is very manageable.
Very good lectures and professor. If you attend class and try to understand, you will do good.

He is very lecture heavy, go to the lectures and make sure you understand, as while he moves on quickly, he will go over it as many times as you need during class if you have questions. He also has recorded lectures available, but I don't find them to be as helpful as going to class. He is always very engaging and truly wants you to succeed!
Best teacher to take for orgo makes the class feel like a breeze and teaches it perfectly also makes it very clear what will be on the exam and gives you materials for it.

Dr Bazgir is the best professor at MSU, hands down! He gives his class amiable opportunities to succeed by offering a ton of extra credit and quiz retakes. Even if Dr. Bazgir gave us 0 extra credit and no quiz retakes, it would still be easy to 4.0 the class due to the engaging way he teaches the class. It is semi-impossible to do bad in his class.

one of the best teachers i have had at MSU. I had Dr. Bazgir for both Orgo1 and orgo 2 and struggled a lot in the beginning but he was always very patient and didnt mind re-explaining things 30 different times lol. i am not the best in chem but i remember so much from his classes ! if you put in the work, his classes are an easy 4.0 and he gives ec
Amazing teacher for orgo. His lectures and slides makes organic chemistry much easier to understand. Would highly recommend taking him if you can.

Ayoob is a great professor and his lectures are always interesting; I always came even though attendance wasn't mandatory. There is lots of extra credit, making it fairly easy to 4.0 if you don't do well on exams. He always reviews content at the beginning of lecture before starting new material which I found very helpful.

Ayoob is hands down the best professor at MSU. 4.0'd both Orgo I and II because of him. He offers tons of extra credit, gives engaging and fun lectures, and truly wants you to do well. You have to put the effort forth, but you will do well if you do. I wouldn't take orgo with anyone else!

AYOOB IS MY MAN. I 4.0d easily in orgo 1&2 bc of this blessing of a man. He's my favorite professor I've ever had. Very loved by his students. Offers so much extra credit I had to get a 20% on the final to 4.0. Lectures are funny and engaging. Requires effort but that is normal, the bad reviewers are the people who expect to 4.0 without any effort.

Prof. Bazgir was one of the best professors I've had here. He made orgo 2 so easy with all of the extra credit he offered and his great lectures. I took orgo 1 online and was nervous about taking 2 in person but it was the best choice I could've made.

I LOVE AYOOB!!! SO much EC offered because he simply wants you to do well in this course. Lectures are posted online so if you miss a class you can get caught up (or never go to class if you want to). Always posts practices before the exams as well as videos. Learn the different reactions and you should do great!

I had Dr. Bazgir for orgo 1 and 2. I absolutely would recommend him to anyone! He taught the material is a very straightforward manner, reviewed content during the lecture before the exam, answered all my questions during office hours, and offered tons of extra credit. He absolutely wants his students to succeed. 10/10 recommend!!

Take Ayoob for orgo, and nobody else. his 8am lectures both semesters are the only 8am classes I've ever taken, only because I actually loved the class. Orgo is notoriously a weeder class but NOT Ayoobs class. You will learn the material so well and enjoy it. This might be a hot take but general chem was harder than his classes. Take his class!
Great lectures, lots of in-class examples on the chalkboard, much extra credit, great at explaining complex concepts simply, and overall a chill dude.

He genuinely wants his students to succeed. He gives so many opportunities for extra credit and ways to boost your grade. If you don't understand a topic talk to him and he will take the time to explain until it makes sense.

Bazgir is a great Prof. If you can get him for organic chem, do it. Helped me 4.0, available outside of class and always willing to re-explain concepts. Made material feel easy. Straight forward with concepts so they were easy to get. Lots of extra credit and online assessments.

This guy is one of the best professors I've ever had. Breaks down Orgo very well and provides plenty of resources to learn inside and outside of class. Very funny and plenty of extra credit opportunities which make the class lower stress. Genuinely sad that the class is over. The Persian Prince is the professor to take Orgo I and II with.

WORTH TAKING THE 8AM FOR! He offers lots of extra credit as the class is only a few hw grades, 4 quizzes, the 2 midterms and final. His class is all lectures (with slides posted) and he posts recorded lectures online. He is very funny and tries to keep the students engaged during class. I would highly recommend, ONE OF THE BEST PROFS AT MSU.

WORTH TAKING THE 8AM FOR! Ayoob loves to teach and is very funny during lectures, but he also posts them online so you don't even need to go. There is SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT, no one should pass with less than a 4.0 imo. He wants everyone to do good and he makes it very easy to; I would highly recommend him for Orgo 1 and 2. He is a great caring prof!
Organic chemistry goat. TAKE HIM IF YOU NEED TO TAKE ORGO.

Beware of his accent for some people that can be a game changer. He likes to move on from information fast without much context other than writing it on the board only to erase it 2 minutes later. If the material was taught different with more consideration for the students I feel like I would've done better.

This professor truly wants everyone to succeed. Homework is what you see on quizzes, quizzes are almost exactly what you see on the exams. overall a really good professor. Do the homework, learn how to do it the other ways (where the answer becomes the question). Learn that, you'll be just fine.

reviews.comment: He is literally the GOAT, make sure you take him for orgo!

You are making a mistake by taking any other orgo prof. This guy made orgo genuinely an enjoyable class. TAKE HIS CLASS!

One of the best professors I've ever had. Funny, but watch out for small details on quizzes and exams! Neither class nor recitation is mandatory (and he posts shortened lectures online), but I highly recommend going. Recitations are also bonus points for attending. All my extra credit meant I only needed 45% on the final instead of 87% for a 4.0!

Dr. Bazgir is a fantastic professor and extremely likable. Makes lectures extremely enjoyable and understandable. Orgo is hard no matter what professor you have but he tries his hardest to make sure everyone understands the content. Very easy to 4.0 as well since he gives out so much extra credit.

There aren't many grades that he puts in, just tests and quizzes. However, he hands out extra credit like it's candy. He also records lectures, which is helpful when you don't want to drag yourself to the 8 a.m. lecture. Overall, he is good at teaching the concepts.

Great Professor. He makes the class lighthearted and fun, and gives a LOT of extra credit, making a difficult subject more manageable. His accent is a bit thick, so it may be a challenge if you struggle with that, but it's honestly easy to get used to. Definitely taking him again for orgo 2!
THIS MAN IS A HERO! Please take him when you take organic chemistry, you will be glad you did!

I enjoyed your lectures a lot, it was easy and understandable to follow along. I know that I skipped one of the lectures, but I'm glad you posted it online, if we couldn't make it to class, because personally for me I would get stressed out if I didn't know what we are covering. I utilized the office hours you held (thanks to one of my friends)!

The Michael Jordan of Organic Chemistry at MSU. Dr. Bazgir is an amazing guy, hilarious lecturer, constantly available outside class and makes Organic digestible and understandable. The only knock on him is that he gave out so much extra credit it almost led me not to learn the material, but if you study out of class it's just more of a boost.

Professor Bazgir is by far the best prof I have ever had. Orgo is hard, but he makes it as easy and understandable, and as a plus, he is hilarious. He offers plenty of extra credit and wants you to do well - always available outside of class. Looking forward to 252 with him, I would only take this class with him if at all possible.

My glorious Persian king, my all-time goat, I cannot stress how much I recommend taking 251 with Dr. Bazgir. As other reviews have mentioned, he provides plenty of extra credit in his class. Additionally, he is super accessible outside of lectures and generally responds to emails within an hour or less in my experience.

My persian prince. He is literally the best orgo professor you can have. Do not listen to the 1/5 person, clearly they did not gaf about their grades because if they actually took the time to listen they wouldn't even need the extra credit. He lets you leave for the quizzes and their online. ASK HIM QUESTIONS ON EXAMS!!

Dr. Bazgir is a really good professor and his lectures are really concise and easy to follow. He gives out lots of extra credit (+1 for every recitation attended, +50 for practice problems) and is very easy to reach outside of class despite having hundreds of students. Highly recommend taking this class, he makes Orgo easy and understandable.

Dr. Bazgir is a really funny professor, and he takes time to explain everything in depth. His accent is a little heavy, however, it's understandable enough to get a great grade in the class. He provided so much extra credit during the class time that it literally could've "erased" a bombed midterm from your grades.
Best professor at MSU. Truly loves his job and is freaking hilarious. Makes Orgo easy. So much extra credit and exams are easy. GOAT.

Honestly, best prof I've had here, I'm even taking him again next semester for 252. Posts all lectures online so you don't technically have to go to class, and offers a ton of EC. He is very funny in lecture and is always available to help. Homework is graded on accuracy, but you have 3-6 attempts/question depending on the assignment.

BEST PROF EVER. love this man. I was so scared for organic chemistry but he makes it so easy. He's also hilarious and made me laugh in my 8 am lecture. Don't take this class unless he is your professor.

This is the best professor at msu. Organic is such a hard class, but this professor is funny and so smart. He has an accent, but you get used to it very fast. The material is hard but there is so much extra credit that makes a huge difference in your grade. I cannot explain how good of a professor he is and can't wait to take him again. #Ayoobontop

Bazgir is very knowledgeable and he is just a great professor. Some people complain about his accent, but it's actually pretty easy to understand him. Chemistry is hard but Bazgir will go out of his way to help! He is absolutely the best prof!

Professor Bazgir is great! Recorded lectures, lecture slides, practice problems, & exam reviews are all on D2L. The grade is 4 quizzes, 2 midterms, final exam, & Aktiv homework. Very easy professor but leads me to not remember the material or even learn it. Gave around 11% of the total grade as extra credit for CEM 252 and rounded by CEM 251 grade by like 5% with a lot of extra credit on top of that.

Professor Bazgir is your best bet at understanding organic chemistry. Had him for two semesters and I think he is a gift to chemistry. Makes lectures available online, in case if you want to sleep in (I have the 8m). Funny guy who makes me want to come to lecture and learn. 100/10.

I love Professor Bazgir! I was intimidated taking Orgo 1 at first but he takes the time to answer questions, re-explain topics, gives many examples, and gives many practice problems. I have also heard his office hours were very helpful which I regret not taking advantage of. I am taking him again for Orgo 2!

I loved Prof. Bazgir. His lectures were well organized and his quizzes accurately tested the material. Prof. is caring and easy to communicate with. He responds to emails quickly and is understanding.

I took CEM 251 with him and am not in 252 with him as well. He covers what we need to know and does so in a concise manner. He (and his TA's) is/are accessible outside of class to help students. Go to office hours if you need it and you will be able to succeed. One of my favorite classes and had great instruction!
This professor really does care about getting us through the class. Lots of opportunities for extra credit which was great. Overall very nice and caring.

Professor Bazgir was good. You can tell that he cares greatly for his students and genuinely wants you to succeed. However, orgo itself is difficult so go to class!! He does have a thick accent, but if you pay attention, you can understand what is going on. I'd also reccommend that you buy the orgo for dummies book; it pairs well with this class.

I personally loved ayyob. he was incredibly kind, if you send him an email he responds quickly. he allowed me to make up a quiz i missed and clearly wants students to succeed. orgo 1 is a lot of content and fast paced, and ayoob has a thick accent and is not tech savvy at all. offers extra credit and is overall a great guy

reviews.comment: Hes my sweet prince. Made Orgo the easiest class ever, IDEK how. If you have to take orgo, take it with Ayoob or don't take it all. WE LOVE AYOOB!!!!!!!!!!!

Dr. Bazgir is an amazing professor. He is extremely kind, caring and fair. He gives out a ton of extra credit to help relieve the stress of the class. He explains the concepts very well in lecture, but also has super helpful Office hours where he will help with anything. The lectures are not mandatory, but I highly recommend going!!

Whenever i emailed him about a quiz question i didn't understand why i got wrong, he emailed me back almost always within an hour, with an explanation and images to help me. He was very good in lecture and would even demonstrate stereochemistry to us with molecules. he even would say funny things during class and even get the class to laugh at 8am

Dr. Bazgir breaks down confusing topics into more understandable material. However, good luck if you have any questions because he does not understand how to answer them. Exams are heavily weighted and there's only 2 of them!! Get ready to put time into this class.

Super clear and concise teaching and makes sure to go over things many times so you understand. Graded on 2 exams, 4/6 of the quizzes, and 20 homework questions every other week or so. Dr. Bazgir was one of my favorite professors. Warning, he does have an accent that makes it difficult to understand him at times but you get used to it. He is amazing at explaining concepts and tries his best to help you pass.

Ayoob has a heavy accent and is not tech savvy. There are only 2 exams and are heavily weighted. They are also not like the hw or quizzes. He is quite hard to understand which wouldn't be a problem if he didn't speak so fast. Horrible. You can NOT understand a thing he is saying. He has a very heavy accent, which makes it very difficult when trying to learn complex chemistry concepts. He does not care about learning. Literally, just pay attention. I get the feeling a lot of students may not pay attention because of his accent. If you pay attention, you will realize his explanations are very easy to understand. It's organic chemistry so obviously expect to put in some time outside of lecture as well.

This professor has the ability to simplify complex topics so students can understand and truly cares about the success of students. Terribly structured class. He takes over 60 slides to explain a topic that our in class professors can explain in 6. I wish I could attach a photo to this review to help you visualize how crowded and confusing  the slides unnecessarily are. He uses grammar structures to explain themself, harder if you aren't familiar with concepts already.

Ausin is really funny and silly, and the TA was great. The class was confusing at times, because the organization of topics is kind of weird. Just dont let content pile up and youre fine. I never actually bought the textbook, its on internetarchive. Buy the Spanish verb tenses book from mcgraw (its like a workbook) and its genuinely a cheat code.

Professor Ausin killed my passion for Spanish. He is difficult to work with, unaccomadating, and impersonal. Professor Ausin is very strict and very difficult. He is one of the least understanding and accommodating professors I've ever had. He's very impersonal and is not invested in your success in his class. His online lectures are poorly structured and hard to follow. Avoid

Basically this course is taught by like random teachers that answer to Professor Ausin, he's not involved like whatsoever he just does the grading and posts the assignments but he's not there for the actual in person class. Lots of homework every week and very heavy lecture material.

I took Professor Ausin for online SPN310 during the summer. It was all online, and we met once a week for a short quiz over what we learned during the previous week.
