reviews.comment: Very easy professor, canceled the final. I personally loved how he challenged our existing beliefs but that can rub some people the wrong way. Very lecture heavy, no recorded lectures and gave extra credit for participation. Can be very test heavy so if you do badly on one exam it might be very hard to recover.

Abysmal professor. Don't expect to be able to debate this guy in ANY way. Will constantly say "there's statistics to support this" and then never bring anything forward. Three of the videos shown to us were taken off YouTube for literal misinformation. Unless you have GPA to spare or are willing to nod to whatever this guy says, don't take this.

Do NOT take SOC 161. It's an opportunity for this walking fallacy of a professor to peddle his own political agenda. Spent the whole semester complaining about neoliberalism and capitalism, with little on the actual development of society. Only take if looking for a headache.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Marley is by far the best professor I have ever had. He is extremely engaged and truly wants his students to learn about how the world works. He is a very fair grader and explains everything in depth so that students do well on the tests. If you come to lectures, do most of the readings, and are engaged you will do great in this class!

Very lecture heavy, but it's a sociology class so what did you expect? Attend every class. Get ready to take notes. Loved him as a person. Very caring and passionate about his teaching, and very smart in general. If you miss a class, make sure to get the notes for sure. He's very understanding and didn't take attendance ever, but make sure to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please avoid this class, if not the professor. This man's ideology bleeds through anything he says, unabashedly. He turned a class meant to be about how we socially developed as humans into half a hundred lectures going after capitalism within a 50 year span. If you are a political moderate of either party; AVOID THIS CLASS. You will be picked on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Workload was super light. Five critical reflections that were three paragraphs, three quizzes, three exams (he cancelled our final). The exams are partner exams with two essay questions that were based on readings. He had an author on one of the books we read as a guest speaker and if you asked him a question you would get extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Will try to explain your own point to you, as if you don't understand what you're saying. Lectures fraught with fallacies, to a distressing degree. Has a very narrow scope of how certain things affect society (there are hundreds of factors that influence us as humans, especially in large groups). Nice enough dude, but an unbearable professor.

Professor Marley is deeply passionate about sociology and wants his students to learn. He loves participation. He is very anti-capitalism, so be prepared to be open minded. Tests are with partners, and the class is mostly essay writing. There is a LOT of reading and the lectures are closely related to them. Overall though, a very interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great professor to gain new perspectives, he is kind of a Marxist, but presents real data and evidence for what is taught. The workload is very light, the only assignments were four discussion questions. The exams were online and open-book so they were very easy and low-stress. Participation in class is heavily encouraged but never forced!

no stress class, good lectures, content is interesting, there is practically no homework except two to three essays, with a few 5 question quizzes and essay-question exams. None of the content is really difficult or hard to wrap your head around. If you dont like reading all the texts just attend class as he reviews all the content from readings

As an introverted student, Prof. Marley's class definitely pushed me out of my comfort zone. He puts a lot of emphasis on participation, so be ready to share your thoughts throughout the course. Nonetheless, I felt as though he was a fair grader and his work was very manageable, though there was often a lot of reading.

Prof. Marley was an amazing instructor. He explains content very well and makes sure you have an understanding of all the material. Attendance is not "mandatory" however, the lectures are where you get most of the information that you will be tested on. Take good notes!
He is a fair professor, he respects your time and gives you opportunities to make up assignments should you miss them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures can feel long and tedious, however as long as you're taking good notes, paying attention, and doing most of the readings you'll get an easy A+.  He loves when people participate in lectures, so the more people raise their hands the more fun the class will be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ben Marley is the absolute goat. Even though ISS220 was a lecture heavy class, all you have to do is pay a little bit of attention, do the reading and the other homework assignments and you will get a 4.0 no problem. Even if you omit some of the reading but pay attention in class, you will still most likely get a 4.0. It is important to not skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was my most favorite professor I had this semester. Completely changed my viewpoint on the world and taught us all how to critically think. He lets you take quizzes and exams at home and even gave us all 100% on our final for being such a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had so far and by far the best class of my first semester! He really cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches, which shows in his lectures. You are guaranteed a good grade if you complete the readings and attend lectures. Completely changed my perspective on the world and improved my writing.

Professor Marley was by far my favorite professor this semester. The class was very lecture heavy about the book we were reading in class but Professor Marley does a good job interacting with the class leading to many class discussions.

Prof. Marley is one of the best teachers I have ever had. My perception of the world has been completely flipped upside down since taking his class, and he has so much knowledge on how the world works that it is so eye-opening. There is lots of reading, but it's so worth it. I came into his class knowing nothing, and now I feel 100x smarter!!
Super chill dude, as long as you show up, give half of your attention, moderately pay attention to the lecture, and read the book you'll get a 4.0. Very understanding, and relaxed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took this course in the summer. It's pretty easy and only one assignment each week. Either it's a quiz or a short paper. Easy grader and gives some extra credit, and the quizzes and assignments are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Marley was great! There was not a moment when I didn't love his teaching style. He genuinely opened my eyes to see the world in a different way, and I will always remember. He is very understanding of students and the pressure that they are under. He is also very helpful and a fair grader. I would take a class just to have him as a professor.
Really cool guy, I had his async. class so I never got to interact in person but he was a great prof. He was a fair grader and gives good heads up about exams/assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Marley is definitely a more chill & "go-with-the-flow" kinda guy! He keeps all his students in check and has expectations that he only slightly budges away from. Personally, I didn't enjoy the class topic (capitalism/environment) but Professor Marley always had good discussions. The only con would be the 5 min breaks for our 2 hr. class

I really enjoyed taking this class and the professor! While the professor is very accessible and open to any questions, he was also very hands off. If you do not mind a lot of reading this is a good class to consider taking!

I loved this class, in fact, I feel spoiled that I got it my freshman year. This is what a college class should be. It completely changed my worldview and made me think more deeply about everything. he pushes his students to really develop their own views. I cannot stress enough that you should take this class. You will not regret it.

Dr. Marley is honestly super nice, the class my come off as difficult but don't worry because he breaks it down and is super generous with extra credit. There's partner exams and many extra opportunities to get points. Exams were not as bad if you are somewhat prepared. There are alot of articles and reading outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Marley is a really nice guy who cares for his students. By the end of this semester I think he was feeling burnt out because he def starts to grade harder. If you do the readings you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Marley is the best professor I've had at MSU. You do have to read or you won't understand the lectures. The readings are hard, but he comes to class and really clears things up so you feel like you didn't waste your time.

Loved this class! Marley is a great guy who is super knowledgeable and wants students to be engaged. Participation/attendance is important but I really enjoyed the lectures, they were very well put together and he always answered questions thoroughly. Sometimes the reading was heavy but after coming to class it all came together/made sense.

Prof Marley was great. Tbh I didn't love the class for the first two months bc I am not into class discussion or readings due every class. but I came to love the class. Marley is a very relaxed guy and respects everyone's opinions. You have to come to class tho, he posts slides but main discussion you need to be in class for.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took this class as an elective and I regret. Do not take this course if you don't like reading or writing. His way of writing is difficult, but I will admit that they help you develop skill. His tests are partnered and he grades hard I am just not a fan of his teaching style.

LOTS of reading and reading questions and in class assignments. Very easy class though: Tests are taken in groups and the only project in the class is done with a partner. Class is very heavily interactive and discussion based with some powerpoint slide info. Challenging content, but made easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This professor is prob my least favorite prof I've ever had. She is extremely difficult and frustrating to work with. She NEVER fully communicates what is going to be on the quizzes, to the point where the whole class banded together because we felt it wasn't fair, and she got defensive and said it would be our ONE quiz drop. (GLG 203)

She understands what she's lecturing about, but her skills are overshadowed by strict rules. Attendance VERY MANDATORY. If you miss the first minute of class you will lose attendance points. Only two iClicker drops a semester. Won't take doctors notes. The busywork is simple but pray you don't get sick twice. 93% to earn a 4.0. Difficult experience

Dr B is a decent professor. She was a bit strict with IClicker and in-class assignments, but you got 5 drops, which I think is pretty fair. Exams were basically word-for-word from the study guide. Just go to class and you'll do fine.

Worst professor I've ever had. She couldn't care less about students, course is exam heavy and mandatory attendance. 1 min late you'll lose points, group projects every single day and tons of hw every week that u have to pay for. mandatory long study guides and the material will not be on the exam. please never take this class with her she's awful
Doesn't care about her students. Will screw you if it means she has to do the tiniest amount of less work.

Very clear what you need to do to succeed, need to get a 93 to get a 4. I got 100% on every non-exam and 88% on exams and got a 3.5. Prof is knowledgeable and does a good job of actually teaching the material and exams are quite easy, but the threshold for what is needed to get a 4 is very high, especially for a 200-level class. ATTENDENCE CRUCIAL

The class is very test heavy(exams make up 60% of your grade). Lots of in class assignments as well, but the assignments are only worth 0.71 points each. Homework is fairly easy(read and respond to articles). I personally think its ridiculous to make all assignments less than 2 points each and make the exams 50, but then again Im not a professor.

Professor Buchholz was a good teacher in that she laid out what was expected of students, but exams were weighted heavily and were quite difficult if you don't look at the study guides. Iclicker is used heavily and she packs so many google forms and activities into class periods, making it feel like middle school all over again.

Good professor, but the daily iClicker is quite annoying. Even if you are 1 minute late you could lose points. Exams are also hard with some questions being on things never discussed in class. That being said, the class content isn't all that difficult and you could pass as long as you give some effort.

Dr. B is awful. Each class has iClicker questions, and being one minute late costs many attendance points. We're only allowed three absences, which is tough since I get sick often. The exams are brutal, making it hard to pass, and her passive-aggressive teaching style is frustrating. I'm worried I won't pass since exams count for 60% of the grade.

The class itself is fairly easy if you take notes and show up daily. There is a graded iClicker daily, which got increasingly strict with attendance as the semester progressed. Buchholtz is very knowledgeable, but a little strict and not the most engaging lecturer. Probably wouldn't take her again personally, but still a solid professor.

Dr. B was really nice and super helpful while in class, but she is incredibly strict with grading. Attendance is mandatory, and can affect your grade in a huge way. If you aren't in class every day, you will miss out on assignments for credit, as well as iClicker questions, which are also for credit. It's super easy to lose points in this class.

She used iClicker and attendance was strict and mandatory. She did iClicker questions and had an in class assignment that both counted for points (combined). Exams were not bad as long as you used the practice study guide. Also does handwritten notes you can only get if you attend class for the day.

Lectures the whole 70 minutes and repeats himself all the time when trying to lecture. Mainly relies on class discussions to stretch out his lecture for the full time. 2 projects the whole semester that are only difficult if your group members don't show. He is strict with attendance, and makes going to class a drag.

Do NOT take this class, whatever you do. All he does is lecture the whole class, and it's not even like a note-taking type class. 2 group projects could have been individual. It was so hard to get myself to go to class, and he only allows 4 absences, and it's 3 days a week. You've been warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not an accommodating professor at all. Very rude and expects you to show up 3 days a week and never ever have anything else come up. Is tricky with iclicker attendance to catch students and just overall unnecessary ways to make sure he has us in his grip. You do not get your points unless you are there for every second of his lectures.
This guy never stops talking and uses big words to sound smart

Very rough class

Really negative option about him. I am so happy to never take this class again

Overall it's a pretty easy class. Usually all you have to do in a week is the weekly reading, 10 question quiz, and short discussion post/response. My main problem with him is that he's pretty unclear about the criteria for the 2 group assignments, which make up half the points in the class. The professor has a very weird teaching style that makes almost no sense. You go over and do the notes together in class but you only do maybe 3 pages out of like 15. So what you're just supposed to figure out the rest on your own? Yup. Most of my learning from this class came from youtube videos.

Awful at explaining, barely goes over the notes. I basically had to teach myself everything, which was extremely difficult. Every time I asked a question to her or her teaching assistants, I was more lost than I was before I asked the question. quizzes are only graded out of 4, and I was once marked down for "overexplaining" my answer.

The only reason I passed was that I taught myself/retaught myself everything. She can be a little rude when talking to students. She always seems to do the easiest problems in class then has us do the hard problems by ourselves. The webwork also doesn't really help on quizzes and exams. Most of the time the webwork is different than the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She does go over the material a bit fast during lectures but she's always eager to explain everything after class and during office hours. Prof. Cioni really wants you to understand what's being taught and so she takes her time coming up with great analogies when you meet her one on one. She's surprisingly approachable.
She is a great teacher. She really cares about her students succeeding. Please attend her office hours she will really work with you so you can have that grade you would like.

If you want to sit in a class and be confused for most of it this is your class. The whole semester I felt as if I was being rushed and she had no time for questions and made you feel dumb whenever asking a question. She would try to explain each problem but would simply confuse you even more and leave you with more questions than answers.

I'm a freshman this year and I absolutely love Professor Cioni. She is one of my favorites. She is very nice and helpful. She wants you to pass her class and to understand what she is teaching and welcomes questions unless she is running out of time.

I really like the concept of this class because it is split. However, her specifically as a professor really changed the game. I felt really disrespected half the time. It always seemed like she was disappointed in us. I felt like if I asked a question I would be judged. Make sure to get a high score on all your quizzes, you will be sorry later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I rarely went to class but I passed every quiz and exam. She posts everything online. Does not tell good stories to try and explain math problems.

She is the most annoying teacher I've ever had and is pretty bad at explaining the materials (so no one goes to class). spends a lot of time just being upset. if you get all the answers right on a unit, but don't explain something well enough, you get a 2. get one answer wrong and it's a 1 for an entire unit. don't take 103A-B just do regular 103

She is honestly the best math teacher I have ever had and my grades reflect that. I have always struggled with math but not in professor Cionis class. She takes the time to break everything down to the point where you don't just memorize how to do the problem you understand every aspect of how it works with out throwing to much in there.
Great professor! She is very smart and cares for everypne in the class to learn and ask questions. The class is never boring and she good at explaining.

Took MTH102 with her as the lecturer, her lectures are a bit boring and you have to print out note packets frequently. The course itself is extremely easy and there are only 3 tests the whole semester. Recitations are mandatory, the lecture is not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: I thought she was a great professor. She was to the point and told you exactly what you needed to know. She also did a great job of reviewing before each quiz/exam as best as she could. I would recommend her, she made me not hate going to math lecture.

What is expected is clear and to the point. If you skip lecture you won't know what is going on however the tests are hard. This class was overly challenging as trick problems are constantly thrown on tests.

She teaches MTH 1825 and although I never had as my instructor, I've dealt with Julie plenty. She has this attitude about her that annoys me. She acts way too much like this is a high school instead of a university. We're all adults here. If she has a problem, she should kick them out the room. Instead, she yells and talks like you are a child.

Great professor. She was always very concerned for her students and always made sure everyone knew when deadlines were coming up. She gave everyone a million opportunities to get help or to ask questions and she always had good examples. She also reviewed before every test to make sure everyone was as ready as possible.
He literally just makes no sense. It feels like he doesn't even know what he's talking about. So many discussion posts with confusing wording.

I totally recommend him! Super fun and laid back. He is so passionate about what he teaches and it shows! He's also accommodating and he genuinely really cares about his students. He always has a smile on his face and he loves to see students' work. He does a lot of group projects, so if you're not into that thing, that's something to be aware of.
I 10/10 recommend this professor! He was extremely accommodating, and both the midterm and final project were group projects. We watched a lot of interesting movies, and we often got out early

Professor Emery is really nice and wants his students to acheive. His class consists of lectures, and the midterm and final are group projects, which is nice. Most of the homework you receive is weekly discussion posts about topics you learned in class that week. I would recommend only buying the least expensive book he tells you to purchase.

Professor Emery is kind, and it's clear that he truly loves teaching. For this IAH course, we watched & analyzed horror movies, which I absolutely loved. We watched a lot of really good stuff, and the discussions were also engaging. There was little homework, usually just a discussion post a week, 1 group presentation, a final project, & a midterm.

Prof Emery is so nice and understanding. His lectures are never too intense and he often has breaks. We also get out early more often than not. There are no quizzes/exams, just a midterm group project and final group project plus one discussion post a week. You get 4 absences, your grade goes down by .5 (letter grade) per absence after. Nice class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Emery is a great prof. The work load of this class can be a lot, but nothing one couldn't handle. We watch horror films in class and analyze them in class discussion, as well as for the hw discussion posts. Other than that we have group presentation and group final. Overall, very understanding and kind professor.
The grade I got is lowk my fault because I kept forgetting to do the quizzes. Everything is super easy and he's really funny

Don't take his class; it's intolerable. His lectures are circuitous and full of unnecessary info, he gives horrendous feedback for assignments he'd create misleading criteria for, and he grades everything off of very little.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy this class, I struggle going to the letures and then the amount of time I spent studying for the course outside of class was significant. I somewhat enjoyed Professor Pedro but the way he stutured the class was a pain and would go on rants that didn't add anything to the class or what you needed to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy, really funny, absolutely despise the way he grades. I got an 84% in the class and got a 2.5 because of his 5 point grading scheme. Don't take this class unless your a film major because the required attendance and strict grading makes it a total pain in the gpa

Dr. Donelson was an amazing teacher for WRA 101. She made the class enjoyable and very obtainable to achieve a 4.0. She made the lectures fun, gave lots of time to do work, and gave good feedback and ability to improve. She's always willing to stay after class and help even for other classes. Outfits were on point, always.
She is a very kind and funny individual who makes class better

Dr. Donelson is an amazing professor. If you stay on top of the work and follow her instructions, you will pass. She makes a real effort to connect with her students and gives honest, helpful feedback that actually helps you improve. She's also super relatable; she talks about her love of hip hop, and her outfits are always on point.

The only good thing about this class was that attendance wasn't mandatory. She was never clear on instructions, and assignment dates. Honestly, this class should've just been an online class because she canceled class so much.
Aggravatingly taught class

Dr. Donelson is a very good professor. I loved her not only did she have an outstanding personality but she taught her class very well. I was surprised now thinking about her rate my professor beforehand but now that i've been through her class she is amazing. She knows holiday's are important so she is very lenient with those days. Very engaging!

Professor Donelson was an outstanding professor who not only helped me become a better writer but also encouraged me to think critically about the world around me. Her clear teaching, constructive feedback, and engaging classroom environment made this course a truly valuable experience.

Dr. Donelson is a great teacher. She sets instructions for spreading out the work load, and is easy to get into contact with after class or in class if you have any questions. She is very caring and has an amazing sense of humor. She cancels classes during the holidays and important week days. I would recommend her to anyone wanting to take WRA101.

Dr. Donelson is a very good professor. She is very easy to get in contact with outside of class, and she lets you know what you have to do to get a good grade, and gives lots of examples on projects, essays, etc. I would definitely recommend her to other people looking to take WRA 101.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Changed the rules for the essays and assignments throughout the semester. She told us a lot of things about the course that actually got me excited, but all just ended up being untrue. I really don't think she knew where she was taking the class when the semester started, or at least it doesn't seem like it. Pointless assignments don't make sense.

Dr. Donelson is truly a great professor. I am very confused on why so many people do not like her. She makes all the assignments/papers very clear and she is very approachable if you have a question. Also, Dr. Donelson is very funny. She cancels classes during holidays or the week of a holiday, just make sure to check your email the morning of.

This professor seems to have clear expectations during class, however when you leave you end up feeling like you have no clue what's going on. She claims to be open to answer any questions but will make snide remarks occasionally. She's not a bad person and if you can manage the first 2 months you'll be fine. She grades really easy as well.

This is the worst and most difficult Professor I have ever had. Her directions were extremely vague and confusing, and whenever we asked her questions, she would either not respond or assume we didn't read the directions thoroughly enough. Also, the class is riddled with leftist bias.
Dont take her
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: No clear instructions for assignments. Loves to plan/cancel zooms with very little notice. Also loves to give 0 feedback on assignments. Will say she is available for outside help & questions but really is not. Always is changing aspects of projects and contradicting herself. Worst class I have ever taken, switch out if you can.

No clear instructions are provided for assignments. She loves to change things last minute, plan and cancel class without warning, and is always contradicting herself, which is very frustrating. She says she is available for outside help & questions but is not really not willing to help. Worst class ever taken, switch out if you can.

This was by far the worst professor I've ever had. Has no respect for students/their time and would belittle us if we asked questions when her directions were NEVER transparent. She planned zoom meetings 10 minutes before they started and would cancel scheduled meetings. Basically told us her laundry was more important than the questions we had.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the most challenging professors I've ever worked with. She constantly contradicted herself with the grading, she had no consistency with zoom calls, she would vanish for long periods of time without actually teaching us what we needed to know for projects. She would even yell and poke fun at students for merely asking questions. Switch out..

Does not explain assignments at all. When you ask her a question about an assignment she gives you a confusing answer or makes you feel dumb. Avoid at all costs. Not to mention you need a 95% to get a 4.0 and she doesnt grade anything til the semester is over.
Terrible teacher. Hard to understand whats being taught. The way she writes things for assignments is not thorough enough with descriptions. She teaches at MSU and U of M Dearborn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I find that Professor Donelson is not for everyone as she is primarily there to enhance your writing skills and overall confidence in yourself as a writer. If you have her as a professor my advice is to show her that you care, ask as many questions as possible about the assignment, and have her check your assignment before turning you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was horrible beyond words. First of all, little instruction and no rough drafts are given on assignments and then it is expected to be perfect. When it's not perfect, the class gets yelled at when it is clearly not the classes fault. Also, the class was revolved around white privilege, which I found to be totally unnecessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She does not give much instructions on assignments and there was one assignment that she said we werent allowed to email questions about. We did group presentations, and after a group presented, she would critique them in front of the class and gave the other groups the opportunity to change theirs based on her critiques of others, was is not fair

The professor is a really engaging and thoughtful instructor who makes cultural heritage interesting and easy to understand. He explains concepts clearly and encourages open discussion, which makes it easier to connect with the material. Overall, he is approachable, supportive, and genuinely invested in his students' learning.
Prof. Draper could take on a pure blooded viltrumite easily

Great teacher, it starts off easy like every essay class and then snowballs near the end.  I learned a lot and he asked questions which makes you think critically.  The class is relevant today and allows you to learn about something in-depth.

I personally didn't like him. At first I thought that he was going to be good, but after a while if he doesn't agree with what you're writing about, or your personal beliefs, he will give you an awful grade. But overall, if you're not aiming for a 4.0, he'd be a good teacher.
He is easy to understand and keeps everyone stress free. He is an organic teacher and goes with the needs of the class. :) I enjoyed the class
LOVE HIM!!!!!!!!
Amazing Man

Amazing teacher! Very down to earth and funny. All the writing assignments were about topics we could make our own. He encourages you to write in your own style. Great feedback on papers. Somehow got our class to interact and have actual discussions. Final project was an amazing experience. By far the best teacher I've had yet.
doing the extra credit really helped me. also, after i had surgery, he invited me to come in for office hours and gave me extension on homework. he is a kind guy.
Very average professor, the lectures can be long and boring but it is stats class so. He does ok. He is very caring and does care about his class.

He has been my fav so far. His lectures are engaging and enthusiastic, he spends plenty of time on each topic, and he even sends out helpful emails each week. He goes the extra mile, even offering an outside-of-class study group before exams! I've never liked math, but he makes it more enjoyable.

Had for STT315 but couldn't select that option. Easy going professor. Very understanding if you show up to class. Pay attention and do the extra credit and you'll be fine. Practice exam questions every similar to actual exams so they're helpful.
Professor Dikong is a fantastic professor. Very straightforward, just go to the lecture and spend a decent amount of time preparing for exams, and you'll be good.
Very solid professor, you can always get help from him. Only problem I had was that my TA was not very helpful.

As long as you show up and do the extra credit you'll do good in this class. Helps you a lot with preparation for exams and truly wants the best for his students. Engaging lecture. Attend the recitations they actually help a lot.
Very good professor and always looks for the best in you. if you put in the time and effort to prepare for this course, you will be successful.

Prof. Dikong is amazing! He is very clear about due dates and assignments. This class has a substantial amount of homework, but completing it all really pays off on the exams. Going to class is a must because he tells you exactly how to succeed on the exams. He is a sweet guy and sends emails multiple times a week to keep everyone in the loop
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Dikong was wonderful. He does have an accent, but you get used to it. He started taking attendance through TopHat, which could be done from anywhere. Although being in class wasn't required, I highly recommend attending to succeed. The material is easy if you apply yourself. Homework and practice exams really help prepare for exams. Easy 4.0

This guy was great. I missed a homework assignment in the first week and came to his office hours. Not only was he very understanding but we ended up having a great conversation. The material can be difficult but doing the homework helps it makes sense. Attendance was taken with TopHat but after the first few months he stopped using it.

Great professor! There was (almost) weekly Top Hat and Webwork but it was never super difficult. He also posts the notes from class, so if you didn't grasp the concept in the lecture it is easy to reteach yourself.

I took STT 315 and I found the class somewhat difficult especially after the 1st test. He teaches decently well but he's not the most responsive when it comes to issues with grading. I would have preferred it not to be so dependent on McGraw hill as the questions are worded strangely and the grading is flawed. Besides that a good class though.

Great profesor. He explained things very clearly. Hard to catch up if you don't go to class because he doesn't post videos or anything. If you go to class, do the webwork, and do the practice exams it is easy to do good in the class. Lots of extra credit but you have to keep up with it and the hw. Overall great guy and he seemed very passionate.
AMAZING!
Great professor. Only thing I struggled with was his foreign accent, but after a few weeks I became familiar with it. You can tell he cares about the students success.

Prof. Dikong was amazing; very lecture-heavy, so be ready for that. Homework was once a week most weeks except for exam weeks. He is very fair, so you will most likely get the grade you have earned. Would definitely take again!

Professor Dikong tries to make his class sound hard but in reality, it is pretty easy. His lectures are easy to understand and he is pretty funny. Don't skip the lectures though or you will fall behind. Do all the extra credit before the webwork and that makes it much easier. And don't hesitate to go to his office hours if you are confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Some of the notes were hard to take becuase his slideshows didn't always line up with our packet. I skipped a lot of lectures and did fine but if you want to fully understand the content than you should go to class. He gave a homework assignment every week that was easy for the most part and an extra credit that went with it.
overall bad experience

Dikong is a pretty good teacher to have. He does tend to be very slow when lecturing, but his slides are amazing, and he gives a practice exam that looks identical to the test. He is pretty funny and as long as you go to class you will get an A.

Lectures are painfully slow and go over the easy topics and ignores the hard stuff on your own. the exams were also so out of pocket and way worse than any homework problem/lecture. dikong is funny in your senile grandpa sort of way but that's kind of it. if you have to take it make sure to go to recitation bc that's the only place where I learned

Dikongs lectures are unbearable, I ended up teaching myself. It seemed like he was teaching the simplest concepts but ignoring the complex ones found on the homework and exams. Maybe he would be alright if you really struggle with math (to the point that you dont understand mean) otherwise his pace is too slow and impossible to stay engaged with.

Great professor and great person but his accent is incredibly heavy. So much so that I still can only tell half of what he's saying at the end of the year. He's a good professor but there are definitely better ones out there.

Dikong is a pretty good professor, although I think that his slides are more helpful than the lecture. He's very nice, and clearly cares about his students. The course gets harder as you go on, but as long as you do the work - reasonable amount btw - you'll probably be okay.

STT200 is a difficult course. It is complex material and the course moves rather quickly. However, Dikong was extremely accommodating. At first, I was terrified to take this course, (its a requirement for my psychology major) but with Dikong's help, I passed with a 4.0. Be resourceful, ask for help, attend the lectures, and do the homework.

I didn't go to class a lot but if you are taking STT 200 it is an easy class if you attend your recitation and stay on top of the notes. From what I've heard he is a kind professor and I believe that! For HW, we used webwork and tophat and I struggled on some of the units and workload but going to my recitation helped a lot! Also uploads lectures.

I really enjoyed having Professor Dikong for STT 200. I thought he explained course concepts and expectations really well. His accent can be a tad hard to understand sometimes, but if you sit closer to the front and pay attention you'll be fine. He is really accessible outside of class and wants students to do well. Good for "math-hating" students.

Professor Dikong is my favorite professor ever. He is very caring and is great at explaining the material. He spends lots of time on subjects and doesn't rush through it like other math classes. Lectures are posted online and are very easy to understand. I don't like math and am bad at it but he makes it enjoyable and easy. Strongly recommend

Super genuinely nice guy. Really cares about his students and that is very evident throughout his class. If you pay attention and do notes you will have no problem passing the class. However, it is very easy to fall behind if you don't pay attention or skip.
Professor Dikong is amazing. He is so caring and understanding. Lectures are very clear and helpful for the work to be completed. Take stats with him.

-Prof Dikong uploads the lecture slides so if you miss a lecture you can look back to see what you missed
-Attendance is based on a weekend assignment
-Weekly webwork + extra credit
-Prof Dikong is very kind and cares about the students success
- No quizzes and 3 exams total
-The practice exam is usually what the actual exam looks like

An overall great professor and a very easy class. You can tell he really cares to make sure everyone understands the concepts. If you do the home work and attend lectures the material is not at all difficult. There are only 3 exams in total and the study guides and practice exams provided to study with are very comparable to the actual exams.

he is a really nice professor! there are many opportunities to bring up your grade (weekly webwork, tophat quizzes, extra credit) if you don't get your participation points in class. a lot of lectures but they aren't mandatory (recitation is tho so make sure you go). i probably spent an hour per week on homework. def would recommend this professor!

DiKong was fantastic! Showing up to lectures made you feel like he enjoyed teaching the material and was enthusiastic, and has great insight to explain concepts. Preparing for exam was also straight forward, DiKong released a practice exam that was comprehensive and very easy to study. Would definitely recommend this class anyone.
Good lectures and assessments align with the material we covered.

If you need to take a pre-req class, I can recommend him. A lot of lectures but they're only 50 mins each. Recitations are mandatory (don't miss them!) and u need a doctor's note to be excused. Otherwise, there is weekly webwork homework and a quiz that lets you catch up if u weren't in the lecture. I did hw once a week, can definitely recommend :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor! Sometimes hard to understand because of his accent, but if you sit closer to the front you will be fine. 1 homework assignment a week online. Attendance is not mandatory. Posts all lecture slides online and gives a practice exam and study guide before each exam that are extremely helpful!

I love this professor. He wants all his students to succeed and it is easy to ask him questions and get help. He has an accent but it is easy to understand him. Attendance isn't mandatory but the more you go the easier it is to understand the material. He does review sessions for exams and is always open to answering questions. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he makes stats easy to understand, as long as you attend lectures and do the work, you'll do great. you can tell that he wants his students to succeed. he creates study guides and practice exams that are similar to the actual exams that prepare you well. our section does better on exams than other sections because of him.

Prof Dikong is very nice and you can tell that he wants his students to succeed. He mentions quite often that our lecture hour consistently had the best exam scores. He uses TopHat sometimes in class but more often outside class.

Professor Dikong is an amazing teacher. You get used to the accent, it is not that difficult to understand. I feel like he gets a bad rap and I don't know why. He is so funny and really cares about his students and very willing to help you succeed. It does get harder as the course goes on but there are many resources.

He explains everything really well and has detailed slides to go with each lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you don't attend the lectures then you'll definitely miss out on a lot of content.
Keep up weekly and youll do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Dikong is a really funny guy, and his lectures are better than the usual boring math lecture. His assignments are reasonable, as long as you put some effort in you'll be fine. First exam is super easy, then the class gets significantly harder.

Definitely one of my favorite professors! He worked so hard to make sure that everyone succeeded. I see a lot of comments saying that he's hard to understand but that's not the case at all. Recently we have transitioned to online schooling due to COVID-19 and he has made the transition so much smoother. For someone who hates stats, I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His accent is hard to understand at first but you will get used to it quickly. He is very helpful with Webwork and exam study guides.

I had to work to do well in stats but Dikong really tried to make concepts understandable. He tries and explains a lot of things with analogies and sometimes it helps but either way, he's always answering questions before class starts and makes tough concepts clear. Great guy and an awesome professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dikong is a great professor and a nice man. He is usually willing to help students before and after class with any questions. Attendance isn't mandatory, just make sure to study the slides on D2L if you skip class or else you'll fall behind. The WebWork homework assignments and three exams make up most of your grade.

Professor Dikong is a great professor. His accent is a little thick, but once you become accustomed to it, he is very easy to understand. He pretty much lectures straight from the powerpoint slides (which all students have access to through D2L) and he gives great test prep material (one study guide and practice exam with answers). Very easy to 4.0

Prof Dikong is a very good professor. He truly cares about his students and prepares you for the exams. He holds extra review sessions for the exams, so definitely go to these, they help a ton. He basically tells you what to study. He has a bit of an accent but he is really caring and a funny guy.

Professor Dikong really cares that his students do well, He makes study guides for every exam and holds study sessions during and outside of class. I dont find him hard to understand but If you skip lecture and recitation youll fall behind easily. Exams are fairy easy if you dont wait until the night before to study.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Dikong is a nice and funny man, but he is not a great teacher. He has a heavy accent and it is hard to understand. Also, he does not reply to emails. You have to go to office hours to see him, which is inconvenient if you have a class during those times. I would not recommend taking his class.
Funny guy if you don't take yourself too seriously! Stats 200 with him is great as long as you stay on top of the material and show up to class

Professor Dikong is hidden gem! He provides weekend exam reviews for his students to ensure they understand how to solve problems that will be on the exam. He's always available during office hours, provides 2 practice exams that are exactly like the real exams and goes over them heavily in class. He tries to get his point across by overexplaining
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: DO NOT take a class with him. He can't teach, just look at the grades he has given on msu grades. His exams are way harder than the homework. The man literally sent us an email the day before an exam saying that a certain topic won't be on it, and that ended up being the first question on the exam. His notes are WACK too. Switch out ASAP.

This class was fairly easy IF you go to the recitations. I learned more at the recitation than I did during the lectures. He goes over the content during lectures but the pace is very slow so it gets pretty boring. He rarely takes attendance. To pass just do the exam reviews and you will be fine
Very tough to understand during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor. Dikong is one of the best professor I've ever had. You can tell he really cares about his students. He does have an accent but it's easy he is still easy to understand. He makes Stats class enjoyable. There is 2 exams worth 20 percent of your grade, as well as webwork and top hat. He gives 2.5% extra credit added to your final grade.

Great man, but rambles too much as a professor. Loses the point with weird metaphors. Snippy when answering questions sometimes. Hilarious, but not the best at explaining introductory math concepts to people who are first learning it.

He does have an accent but he uses a lot of examples and is funny, so easy to relate/learn. Theres only 5 homework assignments total (not every week), 3 exams, 1 final. Pop quizzes are for extra credit ONLY. So attendance is your choice. Office hours 3 times a week for extra credit, also by choice. So much opportunity for points.
Pretty funny and interesting. Heavy lecture focus, class does not take attendance but if you don't go to class you'll fall behind quickly. Approachable and very kind
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a very nice person but not a good teacher. I paid $80 for a book and I didn't even open it. His accent is very thick and it is hard to understand. I did terrible on the homework which was assigned weekly (usually like 50 problems) and I did even worse on the exams. I barely passed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Isn't very good at teaching the content to the class. His thick accent makes him hard to understand for a large portion of class. The only time you actually learn anything is during recitation. The book he gives you is also totally useless and will not help you.

The first couple of exams are easy and he gives you good material to study from. The last two are absolutely ridiculous. He does not go over any of the material and the supplemental information does not do a whole lot. I went into the final with a 4.0 and walked out with a 3.0.

The lectures are long and boring.  He's not the easiest person to understand and follow.  It takes him forever to get though one example problem.  The first couple of tests aren't that bad, but expect the final to be SUPER hard.

His exams weren't too bad as long as you did EVERY single question on his practice exams. Mostly because his practice exams were basically his exam. The final, completely screwed me over! The final came out of no where. I studied a lot for it and still failed. I was borderline for a 4.0, after the final I 2.5 the class.

Dikong is very unclear. His accent is hard to understand. But he gives out tons of extra credit. You get extra credit for doing certain assignments, which you can only turn in at his office hours, which you get extra credit for going to. So you literally get extra credit for turning in extra credit.

Excellent professor. Very knowledgeable and helpful when it comes to questions on homework or upcoming exams. Very open with office hours. Also, he assigns a lot of extra credit which can really boost your grade.

Dickong is one of the best professor, he help students as well as you want to but in his office. That is convenience place that you can take time with him. Understand the situation how can he will help students in the class when other class is coming. if you failed the class, that might be your fault.
He makes the complicated subjects easy to understand and he is always available to talk to if you need questions. He also gives out a lot of opportunities to gain extra credit.

Don't be fooled by the early super-easy material, Dikong gets progressively less clear as the course goes on and the material gets harder, requiring you to self-teach. The last exam and final were overly long for their time-limits; knowing formulae cold would be helpful. As others, I'm a 4.0 student with a 3.5 in this class.

Dikong is hard to understand, and is not approachable. He gets frustrated when asked questions and refuses to help students unless they come to his office. He is blatantly RUDE to students when they need help. NOT CONCERNED ABOUT ACTUALLY HELPING THE STUDENTS LEARN. I am a 4.0 student and i'm getting a 3.5 in this supposed to be easy class.
Gives a lot of extra credit which is helpful.
No Comments

dont bother asking him for help, but his practice exams that he hands out, ARE the exam with different numbers. do the practice exams and homewrk and understand the formulas and ur set. and the quizes, are the exact problems he assigns for each chapter. but u need to teach urself for the most part

Dr. Dikong is always willing and able to be helpful. His class can get boring, but good attendance will earn you extra credit, even if it is in a large lecture hall. This is an easy 4.0 with a marginal amount of effort.

This class is so unstructured and makes no sense. I have had to go into the help room two times and remind the TA's to post the work for the week. Many times I have went in there and they did not even know we had an exam the next day. Also, don't expect fast reponces on emails. Worst class I have taken at MSU.

This professor makes the class way harder than it needs to be. The class/project directions are very un-clear and projects aren't able to be done without a TA. Glad this is my last semester with this teacher.

While Dixon isn't necessarily active in her class, you can tell she changed things up this year compared to the last few years of this class. I truly want to say I am learning a lot about Excel in this class, and I like the format. While it is a big disorganized and could definitely use some tweaking, overall this class has improved.
Very flexible and accommodating. There's a lot of work but It's easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really sorry for your loss Teagan.

Class is taught by college kids. You don't learn anything and assignments are so hard to find. The material that we're supposed to learn is important but the method they use for teaching is easily the worst.

Easily the worst instructor out of any of the Broad core classes. Course is terribly formatted, especially the final exam, which quizzes you on highly specific things about Tableau instead of just allowing you to create something using the platform which is what the rest of the unit was about. Thankfully the coursework is fairly easy

The TA's SUCKED. Almost no learning happened during the recitations.  There was also a huge disconnect between the online lectures, the recitations, and the homework assignments. The course was organized poorly too.

This is the most unorganized class I've had the displeasure of taking, which sucks, as this is a required class for Broad. I wouldn't call the content overly difficult, but the class is entirely run by TAs (you will NEVER see Teagan) so if they don't know how to answer your question (good chance they don't) you're screwed. Needs major restructuring

Horrible class. Teagan is an awful professor and has organized the whole curriculum so poorly. The TAs are just as bad if not worse. Never knew how to answer any question I had and were just focused on getting out class as fast as possible, and were overall just extremely unprofessional. MSU needs to get rid of this course or replace Teagan and TAs

Never met Dixon all semester, but it didn't ever matter. TAs were outstanding. The work could not be easier, easiest 4.0 ever. Not a lot of homework. If you have half a braincell you will be just fine. Everything is online and easily accessible. Grading is super slow and Dixon uses AI for literally everything, like lessons and grading

Course needs to be removed or Teagan needs to be replaced. Very unorganized course but she never shows up. All TA led and they didn't know when our exams were. So many different platforms to use and tests do not match what homework is.

This course is so unorganized. There's so much work that is unrelated to the course and the exams. For instance, BOL, lecture videos, and knowledge checks. Also, the grading is really slow, and every week you have to show up to class just for attendance, then you're good to go. Overall, MSU has to either cancel this course or replace Teagan.

This class isn't very difficult, but the way it is run is horrible. Teagan never shows up, and she is a very slow grader. I am a week out of the course, and I have only been graded on half of the assignments, and some of the group projects that were done in module 2 are somehow not graded. The excessive homework is worth little in your final grade

Throughout the class, she would say she "leveraged AI" to create the videos, which is probably the dumbest thing I've ever heard. She might as well have said, "I'm too lazy to do my job, so I make AI robots do it for me." At least then I would have a little respect for her honesty. I would rather dig forks in my eyes than take this class again.
This class is a complete waste of time.

You never actually interact with Tegan in this class and instead you are up to the mercy of having good TAs (Shoutout Neel and Vivian). Even then, the class is simple enough where you can learn most of it on your own anyway. Genuinely one of the easiest classes I've taken in Broad and is actually relevant to what you might do in your career.

Lecture videos are extremely vague and taught as if you already know what is going on. TAs simply do not care and just want to get out of class as fast as possible. The course does not follow a specific timeline; it jumps around and can be very confusing.

This class needs to seriously be looked at by Broad if they are making it a required class. We are in Module 2 and I still have no idea what is ever happening in the class. The TA's don't know anything and make things more confusing than before. They flip through slides as fast as possible and there is no teaching at all that goes into the class.

The complete lack of effort put into this class  is astonishing. Reading a lazy, and meaningless AI-constructed powerpoint was not only demoralizing for the price I pay to go to this college, but also embarrassing for the professor.

The Lecture to accompany it was two AI voices glazing each other for an hour straight.

SIMnet is expensive too.

TAs lead class in person and you will watch videos outside of class to teach you the material. My TA, Patrick, was the goat so the class was pretty fun for me. Exams aren't too difficult if you do the practice exams and pay attention to the demos. Definitely take advantage of every extra credit opportunity that you get throughout the semester.

The teaching quality was disappointing. Lectures relied too heavily on videos instead of interactive instruction, and the practice exams did not reflect the actual exam content at all. We were also required to pay for an external platform that we only ended up using for four weeks, which felt like a waste of money. TA did the bare minimum.

The TA's know nothing and can barely ever answer questions. You never see the professor. Unorganized D2L page and uses a flipped model so you basically learn everything yourself. Exams are different from what you do in class and group projects suck. Bad class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Needs to choose better TAs for the class, and the flipped model is AWFUL. The in-class demos aren't well thought out & not taught even remotely well. Expect to either learn it all on your own, or rely on groupmates for help. Also the switch to an AI platform (that you have to pay for!) to do the one project not graded by their TAs is...interesting.

Horrible class. You will never see her, the TAs teach the class. One TA I had was good and the other barely knew how to open Excel or SQL. The material is not that difficult to understand but you have to teach yourself everything. She is more worried about sending out articles about sexism in data analytics than teaching the class.

Had to buy a $70 platform to use for 4 weeks. Too lazy to teach so uses flipped classroom, TAs suck. Might as well just put it online and save everyone some time. Easy class, but EASILY one of my least favorite professors here. The only thing she does is post on d2l, but the class page is the worst ive seen. Not sure what she actually does...

This is a poor professor, she has a flipped classroom, the videos are uninformative and are rather difficult to follow as well. The TA's are inadequate too. I wish MSU would put somebody in administration for these "flipped" roles instead since there is no teaching involved. An Arby's or perhaps a McDonald's manager might have enough experience.

I have never seen her in class because it is a "flipped classroom" where the TAs (who aren't knowledgeable) do the teaching. I chalk that up to laziness, she doesn't even have videos for us to watch, just a very expensive online textbook. I wish MSU would do something about this, I will gain nothing from this class because she doesn't want to help.

Not a well set up class in my opinion. One of the most useful classes in Broad, but horribly executed. Everything is ran by TA's, who are mediocre teachers at best. This class structure feels like there was no effort or thought put in. I'd recommend finding an alternative institution to fill this credit.

ITM209 is not that difficult of a class. It does take a little bit of a time commitment, but overall I didn't find it to be as difficult as everyone says. The hardest unit is SQL. There is only homework for the Excel unit. The group projects are ok they are easy if you have a good group. Overall not as hard as I expected.

This is one of the worst courses I have taken due to the extremely poor organization and set up of the class. It is a flipped lecture which means your TA's explain almost nothing to you and put no effort, as well as assignments 4/7 days of the week, all in different places. It is a shame because the information is useful but terribly executed.

It's similar to CSE where she shows up for 3 minutes on the first day and then you never see her again. Everything after the first unit is learned through long, boring lecture videos. She made us pay a lot for simnet just to only use it for the first unit. The D2L announcements which are the only communication we get are very passive aggressive.
Never once saw her in person. Made super long videos we were supposed to watch that were super boring and hard to follow. Only class I haven't 4.0 in at MSU.

...so...

I honestly felt completely overwhelmed and drained by the first day. I understand and expect that summer classes are quicker/condensed, but it felt that no class material was even cut out to adjust for the shorter summertime. Good professor, decent class, terrible approach. Just doesn't seem to consider students summer schedules.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You basically have to teach yourself everything, the TA's are nice and helpful but Dixon is basically a non-existent factor. Video lectures are a waste of time. There are group projects and exams for 3 units, you learn excel, sql, and tableau, and it is all boring, but not hard to get a decent grade if you do assignments. Overall this class sucks.

I didn't mind Teagan but the class was organized so poorly. It's a flipped classroom, and I rarely even watched her videos. I learned everything from my TAs. The content itself isn't too difficult if you pay attention, but the weekly quizzes and exams are taken on a lockdown browser (but you do get a notecard). Offers extra credit for participation

This class is taught basically all by TAs. She puts content and lectures online, but most of your learning will come from what you learn in-person from your TAs. Probably out of her control, but I'm just not a fan of this system.

This class/professor isn't enjoyable at all. The lectures are all online with a weekly lockdown knowledge check. The professor is extremely boring to listen to, which makes it difficult to retain the information. 2 Midterms and a cumulative final. Paid for a required book and only used if for one unit. They need to restructure this class.

This class seriously makes me wonder about the thought process behind their decisions of this course. Same thing as CSE 102, watch the extremely long and numerous lectures before class and hope that your TA's are helpful. In-class activities are useless, 3 group projects,3 exams, and lockdown quiz weekly. Please restructure this class.
Takes forever to grade everything. Waited about 6 weeks to get some grades back. Also the online lectures are really stupid on how they organize them and make the quizzes every week.

Professor Dixon is amazing and very helpful if you utilize the help rooms and office hours. Ta's are also a blessing in this class, and they are always down to help before and after class. If you watch all of the lectures and read the project instructions carefully, then you'll do well in the class. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dixon was accessible outside of class which is nice. TAs do the teaching, so if they're bad you're screwed. To do good you have to be a genius or watch every lecture video. An important course and definitely helped. So many projects and the end of the semester was thrown together with 2 projects and 2 quizzes due the Friday before finals week.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is disorganized and unclear. In-class sessions are more than useless. Tried to ADR 10% of the class because they forgot they taught us how to use =count() functions & refused to apologize. Avoid if you can, keep your head down if you can't. Don't expect a lot.
Very helpful class in terms of content. SQL unit is incredibly difficult. The flipped classroom format is frustrating and would be nice if it were different.

The worst class I've ever taken. Professors do not come to class and only upload uselessly long videos. The projects are difficult, especially the group projects are terrible, even though she doesn't teach a properly. If you have another professor's class, you should definitely take it! I never wanna take her class again.

Highly disorganized class. Students are expected to watch long mundane lectures and complete projects and exams with no practice of course material. TAs run the class. Practice exams do not relate to exam content.

Worst class I have ever taken. The professor tells you watch the most mundane lectures ever and it is the only thing you are tested on. The classes are absolutely pointless (you learn nothing). Overall, horrible structure.
Teagon doesn't do anything for this class the lectures don't teach you anything, but it is a required class for broad so good luck!
It is very poorly laid out, you will have three projects due on the same day. Taught by TA's, professor just makes really boring and lengthy lecture videos.
Never met professor class is taught by TA's that have no clue what is going on.

Worst class ever. She does not teach the class at all and gives long lecture videos where only very small portions of them are relevant. The TAs try their best but ultimately this is a self-taught class. Threatened about 15% of the students in the class with an ADR on the final project and then takes it back because she was wrong.

Teagan teaches asynchronously which doesn't really help when wanting to ask in person classes. TA's barely know what they are talking about during class periods. Class is very test/quiz/project heavy and have to watch long boring lecture videos. Excel is the only useful thing you learn!

The first lecture video caught me off guard.. lady with a deep voice. The TAs basically run the class and they barely know how to answer your questions. It was pretty much self-taught, but I did all of the work and was able to get a 4.0. There was a help room for projects, and Teagan usually gave practice exams which were similar to the real one.

online lectures are hard to follow because she goes on so many unnnessesary rants. The class final grade was a 70. A 70!!!! I am a junior and I have never seen an exam average that low. she then proceeds to take weeks to grade a project and threatens everyone with ADRS. My stress level has never been so high than when im in Teagans class.

Teagan responds pretty quickly via email and the ULAs office hours help a lot. The lecture videos werent bad as long as you watch at 1.5x. The assignments/projects weren't difficult but read the instructions carefully. She also gives out practice exams that are just like the real thing. Overall, as long as you do the work, you'll get at least a 3.5
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Teagan is a very nice, helpful professor. She went above and beyond to make sure I was able to understand the code and platform so I could do my project successfully. ITM is not a fun class but it is very necessary for the business world and Teagan is a great leader for it.
I dont get taught at all in this class. TAs just assign you classwork and are expected to understand with nothing but a video posted lecture that makes no sense

The material in this class isn't hard, so don't take this rating as a rating of ITM. Sure, availability outside of class exists, and there is knowledge on the subject here. But D2L was organized so poorly, and the TAs for my section were often confused by demo instructions. It was just an unnecessarily stressful class because of the way it was run.

Homework assignments are easy. For the individual projects, the instructions are not clear and the TA's aren't super helpful for them either. If you show up to class, you get extra credit most of the time. Group project was very easy. The TA's run the class. You don't need to watch the lectures either, just skim for tests & quizzes.

ITM209 is taught by 2 TAs and lecture videos from the professor. The class felt very unorganized and I always felt lost but it is possible to do good. I 4.0. Study practice exam materials and go to helproom / set up zoom calls if you have questions on projects. There is a lot of points available in this class. You got it!

This entire class is based off of exams, which have nothing to do with the material taught in class. The whole class is taught a TA who barely even know how to do any of the 'demos' done in class. I never once saw the professor except in lecture videos that you must watch in order to know exam material. If I could, I would choose any other prof.

Used McGraw-Hill SIMbook, which is an absolute crap system, almost shovelware. Lectures were a waste of time, most of the homework is "brain off, follow these exact instructions." Poor quality, and activities don't seem to align well with the stated course objectives. Would be nice if they put some effort into this class. 
Two thumbs down :(

Absolutely the worst class I've ever taken. I can't believe they made me pay money for it. The class is only taught by TAs and most of the work is HW. The worst part of it all is the quizzes. They do NOT match up with what you learn and practice in class or for homework AT ALL. If you can, avoid this class and learn Excel on your own.

Never saw this professor once. Your TA's teach you everything and you have no clue if they're good or not until class starts. Attendance is required. Lots of things to do before each class, multiple projects, and difficult exams which don't focus on what you learned in class. Got early to help room for projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pain class, you will hate every moment
This class was the worst class I have ever taken. I would not recommend this class to anyone avoid it at all costs. The grading scale was absolutely ridiculous and completely unfair. Worst prof ever.

Awful class, moved through big topics quickly, tested on material not covered in class, Would not recommend to anyone, No curve on anything even from the excel unit where the tech used would randomly mark answers wrong for clicking an extra button etc., insultingly added 0.1% to everyone's course grades, thank you so much for your generosity!

Wish I had more than 350 letters. Poorly organized, class was run with no curve on any exams or quizzes or course overall, Received a raw 79% of all 990 points in the class, and will be receiving a 2.5. Taught completely by TAs, test are completely based on irrelevant information from additional lecture videos you must watch outside of class 0/1000

Participation isn't mandatory, but the few times I wasn't able to attend, I didn't understand the homework -- so I highly suggest attending. Professor Dixon is always available to help, and helprooms are also very useful. There is a lot of homework, but it isn't too bad if you watch the lectures and go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The set up of class could not have been worst. The material was challenging and it was solely taught by the TAs. Both the TAs and the professor were not good with answering emails and when they did, they did not address all of the questions asked. It was very difficult to get helpful feedback on assignments in a timely manner. Overall, -1000/10.

Professor is very absent from the course and office hours canceled often, so good luck finding help. TA's are less than helpful. When you ask further questions on lectures they don't know how to explain better. Course starts out pretty easy and only gets harder with harsher grading so be prepared. Grades are given back late often without feedback.

Professor and TAs are very absent. They do not provide feedback for assignments so you have know knowledge of what to fix to improve your grade. Also, they do not respond to emails in a timely manor and the responses are not helpful. Do not recommend.

Make sure you attend every class, its not mandatory but it is super hard to do the assignments totally by yourself. Use your TAs. Find a good group of people to do the assignments with cause it seriously helps so much. Get into a group chat. First exam is open note. Teagan is totally absent from course, TAs teach, and Teagan is hard to reach.

Overall the class requires a lot more effort than I anticipated. Tests are only based on memorization, so that makes a challenge specifically for the contents of this course. Really difficult to get help from the TA's or professor when you have questions outside of class, they don't respond to emails. Professor is never in class, only TA led.

I think this class is set up really well. The in class assignments are pretty easy, and if you go to help room, the projects are not too bad. She tells you everything you can expect on the exams as well so as long as you study for the exams you will be fine. This class definitely did keep me busy though as their is a lot to do per week.

Im sure he is a great person, but I just dont see the point of having quizzes on EXCEL. The questions are taken randomly out of the textbook and the only way to get 100% is memorizing every sentence. If my ACC or ECON professors made this type of quiz I wouldnt complain, but for an ITM course????
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Alexandria is an awesome dance professor! She cares so much for her students and makes class like a fun workout! Totally recommend! I will keep taking her classes!

Alexandra is a kind person who is very passionate. But from a dancer perspective I feel I didn't learn much from what I thought the class was going to be. Along with that many things we did in class and talked about made me uncomfortable. If you are a dancer and wanting to dance I don't recommend

I love Alexandria! I am not a dancer by nature but I had a great time in her class. She really cares about your progress and is super understanding. I think I've really improved because of her. I would highly recommend her class

His class is overall easy but attendance is required and there's a lot of out of class readings that your grade depends on. Overall, not hard but his lectures are long and somewhat boring and he enforces a strong no technology policy.

This guy never stops talking. If you try to use your phone during the 2-hour lecture, be ready to get yelled at for being disrespectful and not "plugging in". The class is easy, but you have to read quite a bit outside of class and watch videos for quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class was easy, lectures were aggravating to sit through

Super fast-paced since it was a month-long course. Work was pretty easy! The only complaint that I have is that the quizzes were timed at 10 minutes for 10 questions, which was super stressful. Otherwise, super nice professor, and light work!

Caring and thoughtful professor. Came up with plenty of activities and opportunities for us to engage with the course that really got my mind going. My advice is to always do the homework as the daily iClickers are 50% of your grade. Not difficult at all if you participate. Funny guy too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He honestly is a good professor, he genuinely wants his students to understand the concepts and have their own peace of mind when it comes to discussion.
