reviews.comment: mattes cares about her students a lot and it shows. pretty easy homework each week and shes always so positive. during the coronavirus it felt good to know she was there if i needed to talk to anyone. there was 4 group projects and two exams. not very difficult and i actually learned stuff.

Dr Seven is literally an icon. Her lectures are so interesting and thought provoking, and this quickly became my favourite class this semester. She is very understanding and kind, definitely cares about her students and that they pass. Though the material is fairly easy it is still an amazing class.

Professor Mattes is an awesome professor. Her class has been really organized and easy to keep up with. The tests correlate well with each weeks notes. Very passionate about her job and makes the class very interesting. I enjoyed it a lot.

She is so passionate about her job. Even though I am online with her as a professor, the students can tell that she cares. Her assignment are never that challenging and her tests are always based around what is learned in class. I wish I could've had her in person.
She was an amazing professor! Super funny and the material is very interesting and makes you think. Fave professor thus far..
Super kind and understanding. She talks about a lot of interesting topics and is a funny lighthearted person!
She is very understanding, but the exams are challenging especially being online.

Dr. Seven is by far one of my favorite professors. I took ISS210 online this semester (while its not yet over), she is a bit quirky, but that's also what makes her so fun, understanding, and bubbly. The way her course is set up is super easy to navigate!

Probably the best professor I've ever hadshe is incredibly understanding and her lectures are 100% worth going to. She is very fun, makes goofy puns and jokes and it makes you enjoy the class. Not too much reading just try to keep up a bit and you'll do great. 10/10 professor. I had her at 8am and didn't mind going to class.

Dr. Seven was a great professor. She's very passionate about the class. The exams were all open note. We did have to read 2 books, but it was nothing crazy. You have to attend because there's an attendance code via Tophat, but you can text a friend if you were lazy. Super easy course & great person!
Professor Seven is super nice and a great teacher. She makes lectures interesting and is really cares about her students. Super fun class and person! 10/10 would recommend her class.

Great class. The professor is super sweet and genuinely cares about what she's teaching. There are small participation activities in every class, weekly discussion posts, and three big tests. Tests are easy, all multiple choice, and you are able to take them from your room. You can miss 4 discussion posts. Lectures are interesting, you learn a lot.

Cool teacher. She is a super happy person and she seems to enjoy her job. She is very knowledgeable and helpful. This class is a free A if you do the study guides because they are exactly like the test and all tests are open note. You get to miss 4 blog posts, so dont feel pressured to do all of them. Extra credit is also awarded.

She's a bit odd, but overall very friendly and upbeat every day. The class can be a little boring at times, but as long as you pay attention and complete the weekly blog assignments it's really an easy A.

Dr. Seven is a great professor!! She is super kind, caring and makes her class fun and interesting. I advise that you do read the books and do the discussion boards though! Those are graded. The tests are not very hard and there are only 3 tests as well. Overall, I would highly recommend her class and I would take it again!!

Seven is a fantastic teacher, best I have had yet. Although the class is a little tough if you do your stuff its not bad at all. She is one of the most knowledgeable teachers about her area of study I have had yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor! Makes her class fun and educational, helps students stay engaged. Very little work for a 4 credit class, just make sure to do the study guide before the exams and you'll be golden.

ISS-210 I would 100% recommend taking this class. The lectures are interesting, the teacher is very helpful, and its a 4 credit class. The exams are quite literally the study guide, which in turn is just the slides she does in class, which are also online. She uses tophat for attendance and questions. Once a week homework and 1 ez group project

Dr. Seven is hands down the most fun, laid-back, and friend-like professor/teacher I've ever met. Add in the fact that she's really passionate about the course and will have you questioning your existence, and you have one of the best classes in the whole school

Dr. Seven creates an inviting space with clear power points that are easy to follow. She made me laugh and truly opened my eyes with the material covered in class. Be prepared to challenge your views on animals and society. Readings are not mandatory to succeed but are sometimes necessary for the weekly prompt.

SUPER easy class. Her lectures are long but she's funny sometimes. She does questions at the beginning of each class, and it was based off of accuracy. The questions were based off of the readings. Loved her.

This class was very informative, but not too hard. For tests, you are allowed to have a note sheet, and she posts a study guide. You are expected to read the textbook, because she will have an in-class quiz before every lecture based on the reading. There is homework for every book chapter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is the easiest class I have taken. The lectures are important to go to for extra credit, lecture points and for exam material. There is so much extra credit given that I had 20 points of extra credit over the maximum points available in the class. You get a cheat sheet on the test and the beginning of lecture quizzes are just vocab.
Pretty easy class. The only thing that might be time consuming are the textbook readings before classes.

I love Prof Nawyn. There are iclicker questions and daily quizzes but they are easy as long as you do the readings which are a little long but its fine. Inquisitives were annoying but easy points. Very fun and followable lectures, shes funny here and there too. Very accommodating and there are many points in the class. Easy exams w a note card.

Dr. Nawyn is amazing. Wasn't super interested in sociology before this semester but she made every class interesting. She clearly cares about her students and she's absolutely hilarious. Exams aren't too hard if you study with inquisitive because she gives you a one page cheat sheet.

Dr. Nawyn actually wants her students to succeed. Make sure to do the inquisitive/reading before every class because there is a quiz at the start of every lecture. You get a reference sheet for every exam and Her study guides are also very accurate to the tests so make sure to base your sheet on them. Lots of extra credit opportunities
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nawny's SOC is extremely easy for an introduction course. There are four exams total, along with quizzes for every class period, which are typically 3-4 questions based off the reading and are terminology based. She is down to earth and HILARIOUS. Not hard at all, reading isn't really necessary for these exams, they are also open note.

This class was extremely easy to the point that showing up basically guarantees a 4.0 because the last couple of weeks are straight extra credit. The exams weren't bad at all, with extra credit on them and multiple correct answers. If you try, you will do well. Dr. Nawyn is also great at teaching and is very insightful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Nawyn is an amazing lecturer who truly cares about her topic. Reading quizzes at the beginning of class with iclicker attendance but other than that very little work. Her study guides make it easy to do well on tests as she tells you what topics will be on it beforehand. As long as you focus a bit in class a good grade is attainable.

Yes, Dr. Nawyn shifted the format of the class, but it was due to the fact that people were cheating on exams by using AI! So, if you are an authentic student who is willing to study and engage in class work, you will be fine! She is extremely generous with extra credit and exams. I took this as an elective my final semester and it was an easy 4.0!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She changed up the class structure, but it still is a super easy class. As long as you show up to class for majority of the semester you're able to easily get an A in the class. Most of your points are from attendance via the iclicker at the end of class. Also you're allowed a double sided cheat sheet for the exam, and she provides a study guide!

Averaging D+ on each exam after studying and having a piece of paper with notes on it. Ratings looked good that's why I took this class in the first place, not at all like the reviews. Professor herself is nice however the exams are stupid hard for no reason. Also a ton of inquizitive and in class quizzes and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's a great professor! She changed the class structure tho... used to be open-note at home online exams but now they're in-person on scantron and you only get a cheat sheet. Exams kinda caught me off guard because of how difficult they can be even after studying. For a 100-level class, the exams should not be that difficult.

Changed the entire structure of the class because too many people were doing good in the past and cheating. Now all exams are in person scantron. reading check quiz nearly every class. shes nice and funny sometimes.

To everyone who said this class was easy, well it isn't anymore. Because of chat, she has made the exams extremely difficult, in person and scantron. This is an elective for most people and is my hardest class for no reason. She seems like a very nice and educated person though.

I really enjoyed Professor Nawyn's lectures. She's funny and explains terms/theories well. She has online open note exams, weekly readings, and iclicker quizzes, but they're fairly easy if you read the textbook and pay attention in class. Would 100% recommend taking SOC 100 with her!

All exams are open note/book, super easy class overall and hard not to 4.0! Lectures can be long/boring, she tends to get off task. The sweetest professor-intelligent, understanding, down to earth, absolutely hilarious. She wants everyone to succeed. I wish I could get coffee with her. Couldn't recommend enough!

Such a wonderful professor to have. She is educated, thoughtful, passionate, and caring to her students. She truly does care, and you can just tell. There were five exams, with the final, and one can be dropped. All are open note, and most were taken online, with an in-person option. No reason not to take a class with such a wonderful person :)

I enjoyed her lectures because she was funny, made it interesting and notes were pretty straightforward. She uses iClicker every lecture for quizzes over the readings you were supposed to read outside of class. Exams are all open note and you have one hour to complete 70 questions, which can be overwhelming. Overall, I had a great experience.

Class is attendance based for iClicker quizzes and attendance. Exams are online 

Teacher is super liberal and biased to the left side of the political spectrum if you do not put up with that stuff.
Amazing professor for SOC 100, she has open note exams and all taken online. Her lectures are very funny and it was very enjoyable. I would recommend taking this course.
Exams are open book and open notes, watch out for in-class quizzes from the textbook, funny lectures with detailed lecture slides.

Super funny and sweet. Lectures can seem boring and drag on for a while even though they're only a couple slides long, but she always let us out early and says important things. Make sure to read the textbook before class because she has in-class quizzes based on assigned readings. Open book and note for exams, and can be taken anywhere.

Class was insanely easy. Exams online no lockdown browser. She is super chill and lecture gets out 30-40 minutes early. Also don't buy the textbook I got a 4.0 and never used it it was a waste of money.

Total queen.  She's very funny and relatable, and she teaches the course material well.  You have to read a decent amount and study some for tests, but her personality and teaching mostly makes it worth it.
Grading is difficult when the test has the same 10 questions and she doesn't give good questions

This professor is very rude and difficult to work with. Her grading criteria is unclear and she even confuses her TA. The tests are poorly made and she does everything in her power to try to get students to stay the whole lecture by tricking us with multiple quizzes even when she says it's a no quiz day. She is not accommodating and disrespectful.

She's a good professor. You don't necessarily need the textbook but there's in-class quizzes everyday that use it and that count for a grade and attendance. You have to either take notes as she lectures or download it before hand because she doesn't provide any note sheets or study guides. Exams are online, no lockdown browser.

Dr. Nawyn is an amazing prof! I wish I could take every class with her. She's so passionate about what she teaches. There will be a few writing assignments but they're not hard. Also do the reading bc she has in class quizzes and sometimes offers bonus points.

Dr. Nawyn is a great lecturer. She keeps the lecture interesting and is really funny. Her class was one of the most interesting classes. There is a short video assignment and a blog assignment, but it isn't too challenging. Dr. Nawyn is the Beyonce of professors at MSU.

Excellent professor, very interested in what she's teaching and wholeheartedly tries to appeal and be sensitive to students of all backgrounds and upbringings. Definitely wants her students to pass & receive good grades.

I loved this class. Super interesting subject matter, and Professor Nawyn kept the lectures upbeat. Professor Nawyn has many real-world examples of the subject matter she teaches, so this made it easier for me to learn. You do have to go to lecture though, because there are (easy) iClicker quizzes everyday.

I was not looking forward to taking this course because I had already taken the equivalent for my other majors, but now I am SO grateful I did. Prof. Nawyn is hilarious, brilliant, and genuinely cares about her students. I have never been to office hours just to talk to the prof until now. Her classes are amazing and her teaching is even better.

She is an awesome professor and I'm taking another one of her courses because I love her style. She speaks to students like equals and has great, real world examples. Her lectures are actually helpful and interesting.

Slow grades (no grades entered more than halfway through the semester), and the course topic is just not what the class is described as. If you want to learn more about Chilean politics, def take this course, but if you're looking for reading writing by women, this isn't it.

McCleese only gave out 5 assignments the whole semester.  She takes attendance randomly so just attend even though it is boring af. Her lessons are so boring, playing minesweeper is more entertaining. She reads everything off of a slideshow, (which that is NOT posted to D2L).

This professor graded everything a week before the course ended. An okay instructor who oddly made the class about food culture. Assignments were easy ten-minute tasks, with only five total grades, so submit on time. Attendance wasn't taken, so skipping didn't matter. Clear grading, but never replied to emails.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. I was expecting the course to relate to the description MSU put out, but she put an "indigenous food studies" twist to it. Lectures consist of her reading slides in a monotone voice. She gives us useless assingments and hasn't graded anything the entire semester (less than a month left). Stay away.

Very careless about student feedback or incidents. Took random attendance for the first month as a scare tactic, then suddenly stopped, nobody knows when she will take attendance next. If you are absent, she gives 0 grace to your situation regardless of how serious. She has a temper, and petty mannerisms. There's not much work she gives out.

Easy 4.0 she didn't really have class a lot and was an easy grader besides that he grading didn't go in till the last day but if you want an easy 4.0 take it with her you also only like have 4 scattered assignments so if you don't really care and are a good writer this class is for you

As an exchange student the class was anything but interesting especially when we had to read a book about a child vampire having relations with adults and we had activities on this without analyzing it in class. Moreover she takes MONTHS to grade homework and if you have a problem don't count on her to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. McCleese lacks clarity in instruction and grading. Lectures consist of reading directly from slides, offering no real engagement. With unclear assignment criteria, it's difficult to perform well. Her teaching style is ineffective and grades are often NEVER returned. It is finals week and I still have not received a single grade back.

Dr.Mccleese is a nice person yet she has no idea how to grade. I have zero grades right now and it is the end of the semester. She will yell at you if you talk and she does not know how to give instruction on any assignment so you have to figure it out yourself. It is an easy class but I wouldn't take it with her.

Dr. McCleese is clearly a great scholar but she CAN NOT TEACH. She only reads off slides the entire lecture and takes forever to grade anything despite promising to grade sooner. She is literally afraid of students and acts very timid.

Other reviews are true, I didn't get anything out of the class, but if you want something easy you found it. I skipped class often and my grade wasn't effected. I didn't put a lot of work into the papers and I just rambled and made stuff up for the final project because I didn't read the book it was about and I got a 4.0 in the class so I'm not mad

My grade on this class was based on 2 300 pnt papers, 1 300 pnt project, and 200 pnts of attendance thats c/nc. Criteria for assignments was unclear and as such they were very difficult to write. The D2L is closed and final grades are due today by 4 but she has not graded a single assignment. Lectures are boring and she reads directly from slides
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reads exclusively off of slides. If you have any questions, Just look it up bc the answer she gives you will just make you more confused. She seems like a very intelligent person, just a bad teacher. Didn't feel like I learned anything. Also takes forever to grade papers. Almost 2 months for Paper #1 to be returned.

Very poor experience. Very late grader, unclear and confusing projects and grading guidelines. Lectures are monotone, unengaging, and unhelpful. Is not accessible outside of class, email regarding course was never returned.

The course was graded by 2 papers, attendance, and the Final Project. The first paper was due October 6th and we only got our grades a week ago. She doesn't take attendance. The Final is a five minute video and seems like she thought about the project before class that day. Lectures consist of her reading off of a slide in a very monotone voice

Every one of these reviews is accurate. The course was extremely unorganized and Professor Mccleese often times seemed like she had no idea what she was talking about. Completely lacking passion, and has not posted a single grade since the semester started. It was difficult to find the will to attend class. If you can avoid it, I suggest you do.

I would not recommend her class. I feel like I've learned nothing and wasted my time attending her lectures. She just reads off slides and doesn't explain anything in simple terms, so it's pretty confusing most of the time, which made me dread participating. There's no course outline and she didn't grade our papers till a month later.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Teaching style terrible. Didn't give out grades till after multiple complaints. Lots of research papers to read outside of class. Teaches concepts in expert level way despite it being new content to us. Don't bother asking questions because her responses are complex and even more confusing. Participation mandatory. Never took attendance.

The class time was poorly used; Her instructions for assignments were unclear; there was poor structure for learning; no effort was put into the syllabus; she refused to give concrete dates at the beginning of the semester for anything; grades for the first essay have not been released, and the next essay is due soon; she gives excuses;

This professor did not aspire to make class interesting. Somehow, reading about profane vampire relations turned boring. She also didn't make attendance mandatory which was nice, as it was hard to self-motivate to go to her class.

DO NOT TAKE CLASSES FROM THIS PROFESSOR. She takes months to grade assignments, gives little to no instruction for her assignments, uploads drop-boxes for assignments after the due date, does not give a syllabus for the class, and doesn't contribute any of her own thinking or work into her class. I strongly STRONGLY advise you to not take her class

She did not consider attendance this semester due to Covid and tried her best to be accommodating. She is a brilliant woman, however, her language is more appropriate for colleagues than introductory-level students. She takes a long time to grade, and her grading policy is somewhat unclear. Classes are mostly her reading directly from PP slides.

I liked Dr. McCleese. She was an alright professor for a basic class. There were only a couple projects in the class but she put the grades in at the last couple weeks of class. Sometimes class was only 10 minutes long when it was supposed to be an almost 2 hour class. It felt pointless to go. She is a very easy grader tho.

Technically attendance is mandatory, but she hasn't taken it since the start of the semester. Due dates unclear, often pushed back because she never gives any place for it to be turned in at. Came into class sick once post COVID when it was explicitly stated not to do that. The class isn't difficult, but emotionally draining lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Too harsh of a grader.

GIVE THIS MAN A RAISE!!! Content & exams are seriously tough, but most of the grade comes from pre class & in class assignments & the project. Show up every day and you'll do great. Dr Haut is an amazing & chill guy who TRULY cares about his students (more than any prof I've ever had). I highly recommend him and getting to know him in this course!
Super hardass over a 2 hundred level course.
Super smart guy. Will give you high-quality detailed advice so make sure you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very helpful with content questions. The in-class assignments aren't too complicated and I learned a lot.

so nice & genuine! really thorough w answering questions, i had a great experience w this class even as someone that doesn't like cs :) one thing is that the ML unit is quite hard, and it's common to not finish the in-class activities (although they are graded for completion). the exams are lowkey rough but they're not heavily weighted.

Anyone who rates him poorly probably never asked him a content question. He will sit with you and help you through your work. His explanations are clear and he is very thorough in his descriptions of the content. Very kind and engaging guy.
Not ideal teaching format

One of the best math professors I've had. His lectures are very clear and simple making them not hard to follow along. His office hours were the main reason I got A's on the tests so I highly recommend going to them if you ever need help on the content or just for review before a test. He is always very kind and helpful whenever you talk to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was good at explaining tough concepts. I didn't get the best grade because I missed some lectures towards the end but every time I attended I was able to understand the concepts, very nice guy.
He is really good and the class in really exam heavy but as long as you come to lecture and understand the material the class is light.

Calc 3 is one of the hardest classes I've taken at Michigan State, but the main difference I vastly prefer it over Calc 2 is because of Professor Ovenhouse. His lectures were always super detailed and he always went over good examples, which prepared you really well for homework and exams. 10/10.
He's really nice and approachable, and easy to understand when he lectures. He's super smart but can teach at a understandable level. Also really helpful in office hours.

Nick is a great teacher. He obviously loves his subject and wants his students to do well. He's very organized and will answer any questions you have in a manner that benefits you as a student. He'll go over homework assignments to make sure you can complete them. The only downside is Lab Day - you'll have to work in groups on a large worksheet.
Great overall person, easy to talk to, teaches great, and he has a manly ass beard

She is VERY picky when it comes to grading. Post-reading assignments will most likely be the lower grades you get in the class, because if you don't answer the questions in the way she wants, she will dock points. Somewhat recommend? It's not an easy 4.0, but if it fits your schedule, then why not.
Seems like a nice person, but I find the class to be mind-numbing. Expect to learn the material on your own time because the whole class time is taken up reviewing the homework from the day before.
Worst professor I've had at MSU. Do not take any courses with her, I'm taking an online IAH course right now and she is so harsh with grading.
Do not take a class with this professor. She is a tough grader for a class that should be easy. I do not recommend.

DO.NOT.TAKE.HER. Has no clear instructions and its a teach your own class. This is based off of homework and says it is based off completion when it is truly based on correctness.  She says you get three excused absences, but only marks participation as grading, so basically you can not miss a single class. I advise you drop the class if signed up

Very direct and can have an attitude. Classes consist of mostly answering HW questions, which wasn't helpful as little time was left for lecture slides. Grading is REALLY tough and instructions can be unclear. However, HW is a big part of your grade which can cover up a bad exam. Very accessible outside class and helpful feedback.

This professor does not help you learn anything. She instead uses her time to send multiple emails out to students accusing them of using AI. Multiple people have now dropped the course due to fears of them receiving an academic dishonesty report, even if they didn't use AI... Adding to that, her D2L is not set up correctly. Do NOT TAKE HER !!!!!!!

This professor is terrible. Grading is impossible to understand, and there's no guidance on how to do better. I reached out multiple times but never got clear answers. The course materials were confusing, and her explanations only made things harder. It's frustrating to feel stuck with no support or direction.

FIRE HER! Worst professor ever hard grader who never gives helpful feedback. The textbook was useless. She said to ask for help, but her replies were unclear and confusing, leaving me more lost. I'm a native speaker, so it's not a language issue. She just doesn't help students improve or understand.

Carmen grades your essays as if you are already a native speaker, and will accuse you of using google translate with no good reason, to the point where i had to purposely put mistakes in my essay just so she doesn't accuse me for it. The grade boundaries are extremely high, and she will not curve it no matter how bad the class is doing.

I was terrified to take her summer SPN202 course after reading the reviews. Her character is blunt and to the point — I believe this is where majority of the bad reviews are coming from. She is, however, an incredible teacher with effective curricula. Her class was challenging, but was the one I improved in most out of the four SPN classes I took.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A year ago I was reading the reviews thinking "she can't be that bad." I was wrong. She has accused me of using google translate when I did not with no evidence. Does not take criticism but instead makes excuses. I truly dreaded each class not because the coursework was difficult but simply because I didn't want to deal with her attitude. Avoid.

As a native speaker this class was SO hard. They DON'T round. A 4.0 is a 94% so make sure to remember that. You have to do lessons before the class (another prof teaches the content) and they are time consuming but extremely important. Your grade relies on participation (2 pts for every lecture). Be sure to do all work & do well on tests/exams.

Profe Carmen was my favorite professor this semester. She is funny and caring. Participation in class is big for your grade so try not to miss classes. But she helps make sure everyone participates. SPN 310 has a pretty big workload since lectures, homework, and quizzes are all outside of class, but she helps clear things up in class.

Carmen was scary at first because of her high expectations and advanced language use in class. LOTS of hw but is the same for all SPN 310 classes and participation in class is required for a grade. She comes off strong but is very willing to help after class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She really cares that every student is on the same page & is very approachable if you need any help. I was always excited to go to her class because she's very funny. She fosters a great environment in class as she's always making jokes in class. She gets to know each of her students and it's clear she puts time into her lectures. Take her class!

Very brute and unapproachable, if you dont do things her way (even if they contradict the syllabus) you wont succeed in her class. She hones in on struggling students and made several cry and made some even abandon the language/minor all together. So bad with technology and communication

Overall, she is a nice lady. She responded to my emails very quickly and you can tell she is passionate about what she teaches. My only complaint is that the grading criteria/syllabus was not very clear at the beginning of this semester (new to the course), but got better as we progressed. She is also not flexible with late assignments at all.

Professor Octavio was pretty good. She is from Spain so she has a Spanish accent. She also hates technology with a burning passion. I took SPN 310 with her. None of the professors for that course give very clear feedback, and you do all the lectures by yourself. The textbook was pretty much useless except for when it was required for homework.

I had her for 201and 202 a year apart; her teaching improved (clearly as she's taken on more classes since). When you have a good group for class she is very entertaining and always joking with students. She really cares that her students are understanding and adjusts her teaching methods accordingly. Her classes are hard but appropriately so.

incredibly rude to all students in class and even picked on a specific person in my section, poor explanations of core concepts and would often not answer questions asked. heavy homework load that doesn't really benefit you in class. mandatory attendance, tough grader in class on both oral and written assignments. just take my word for it and avoid

She is amazing. I've had 2 SPN classes with her. She really cares about whether or not students are learning from her and her teaching methods. I've had private conversations with her and she cares for her student's well-being and success so much. She is so accommodating to personal issues. I would strongly recommend her as a professor.

Profesora Octavio is short-tempered, unreasonable, and difficult to work with. Directions and criteria for assignments are often unclear. She is not tech savvy, she becomes very upset when students make technology related mistakes or have poor connection, but then expects grace when she does the same. Do yourself a favor and avoid her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Octavio requires you to spend a minimum of 70$ on books/conversations if you want to pass. She assigns an abundance of online work/TalkAbroad transcriptions that you are unable to receive any credit for if submitted late, no matter the reason. Attendance is mandatory due to in class activities everyday that receive a 0 if not present
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was one of the best professors I've had since coming to MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: SPN330 is okay, but Octavio is the worst professor I have had. She is condescending, short-tempered, and has no patience when answering valid student questions. You might feel bad for not already knowing it all. She asks for our understanding with her life and technical difficulties but is unwilling to accommodate or be flexible with her students.

In all four years of undergrad, Octavio was by far my least favorite professor. She grades so tough if it were up to her she would fail almost everybody. She also picks on struggling students and makes it impossible to want or receive her help. She even made a student cry once. I'd pick a new language before I'd pick her class.

Worst professor I ever had. Her classroom felt toxic and unsafe, everyday I could sense that everyone else was uncomfortable too. She would snap at students for no reason, name call, use profanity. Her excuse for this behavior is that people in Spain are blunt and that Americans want to be coddled. No, we just want to feel safe and respected.

Do not take this prof if you can avoid it. She is often unclear about directions or expectations, and students are too afraid to ask her to clarify because she's rude when people don't understand. She also doesn't help students when they're struggling with what they're trying to say and instead ridicules them.

reviews.comment: Do not, I mean never ever ever ever ever take her section of SPN. She is horrible, she is condescending and creates a toxic learning environment. She wants heavy participation but does not offer help to students that are struggling with phrasing sentences. Worst professor I have had in my three year of university.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Onsay is the bestest professor I have ever experienced!! She is always very supportive to her students to keep track of the progress we have done and she generally is very appreciative of my eagerness towards learning CSE 331 as well as suggesting me to go to review sessions for exams to clear up all the concepts leading to difficultly
Actually cares about her students, probably one of the most caring professors you can have.
bro w professor bro fr

This course feels very repetitive among all the assignments, with everything being fully taught atleast twice for the most part. While DSA is very important for CS, the amount of work for this class definitely felt like atleast 4 or 5 credits worth. Otherwise, if you study and apply yourself in the coursework, you will be successful in this course.

Onsay is my favorite professor by far, and I have spent 2 years at MSU. She is sweet, caring, respecting, and does everything she can to help us understand the material and do well in the class. She does give a decent bit of easy homework, but all of it is HEAVILY related to the material and WILL HELP YOU and your grade - DO THEM. I will miss her.

Passionate and caring professor, calls us all "colleagues" and has us build our "backpack" of knowledge to apply to future projects, interviews, and jobs. There is a lot of content to learn, but class is paced reasonably. Only critique is many things are redundant (lectures, videos, Zybooks all teach the same thing) and d2l is hard to navigate.

Dr. Onsay is an engaging lecturer, which made the content easy to understand intuitively. The course load is very heavy, so it does take time to get used to, and you should give yourself at least a few hours a week on CCs and Projects. She doesn't penalize for AI, but it's hard to do well on exams if you rely on it entirely to code for you.

Onsay is by far one of the best professors i've had. She really cares for the students and structures the course for our long term career benefit. The exams are very easy to study for, the textbook and assignments give you everything to get at least a 3.0 in the class if you study. Theres a good amount of work required but it comes on the exams.

Bro she a GOAT. The course is chill, a lot of working but if you just see her videos and then go to lecture you'll be fine. She understands you got stuff going. She chill and tbh you can really vibe with her if you enjoy DSA like she does. Also she always looking for TAs so if you wanna be one just participate and make yourself known

You can tell she loves to teach and is good at it. If you put in the work, you will get a good grade. Lots of homework in this class but its good because it reinforces the material you are going to be tested. Class material is useful for future success as well. Great class in general, she is very caring. D2L is a mess lol

The workload is that of a 3 course class but the amount of repetition between the lectures, the lecture videos, and the online book makes it feel like a 4 course class. She really cares for her students and their success. The exam content is very fair for the most part but going back through content to study takes a lot of time.

Very poorly structured & disorganized course. Too much material: unnecessarily repetitive with videos, zybooks, lectures covering the same content. Took WAY more time than my other classes combined. D2L is a mess, with content all over the place. Each project is 1% & each exam is 17% of your grade. Def NOT a 3 credit workload, more like 5 credits.

The professor is great, and you can tell she cares about the students. My only complaint is that the class has tons of material, and she does a terrible job of organizing things on D2L. It is such a mess and hard to study for an exam. The concepts are fairly easy but she tends to overcomplicate them when explaining in class.

Onsay is a good professor and cares about students. However, the course itself is poorly organized and sometimes burdensome for no reason. The flipped classroom introduces repetitive work, which ends up being very time-consuming without significantly improving learning outcomes. Students are flooded with a jumbled collection of course material.

It's easily the biggest relief of a professor at MSU for CSE. Onsay deeply cares about her students and wants them to succeed. There is a lot of work within the course, don't get me wrong, but because of that, It requires little studying because the content is drilled into your head. I would rework a class schedule to be in her class personally.
It is a crying shame that Prof Onsay teaches but one computer science course.

I really liked this class. It was painful and stressful, but that comes with the computer science territory. The online textbook & D2L page have plenty of material, and ChatGPT is semi-allowed. Not to write a whole project, but great as a debugger. Just make sure you know the content by heart before exam night though!

Dr. Onsay will \provide you with support and care about your learning if you participate in class and put in effort. Although this class is not easy, she makes a great learning environment for all of her students. Make sure to utilize helprooms when taking this class as the TA's provide lots to offer as well.

She's definitely my favorite professor I have had within the MSU computer science department. She really seemed to care about her students and her lectures were actually engaging. She tells you exactly how it is, even if it's not what you would want to hear which I really respect in a professor. She was great in preparing us for a future in CS!

Professor Onsay is probably the best professor I've had here. She is passionate about what she teaches and genuinely cares about her students. The workload for this class is heavy, but if you run into problems, the helprooms are well run and worth it. Most of the content follows alongside zybooks. Overall an amazing professor.

Unexpectedly, the professor suggested I switch from my computer science major, despite her reputation for excellence based on positive reviews. The course, biased towards stronger students, missed practical elements and was excessively fast-paced, culminating in a disheartening experience.

Class was poorly structured with project quizzes usually happening 1-2 weeks after the project was due and quiz questions being generally confusing. But it wasn't that difficult, so it's fine. I don't appreciate the exams being outside of scheduled lecture times.

Def go to all the lectures and do Zybooks. There are weekly projects and a lot of the info is contained within both of those. She's excited about the content and I learned a lot about efficient code. Has a temper so don't make her mad. Don't expect her to round your grade up, despite how close you are to the next grade. I was 0.05% away.

Onsay was an incredible professor. After taking 232 with Nahum the bar was set extremely low, but Onsay was outstanding. She really cares about teaching and providing all the necessary material for us to succeed. Super nice and friendly. Overall great professor. Best in the CSE department. 10/10

Onsay was good. You can tell she cared about students doing well in the course and would always give side notes on what's expected in interviews and in your internships/jobs. The flipped-learning style of this class was not the best and there are far too many lectures with most lectures being insanely long. Overall, a very useful class.

Onsay was one of if not the best professor I have had during my time at MSU. She was passionate about what she taught and made it interesting. She was honest with us and wanted us to succeed. Has experience in the industry and offered very helpful and realistic advice about job searching and technical interviewing in the computer science field.
Overall, amazing prof.

One of the nicest professors I have had, very helpful and knowledgeable. Not a good teacher though, lectures are hard to sit through and lecture slides are 100+ slides long every day making it almost impossible to study them or use them for projects.

I had Professor Elemo for MC 201 and am currently taking her MC 492 class. She does an excellent job explaining complex readings and breaking them down clearly. She is thoughtful, supportive, and genuinely cares about her students' success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Elemo's truly one of my favorite JMC professors. I had some medical issues towards the end of the semester and she was extremely understanding when it came to my absences (unlike some other professors). She's truly passionate about what she's teaching and talking to her about class material is extremely beneficial. Highly recommend!

I had her for MC 201. Though I didn't like her class my freshman year, I realized she's actually an amazing professor in MC325! She has amazing lectures, helpful during office hours, and overall a very understanding professor if you show up. Attendance is very important but you're allowed four absences which is much more than other professors.

MC377: Culture, Politics, and Postcolonialism: Profiling Sub-Saharan Africa
Here's the tea: Elemo is VERY supportive in providing resources and suggestions for final projects and large essays. Has engaging lectures and values class participation. Communication is key, highly recommend attending office hours. E-K is a great prof for this subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Contrary to popular belief, she's a very good prof. Her tone may be condescending at times, but she teaches well and has clear expectations. She is a tough grader but provides good advice. Just take her feedback into account and go to office hours if you're struggling and you'll be fine.

I did not feel like Elemo created a safe space for class discussions, as myself and many of my other peers felt afraid to answer questions incorrectly. Her grading was not very consistent in my experience. When I met with her for office hours she was understanding and helpful, although it was difficult to reach her.

I'd never felt so lost. In class I felt I strongly understood material, and was praised on my knowledge of the subject. Yet, she never gave me above a 3.0 on quizzes. When reaching out for help, I left with more questions than answers and felt absolutely humiliated for performing terribly my first year of college. Only did well due to the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Elemo-Kaka was definitely not my favorite, she was extremely passive aggressive and I did not learn much from her. She told us she was leaving a week before her departure and did not help with the transition of the new professor. She does provide A LOT of feedback but overall I would not take this class with her again.

Professor Elmo is tough, but you will learn a lot from her. She is a good teacher. She really makes it so that you can understand the material. You have to be willing to put in the work to receive a decent grade. She gives good feedback on assignments and if you take her feedback you can do well in the class.
Very lecture heavy in a discussion based recitation, calls us her colleague but passive aggressively.

Recommending MC231 with Prof Elemo for those looking a challenging and highly rewarding class. She made me think critically about course material (CM) and gave eye opening experiences throughout the entire sem. Advice: Go to office hours prepared, don't ask questions before class (do after or email), ground points in CM, speak up if confused.

reviews.comment: She does not allow for participation and then gives people low grades for not participating. She grades very hard but it is unclear why you did not meet her expectations. She does not provide rubrics for essay prompts. She does not make herself available to students. Don't take a class with her if you want to get grades you deserve and work for.

She's an okay teacher, but she grades very hard. It's known throughout the class that she doesn't teach us well enough for the way she grades. reviews.comment: Professor Hawkins is brand new to JMC/PTCD, but he is a truly great teacher. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite JMC prof I've had thus far, he creates a comfy environment. I used to be so nervous to join discussions, but I was good to share my takes in this class. He gives genuine feedback, and will happily meet with you if you need help. He also lectures with slides instead of just yapping for a straight hour and a half. Pls take him he's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hawkins is a refreshing change in the PTCD lineup. He has moved away from the usual Straussian dogma toward a more critical, historically grounded approach. If you're a Straussian, you may not enjoy the critical readings so much, but there will be ample opportunity to interpret and grapple with the canonical texts. Participating is key!

reviews.comment: The TAs teach the course. I've never even met the main professor. If you get a good TA, then you will get a good grade. Luckily, mine was amazing!
Very chill, easy 4.0.
rg34g45g34g435g
Very nice and kind, easy class, very involved and passionate about content.

Such a nice professor!!! You also can tell how much he loves teaching this. Made class interesting enough for people who don't like science. Group projects that weren't awful although some days were more boring than others. Mandatory attendance but he usually lets us go early.
Lectures are tough to sit through but I was able to do other homework. Prelab and postlab due before every class which are easy. I think the class in general is boring but overall easy.

Professor is really passionate about rivers and you can tell based off of the lectures. This was a pretty simple course and I would recommend to anyone who needs the ISP credit. The exams were online and there was weekly homework that wasn't too bad!

In class assignments you can do from home, lectures are SO hard to sit through. three exams that were all taken online outside of class, not proctored. I would recommend to others for integrative studies requirement. very easy coursework that takes less than 10 mins. not a lot of homework at all
Homework is extremely light and take about 10 minutes to complete. Exams are a bit weird and lectures are average. Still an amazing professor who cares about his students and the material he teaches

Lectures were boring as I'm not passionate about the environment, but Ozzy is a caring professor and an interesting person. Attendance is based on short questions you have to turn in online after class, and exams were online for the winter/spring '25 semester. He understands outside circumstances and will be lenient as long as you have reason.
His lecture is great. Homework and class assignments aren't too hard. There are three exams.

Very little workload, and he tried his best to make lectures more interesting. There is an in-class assignment due at the end of each class, but they were super easy. The quizzes (4), coursework (10) and homework (4) were all easy and took less than 30 minutes to complete. Easy grader, just a long lecture to get through. Everything is open note.

This class was easy and the only required work was occasionally homework and In Class Activities for attendance (but those can be done outside of class during the class period). Prof. Hernandez was nice, but canceled class a few times. No tests or finals, only open note quizzes.

This was a super chill class, he canceled lectures a lot so check your email before heading to class. There wasn't a lot of homework or assignments that went along with the class. Overall, super easy ISP credit and Osvaldo is a great guy.

Ozzy was a cool professor ti have this semester. Although he did cancel a lot, the assignments and tests were not that difficult and was easy to complete. ULA was also very accessible when needed. Recommend taking this class as it is very interesting, you just have to like lectures as it is very lecture heavy material.

I loved Ozzy last year when I had him for 203A but in a lab setting he's kinda tough. Like all labs, attendance is mandatory which is expected. One thing I hated is he would keep us in lab even when we didn't need to stay the whole time. 2 assignments due at the start of every lab, pre and post lab. Boring and one huge final project at the end.

reviews.comment: very easy credit for isp. hernandez is a very interesting person but unfortunately his lectures are boring. attendance is technically mandatory because of daily assignments you have to turn in, but you totally can turn them in online without stepping foot in the lecture hall.

He is an easy professor for an ISP requirement. He does have easy homework once a week and four easy online quizzes. He uses an in-class activity for attendance (but can drop 3), posts lecture slides, and cares about his students.
Light work

He is a great professor and thoroughly explains topics. Uses picture-heavy slides and counts participation through in-class assignments that can easily be done outside of class but are due at the end of class. Overall, homework and coursework are easy (look at a graph and interpret or watch a documentary), as are tests which are online open note.

reviews.comment: I did not appreciate how many days he took off along with how he announced quizzes. He would hardly announce them and made the final due at a different time than the rest of the quizzes. I went to his class more times than I can count, and he didn't have class. he also didn't respond to emails. Other than his miscommunication, he was nice.

The class was canceled a lot, which made it hard to do some of the quizzes. Quizzes are not worth a lot, HW is easy but, with documentaries, and Coursework is easy. In-class assignments can be done outside of class and lectures are long. I did learn a lot about water and climate change that has stuck with me!

class was cancelled often due to personal reasons but the work he would assign (if any) was always easy. attendance is taken through in-class activities and 6 are dropped at the end of the semester. lectures get boring, but if you show up some of the information gets through and the exams are 15-question quizzes on d2l
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Hernandez is a nice person, but his execution of teaching kind of fell flat. He canceled class a lot, meaning we had less time to learn things that he would still keep on the quizzes. The courseworks are easy, but the homeworks often require watching lengthy videos. I don't think attendance is mandatory, just go through the lecture slides.

He's a great guy who is very passionate about what he teaches. He cancelled class a number of times, and the class has a low work load with relatively easy quizzes and coursework each week. No exams. Only bad thing is lectures can get boring sometimes.
Great professor and an easy grader. Not many assignments to complete and no exams, only a few at home quizzes throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All around great professor. Grade is mainly based on very short homework assignments and in class activities. Classes can get boring at times but that is heavily due to the content and not his teaching. Class was cancelled a lot but that was due to personal reasons, and he still made sure everything we needed was accessible online. Easy 4.0.

Professor Hernandez was great this semester. He canceled class a lot due to personal reasons but he always provided lecture videos or homework assignments in place of the canceled classes. There are very few quizzes or tests in this class; your grade consists mostly of homework and in class activities. Both of these were very easy to complete.

He was a great professor and he was very understanding for our course. The only thing that people probably don't like is that he dos in class activities which you have to be in class to get credit for. But don't let that discourage you from taking him because he is a great professor.

His lectures were very boring and hard to understand at times, as he did not thoroughly explain the material. He also cancelled class several times throughout the semester; however, he did give freebies. The material in the lectures, were not always what is covered in the quizzes. Be sure to complete all assignments so quiz scores wont affect grade

Really chill professor. You can tell he loves what he teaches. He had us do in-class, paper assignments every day. He also frequently canceled lecture. Even with taking a previous environmental science class, still recommend paying attention in lecture, a lot of what he says will be mentioned on the quizzes.

Not only was Professor Os super sweet and funny, but his class was also super easy. You really don't need to take notes, you just have to do the simple in-class activities every lecture. The majority of this course is super interesting and inspiring. He is super passionate and he is flexible if you just communicate with him.

One of the best classes for your ISP requirement. Overall an easy 4.0. Attendance matters but lecture slides are always posted so at least missing class wouldn't put you behind for tests or assignments. HW was weekly, but easy and not time consuming. Few tests which were all online, and no midterm or final, which made the class a lot less stressful

He was okay! Very easy going professor the only thing that would that annoyed me was the fact that he didn't answer his emails and get in real contact with him I had to stay after class and literally chase him down. He was specific on attendance. Had him during the winter semester and even when we had a really bad snowstorm he didn't cancel.

Prof. Hernandez is a super easy grader and gives out a few assignments. You have to do a short in-class activity and then 5 homework assignments and 5 quizzes for the whole semester. Definitely would recommend to fulfill your ISP requirement.

Professor H is a gem. We only had 5 homework assignments and 5 quizzes the whole semester and they were all easy. Nicest guy you will ever meet, cancelled lecture a few times. Super cool guy, almost threw us a zoom pizza party.

Dr. H is such a cool prof! Although he is a tad disorganized, it doesn't take away from his passion for teaching. The class covers very basic high school-level earth science, and he makes even that interesting to learn about. He also applies the concepts to environmental issues in our society, making the course material be helpful in the long run.

Prof. Hernandez is clearly passionate about what he teaches, but I did not find the material or the way in which he presented it to be accessible. Gave in-class coursework and the slides are not much help to look at without showing up to lecture, so go up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Hernandez is a difficult prof to deal with. Does not make accommodations for legitimate reasons and is extremely difficult to get in touch with. Says attendance isn't mandatory but as 20% of your grade is in-class assignments (that he won't allow make ups) your grade will suffer. His tests are very difficult and study guides unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hernandez is very passionate about this class and makes learning about bugs and the environment fun for people who may not have any interest in it. Attendance isn't necessarily mandatory, but most class points are based on the labs we do in class. He makes it very easy to be successful in this class and he's also super funny!!
Awesome, caring guy that truly gives students all the resources they need to do well in his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I had a great pleasure taking an online course with Mr. Hernandez! The course was very organized and if I did have any questions, would get back to me the same day!! Awesome instructor and would advise to take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is passionate about the subjects he covers in class, but his slides are extremely confusing, so you have to go to class and pay attention because there is almost never actual writing on them, just diagrams and graphs. He is a nice guy, but I have never struggled this much in a university requirement. Extremely hard and brought my GPA down a lot.

You think that you understand the material, you study the study guides he gives you, then you get the exam and are mind blown because it is nothing like you expected! Super hard exams that is for sure. Really boring lectures, too. Randomly gives in class work for credit so you should definitely go to lecture.
lectures are really easy, posts slides online, attendance not mandatory but sometimes there is in-class activities that we hand in, exams are really easy
He was a cool professor. The lectures could get kind of long and boring, but he was passionate about it which helped. His exams were kind of hard, but he always curved them.

He's really a cool dude. If you show up and pay attention you'll not only pass the class but learn a ton about the course. This class provides some real analysis of the real problems we face and he does a great job at addressing them.

Hernandez is a great lecturer who is really knowledgable about the topic and very passionate about what he teaches.  He gives difficult tests but if you thoroughly prepare you shouldn't have a problem- just make sure you remember specifics and be aware that he likes to trick people on exams.  If you want an easy class take someone else, though!

Prof. Hernandez is a nice guy and he's enthusiastic enough about material, but his tests are pretty challenging. That being said, he provides study guides for them, so it's up to you to prepare yourself. Also, during most lectures he has you turn in something to give participation points, so attend lecture! No textbook, which is a plus!

There's no textbook; all the power points were online. With that said, you still had to drag yourself to class and listen to his hour and a half lecture because about 2/3s of the time he'll have an in class assignment (basically attendance points). The material itself isn't hard, just a boring class to go to and felt like it wasted a lot of time.
Was helpful and really wants student participation. Puts PowerPoints online but goes through them too fast in class.

Good professor and interesting course. There was no textbook because the class was new, readings posted online. Good about questions but very limited office hours, go to TA for help on assignments. Attendance is checked by turning in answers to questions from lecture, so make sure you show up because it's random.

Professor is nice but boring and too much HW. Relies on TA too much, and the TA is not good, I think his name was Jeremiah. Very complicated grading system and he calculated grades wrong. I got a 4.0 but he calculated my grade as a 3.5 and I had to email him for weeks to fix my grade and he seemed very annoyed that I was pointing out his mistake
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just do the homework and practice exams. Everything is pretty straightforward.
Class was easy if you come and pay attention, which you have to.

I didn't really pay attention but still ended with a 4.0. Kind of odd grading scale but do the practice exams and they're super similar to exams. All quiz and exam content comes from lecture slides so read those carefully/watch lecture videos to study
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just do the practice exam like 20 times and you'll do well. I know that may seem odd but I rarely paid attention in class but I did each one like 15-20 times and averaged an 85 on all my exams.
He really wants everyone to do well, which I respected.
pretty good.

reviews.comment: Really cares that students do well. I almost missed the midterm and he emailed me to remind me to come!
Really engaging lectures I learned so much

Fantastic dude, super interesting lectures. Could be difficult if you aren't well acquainted with econ topics but there is a pretty generous curve and a lot of practice materials to work with for the class.

While you will have a 20-question quiz and 30 questions of homework a week, he explains everything very well in class. If you pay attention, it is a pretty easy class and he is willing to meet and help if you need it. While leactures can go over a lot he does a good job explaining it all in a way that kept me engaged.
he's a good guy but he makes his class so much harder than what it has to be. nice grade curve though (because of how hard he makes everything)

Not a bad professor. The professor himself is nice but the TA of the class is the worst TA I've ever met in any course. If u take this course and the same guy is ur TA DONT take the class. Awful class. For 98% of people it is a required class that is so obnoxiously hard. Seems like a good guy who teaches his class very harshly. Nothing in this class is meant to help you achieve a good grade within reason, and that is wrong given the current student workload.

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had. Lectures are insanely boring, you can't miss a single class for attendance or iclicker questions and there is an abnormal amount of homework and quizzes. The lecture slides are incomplete and so confusing, and the questions on hw are unnecessarily hard. Seems like a nice guy, but bad professor

I really enjoyed Professor Ziv's class. While the lectures were sometimes dense, he always took time to answer student questions clearly. When I couldn't stay after class, he responded to my emails within 24 hours with helpful explanations, showing his dedication to student success.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was overall fine at teaching the concepts of the class, but the class was really poorly organized. He relied way too heavily on his TAs to do everything, and it led to slow grades, assignments being assigned to the wrong dates constantly, and multiple other problems. His grading system is also horrible and convoluted. Definitely a mixed bag.

Oren Ziv is one of the worst professors I have ever had, to the point where I don't even think he wants to teach. His lectures are disorganized, messy, and useless. He makes his TAs Ziv do all of the work, and as a result, grades and any feedback are slow to come out. Oren ziv is not eager to help and overall has a horrible attitude. Do not take.

The class is easy and he's just funny to listen to in general. It seems like he's always about to make a joke about something. If you do the homework and do well on the quizzes it should be workable 4.0.

Can raise your final grade depending on your circumstances.

At the beginning of the semester he would ask iclicker questions off the top of his head, confusing himself and the class as a whole. He uses pictures of graphs from textbooks and does a poor job of giving context for their use of variables. Lots of self teaching. If you do the homework the tests aren't hard, just confusing.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Truley cares about the students. Has thought provoking assignments and interesting field trips. Lectures can be mundane, but they rarely are and take up a small portion of the class. Could not recommend his class enough.

Dr Thompson is an incredible professor. His lectures are super interesting, and his assignments and field trips are really fun and interactive. He is also extremely understanding and cares about the well being of his students above all, and is just an amazing instructor overall. I would 100% take this class again!

This is a very paper heavy class, but he gives really thorough feedback on everything. Very cool guy that wants you to pass his class. He took us on a few cool field trips too, since we went to the zoo and the beef cattle center.

This was without a doubt the best teacher/professor I've ever had in my whole life. he relates well with students, cares about what he's teaching, and prides himself on his class doing well with how much support he offers. I highly recommend.
Prof. Thompson is a great professor. He is very understanding and helps with essays/understanding concepts whenever needed. I would recommend taking any course with him.

Best professor Ive had at MSU yet. Take his class, you'll find no other HPS prof better. His class was always so interesting, projects were so fun and overall a really good experience. He is always there to support you, he is very caring and will always provide feedback, respects and considers everyones throughs/opinions. GREAT prof.

Amazing professor, very passionate about what he does. Very understanding, he cares about students, understands that people have different struggles. Very good feedback, fast grader, I highly recommend.

reviews.comment: Clearly cares about his students and what everyone to do well in his course. He is willing to give you feedback on your papers before you submit them and isn't a tough grader. As long as you show up to class, you will get a good grade. He also makes class fun.

Dr. Thompson was an amazing professor! He is very passionate about what he teaches. He is also very accommodating when it comes to deadlines. He found fun ways to present the material and made the class very enjoyable and provided great feedback on essays and such.

Professor Thompson is always understanding and easygoing. His class is also a lot of voluntary participation, it will get you thinking. You can tell he really has a passion for his field as well. I don't usually like history, but I didn't mind his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Peter Thompson is such a great professor. He made the class very engaging, especially since this class is not my field of expertise. Long and short readings are required before class, but the overall workload is very manageable.

reviews.comment: Professor Thompson is a great teacher, and cares a lot about his students. He does very well at accommodating to students, and if you participate in class, you will enjoy it. i took pls120 and she was great! she's an attorney herself! attendance is mandatory!!! there's lots of reading + case briefs at first but you get used to them. 2 exams and a group project you have to ask and answer questions on. she lets you use notes on exams but they are handwritten so i had to rush a bit. highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved everything about this class except for the format of the exams. I ran out of time on all three exams because they were handwritten and were based on dense prompts. LOVED this class. At the start of the semester it was very daunting but once you understand the formula of how to write for her class you will be set. Very kind and knowledgeable professor, I will take another class with her in a heartbeat. This class is supposed to act as law school prep, so keep that in mind when considering taking 321.

Professor O'Shea is an amazing professor. She is so passionate about law and really understands what she is teaching. reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor and you can tell she cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Workload was heavy on reading, which is expected, but was never too overwhelming.

reviews.comment: Professor O'shea is an amazing professor and clearly knows a lot about the material she teaches. Professor O'Shea is excellent at what she teaches, and has only heightened my interest in Political Science. You do have to attend class to 4.0, but the lectures and materials are directly what will be on the midterms, for which are both open note. Highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Melissa O'shea is a great professor that truly cares about her students. She encourages you to reach out if you have any questions at all. Attendance is mandatory to 4.0 the class. This is an easy class, it is NOT a political science class. It is strictly law. She is a fair grader and its easy to pass the class. No one assignment will deck your grade. She is dramatic but it is an easy class to pass. You don't have to go to class but I would recommend it.

She has 2 tests, both of which were open written note, a final paper and a group project where she allows you to report group members who slack. She will not extend deadlines however.
I enjoyed this class but you need to come to all the classes. Both of the exams were open-note. You have to read a lot of cases in the beginning of the semester but you can just skim.

Professor O'shea is one of the funniest and most insightful professors I've encountered. It is evident how much she cares for her students and their understanding of the content. While attendance is mandatory, her engaging nature makes showing up to lecture worth it. If you are considering law school, I would 100% recommend taking a course with her

Professor O'shea's wit and sense of personality she includes in her lectures makes it worth showing up. While there is a fair amount of reading and homework, none of it is tedious. It is evident how much she truly listens to students needs and cares about their opinions. Attendance and effort is required, but her aim isn't to make you fail.

Professor O'shea is very knowledgeable and cares that students understand the content. Definitely my favorite class and favorite professor. This class was not only interesting but also gave me the foundations I need for law.
O'Shea is goated. If you are looking to go to law school take as many courses with her as possible. Not much more to say other than that.

Professor O'Shea is a great professor and she really knows what she is talking about. Her teaching style ensure that by the end of the class, you will have learned a lot about the Judicial Process. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

Professor O'Shea was an amazing Professor and Mentor for me at Michigan State. I took four classes with her and she was great every time. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

Professor OShea does challenge her students, but if you put in the effort the class shouldnt be too bad. Her class is one I always enjoy going. It is entertaining and very valuable for prelaw students. I would definitely take her class again.

O'Shea is nothing short of fantastic professor for MSU law. However, I did take a very difficult class for her and it is very easy to slip up with the material or miss points more often than not. Prof O'Shea was amazing! Very straightforward about expectations. Over the course of the semester, we had 6 case briefs, 1 majority opinion to write, and three exams. Professor Arnold is awesome! The class is well structured, and Professor Arnold gives very thoughtful feedback on assignments. I would definitely recommend this class to others.
Great person! Really cares and loves hearing your ideas. Interested in your work and always opened to talk.

Amazing amazing amazing. Super down to earth and relatable to students. Understanding of missing class and gives opportunities to make up points. Big project at the end of the course/throughout but I really enjoyed working on it

Professor Arnolds class was amazing. I felt that the material was good and easy to understand, and they were extremely understanding for every single assignment that there was. There were also no exams! Overall I really liked this class.

Pat is the sweetest professor I've ever had. They clearly want all of their students to succeed and make it a point to get to know every student individually. It's very easy to 4.0 their classes as long as you complete your assignments!

Prof Arnold is easily the best professor I've ever had at MSU. So knowledgeable, welcoming, caring. Everything you could ask for. very kind and understanding. easy assignments

Pat is a wonderful and easygoing instructor. They only have a few assignments per week that are based off of the assigned readings. Attendance can be made up each week by doing an extra assignment. They are also very helpful and their lectures are super interesting.

Pat is an amazing professor. He is a really nice professor and doesn't assign any quizzes or exams. The modules he assigned had really interesting videos and articles. He gives lots of extra credit during class.

easy and super interesting class that only meets once a week. Just gotta go to class and raise your hand 6 times in a semester for full participation so easy again. Easy homework (quizzes) and midterm/final assignments.

Save yourself the trouble and take another class.

Read the weekly course material and participate in class- the course is easy. People love to complain about everything. If you put effort into the essay portion of quiz you'll earn extra credit; I had no problems. 

I recommend this class to anyone genuinely interested in East Asia, b/c I enjoyed the material she provided. The lectures are boring.

Just save yourself the trouble, pick a different class.
