Although he is a decent professor and very passionate about this class, the class is very tough. He purposely makes his exams extremely hard because he wants you to learn the material that he briefly covers in class in great depth. Also he expects you to do 8 hours of homework or studying per lecture which is not even possible to accomplish.

Honestly I don't know why he has such bad reviews. This class is not impossible. I study the night before each exam and I am going to most likely 3.5 or 4.0. I put in minimal work this semester. Marty is a GREAT professor, one of the best I have had. You can tell he really loves what he is talking about and it's scary how smart he is.

He's very smart and I love listening to his lectures because I have learned so much. It's just hard to juggle everything because his exams are tough. He tries to help though and posts the lectures and recordings online. He's a cool guy, it's just a lot of info all at once. I'm glad I got to take the class still.

Easily one of the worst classes I have ever taken. I came into the class the first day and he seemed like a cool professor, turns out he was terrible. He makes the tests almost impossible to pass, and in class he just reads the powerpoint without explaining the concepts. Would never take one of his classes ever again.

Terrible. hardest class you will take, not due to the material but due to his goal to fail his students. HE stated he was happy w/ the performance of our class after a 58% class average. The man designs the exams for you to fail, he admits he puts little thought into his tests which is why only he would be able to answer the question correctly.

I love biology so I thought this class would be easy. I was wrong. I was taking 3 other classes and working 2 jobs and I didn't have extra time for this. He gives quizzes on days when you don't have class, regardless of your schedule. His tests are impossible - I studied three weeks for every minute I wasn't occupied and I only scored a 70%.

I am taking 15 credits, working, and also volunteering. I do not have time to spend 3 hours a night studying for this class. He says his exams aren't hard but then makes them incredibly difficult. Class averages are about 50%. His extra credit he gives for attendance to make his averages look good is the only thing keeping me afloat.

This class is hard as hell but hear me out. He makes you understand the material to do well. I got a 67% on the first exam and then I did what he said and got an 86% on the next one. You will have put a ridiculous amount of work in to do well but its possible. Take easier classes the semester  you take this, you will not have time for other classes

First, during the lecture the professor goes off on tangents much too frequently, and then will breeze over slides to try and make up for lost time. Secondly, his exams are poorly written. For the first exam he told us that he wrote the exam the night before. Thirdly, you will not get a study guide until the night before the exam. Prepare to study.

I thought I was smart, then I took a class taught by this guy. Unless you have three hours a night to spend studying for his class don't take it. Seriously, I'm an honors college student and I'll be lucky to get a 3.0 in this class. Emphasis on LUCKY. Do yourself a solid and avoid this professor.

I liked his take not crap attitude.  He would call out students that are disrupting the class.  He explained everything well and was easy to follow along with.  He was always available to students if they needed help.  However his exams were incredible hard.  He would test us on the smallest of topics that he barley covered.  Expect to study a lot.

Well the exams are incredibly difficult, even after spending countless hours reading and UNDERSTANDING the concepts. I took this while also taking organic chemistry and the orgo was easier. He adds points to everybody's exam, which sounds great but it fluffs up the average so that he looks like he's a really good instructor, but he isn't.

His tests are ridiculously hard and the questions always have more than one right answer. Even after relistening to levitates and rewriting notes, I found that the exams usually cover stuff that isn't emphasised in class. He also claims that he'll never test you on something that isn't mentioned in class or on a PowerPoint - it's a lie.
Hard class. He does not have a pleasant attitude at times.

Talks very fast and the tests are extremely hard. I took three years of biology in high school and struggled to get a 3.5 in this class. He really does know what he's talking about and he mostly tells you what will be on the test.

There was far too much work in the class for what it was. Especially since daily attendance is done as an assignment, it gets to be excessive. She was nice, however, I found the lectures to be quite long and drag on, especially when covering more dense topics. The work isn't hard, it's just busy work, making it more annoying than anything else.

Took this class because I was interested in URP as a major, ended up realizing I cant do it if each class has this much work. I had more work than any of my other classes, and the lectures are so long and draining and she lectures the ENTIRE time. Projects are very tedious and take a lot of energy. She is a nice prof, but I have other work too.

reviews.comment: Took for my major, I really enjoyed the class, but I was already interested in the class material. Not a whole lot of reading and assignments are fairly simple and straight forward. Attendance is mandatory, very easy group assignments will be given every class period and count towards attendance. Exams are fairly easy if you study.

For starters, if you don't wanna talk about urban planning then don't take this class. Every lecture is paired with a discussion assignment. If you do like talking about urban planning then you'll have a great time. She's super knowledgeable and very open to questions. Was a shame so much was online due to her health.

First of all this class is a waste of money. Dr. Morckel is a joke and shouldn't be taken seriously. Her voice is like nails on a chalk board and induces head aches. Took this class for an easy 4. and it ended up having a heavier work load then all my other classes. SAVE YOUR MONEY!

Great professor, readily engages with students and very understanding. She lectures a LOT so be aware of that, but she uploads the slides after every class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she says a lot of stuff during class that isn't on the slides. Assignments and exams were easy overall, make sure to pay attention to court case names.

reviews.comment: Bill is a very good teacher for film, as you can tell, he cares deeply about the industry and his students. Isn't especially technologically savvy, so keep that in mind. Would recommend.

reviews.comment: Loved taking FLM 355 with bill. He is hilarious and great to work with. He takes everyone's opinions into consideration, but isn't afraid to debate you on your film takes. He was an easy grader for this course, so as long as you turned something thoughtful in you receive a good grade. Bill is a legend, I would recommend taking his class.
Seriously wish I would have looked him up on here before I took his class. Terrible structure and too harsh for what is supposed to be an intro class.

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had. Gives no instruction as to what the assignments entail, and the syllabus is literally half a page long. He puts barely any work into the course but expects the opposite from his student. He also plays favorites and your grade matters more about his opinion of you rather than the work.
Worst Professor ever.

As a person, I really liked him and thought he was funny, but as a teacher? This man had me going through it. The quiz + exam questions can be really vague, and when it comes to essays, he'll critique things that you didn't know about. I honestly enjoyed the class a lot, but I would recommend a different professor.

He rarely goes over what to expect on quizzes and exams, so be prepared to do a lot of work outside of class. He's a tough grader when it comes to essays and other written assignments. He's a nice man, just don't expect this class to be an easy 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I've had Bill for 3 different classes, that's how great they are. He's funny and an amazing professor with great stories to tell. His classes are pretty easy but to do well you have to show up, do the work and readings, and participate in the class. All his classes have been some of my favorite film classes. Would highly recommend.

Amazing teacher and a very easy class. A bit of reading but you can survive without doing it. No textbook. Great film selection. Lots of discussion time and very interesting lectures. Quizzes and papers are easy. Wants everyone to do well and will offer extra opportunities for that. Passionate about film, overall a very fun class to be a part of.

Amazing professor who is passionate about film and has so much knowledge on the topic. Has seen all the classics when they came out and has acted in a few films. Super funny and it's amazing to hear about his life with film. Attendance is necessary, but the class is easy. Rare homework, definitely could make it without the textbook.  He's awesome.

I've had Prof. Vincent for several film and humanities classes. His passion for film and the arts is unparalleled, as is his knowledge of those subjects.  His classes are somewhat of a haven for intellectual students and therefore a struggle for those use cell phones and video games for cognitive stimulation.

You either get what he is saying or you do not. His classes are not cookie cutter courses. He will want to see how much you are really paying attention, how involved you are or if you think you are just there because you thought it was going to be an easy 4.0. He can point you in the right direction. Effort  success.
What this guy said pretty much sums it up: "he is feast or famine. you'll either be friends with him and get awesome grades, or you'll be a regular student and just pass the class."
Your grade is based on how much he likes you, so play his games. If your class is small, he might invite you to his creepy, trashy house at the end of the semester.

I took him for screen writing and advanced screen writing.  He is one of the best profs at Michigan State.  He is much like the older father figures that you see in clichéd movies and books--a warm and friendly figure.  Just make sure to use proper grammar (it is possible your work will get stomped on during class--leaving the shame of footprints).
he is feast or famine.  you'll either be friends with him and get awesome grades, or you'll be a regular student and just pass the class.
No Comments

Bill is a great prof and knows his stuff. However, if he likes you, you'll get a better grade than if he doesn't. But, the more classes you take w/him, the more you'll consider him a friend than a prof.

He's pretty goofy, but very passionate about what he does.  His eccentricites alone make attending class a must.  As far as learning from him, yes, you can get a good chunk of screenwriting knowledge from him, but he's more about getting creative ideas flowing then boring "traditional" learning
No Comments
Enjoyable but boring.  Taught Sam Raimi way back when, never gets tired of talking about it.  Disrespects animation.  Otherwise decent.
I like his class structure, especially the individual conference where I usually receive very helpful feedback.

He seems super nice but he gives minimal criteria and zero guidance. His comments when grading an essay were “good” and that's it. He's nice but he doesn't teach you anything about writing and repeats himself a lot during the lecture.
He's easygoing, but more importantly, he's a truly original professor. I really appreciate his efforts to make the class engaging and the many creative ideas he brings.

Took his writing 101 course for this semester. He's a cool and super friendly teacher! Always willing to help you when you have questions. A lot of small homework but they only counted as the participation grade. 3 essay, 1 research paper, and 1 remix Video throughout the semester but they were really easy. Easy grader.

He does not use D2L in a user-friendly way; it is nearly impossible to find materials, and he does not enter grades into the grade book, so you have no idea what the grade is for the whole class. During the two-hour lectures, he talks in circles and often will pick on someone to read because he does not want to. He is very nice but not the best.

Very easy professor, has lots of online/no classes due to one-on-one zoom conferences after each project assigned. However, he often gives unclear and bad feedback. Is a very easy grader but does NOT put grades into the grade book at all. There is no way to see your grade on d2l, and he has extremely boring lectures. Take if you want a 4. though
The class can get boring, but he's a super sweet and understanding professor. There is homework, but it is really easy, and he's a really easy grader. I would recommend him as a professor

He's pretty straightforward with the assignments, He's really nice and understanding. If you're sick or anything and miss class he's flexible with that. He does have an accent which can sometimes make it hard to understand but he's so nice and is an easy grader.

reviews.comment: You do so many assignments and it doesn't go into the grade book, only the papers go into the grade book. reviews.comment: Amazing professor, very understanding. Do the work and its a guaranteed 4.0
Would take again

Avoid.
Unorganized and very unenthusiastic lecturer. Put zero effort into preparing for lectures and often made condescending remarks.
The best geometry professor ever.

Best experience ever
It is fun for this introduction course. I had zero background for statistics before taking this course and I was so confident now after taking it.

If you never coding before, then Prof xie will be the best person to let to getting start. I will absolutly recommend you to choose his class!

He is a great professor. Had him for Stt 441 two years ago. Really want students to succeed and is helpful in and outside of the classroom.
Great teacher

Professor Yuying Xie, XYY, Superman, Clark, or whatever you want to call him is (for me) definitely the best professor I have had at MSU. Good experience
Enjoyed

reviews.comment: You dont get to see your grade until the end. Theres no study guide. Only one question per lecture on exams which wouldn't be bad if we generally knew what from the lecture would be on the exam. Theres also around 5-6 pages of notes per lecture.

If you are looking at this thinking whether you should drop or not after a couple weeks of the class, do it.  Impossible 4.0 just look at msu grades fall 2024, spring 2025, and fall 2025 only 6 out of 138 students had a 4.0.  Tons of effort just to get a 3.5 and never put anything in so it was a mystery on what I was getting.

reviews.comment: He is the hardest grader in the entire world and he seems chill in class but is so hard and no one gets a good grade

reviews.comment: He was an amazing professor. I had him for my first semester freshman year and got scared from the other reviews but he is genuinely kind and cares about what he teaches. He also makes learning about what would normally be a boring subject fun.

reviews.comment: Even if you go to every lecture, I can't promise you will get a good grade. The exams are heavily weighted and are on specific details that you won't remember even if you take notes on everything. Good luck!

Had a paper due a month in, got it back the day of the final. Marked down for disagreeing with him. Took 6 emails to get 2 replies, but by then it was already 2+ weeks into summer break. Class was a joke; he just put on movies and watched with us. No test or exam guidance either. Good luck.

Professor Willis had an engaging course, but his grading and assignments took most of it away & made the rest of the course unenjoyable. reviews.comment: Very prideful and miserable professor and person in general. He talks down to his students in a manner that I have never seen before. He is blind to the concept of grace and should never be teaching a graduation requirement. I hope that he finds what he is missing in his life and doesn't take out his misery out on students. Don't take his classes.

Do not take, a 4.0 is basically unachievable, people take this course because they have to for the IAH credit not because they wan to, the prof makes it a pain to complete.

The absolute worst class I have taken. He grades you very harshly, will only put 10 questions on an exam! I just recently got a 1.75 on a paper. Its absolutely diabolical he thinks he has the power to pass out 2.0s like they are free candy IN A GEN-ED CLASS, he needs to lose his job immediately. Or teach at Harvard if he thinks he's that advanced.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Stuart is an interesting guy but a subpar professor. He does not put any grades on D2L which can be frustrating when most every other professor at MSU does. His "lectures" consist of watching content he did not make and then him "presenting" a rather long and pointless power point on what you just saw. A 4.0 is next to unachievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All the people rating him are so dramatic for no reason. Although his grading can be a little harsh it's honestly not that bad. He's a nice guy who gives entertaining lectures. The grading with the movie quizzes can be a little harsh but after the first 1 or 2 quizzes you should get the hang of it.

Little class work for grade help
Wont post lectures but says its ok to miss some
Content from optional lectures on quiz + exam
2hr lecture could take 20min
Spends lectures expressing broad content 
Broad paper prompts + confusing evidence searches
Most of lecture spent watching movies with specific + confusing quizzes
No grades in D2L
SAVE YOURSELF

reviews.comment: This man does not teach. This class is all movies in which I never went because it was a waste of my time. His exam questions are extremely specific and often difficult to understand. Speaking of difficult to understand, he also has a British accent and wears a mask which only makes it harder to listen and understand his lectures. Save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is bad at teaching and engaging. Poor communicator and writes bad lessons. The classes are mostly pointless to attend (I have attended all of them except for one). Unnecessarily harsh grading system as well. IAH 202 - Europe and the World is the hardest class that I am taking by a mile.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While he's a nice guy, I really learned very little in this course. Most of his lectures could have been condensed into maybe 20 minutes, but instead, they often lasted up to an hour. In addition, he always played a documentary for an hour after a lecture. He doesn't post any grades into D2L, and takes forever to grade papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ok, this professor was so great. If you actually want to learn something you are going to love this class. He was so great, but the class is pretty intense content-wise. There is a lot of reading and a significant research paper, but if you show up to class and do all the assignments you'll get at least a 3.5.

He assigns papers upon papers upon papers and he doesn't make the lecture slides available outside of class. He nit-picks every little things in your papers so that he doesn't have to give you a 4.0. The film quizzes are extremely specific and he will not give you credit unless you answer it exactly how he would want it. Worst professor ever.

Lectures are rushed and have no correlation to the overall objective of the course. Lectures are about small details , yet the quizzes are super short. No way to study, there's no guideline to see what you should know. The whole semester we had 2 assignments, 6 quizzes, 2 papers, and watched probably 20 boring and unrelated movies.

Only did 45 min of lecture and ended every single class with the most boring movies ever. Hard to learn, 2 required books & a 5 page essay. Also, he uses a mic and has a British accent and i don't know how but those two things make it really hard to hear/understand him.
Good instructor. However be prepared to have zero clue what your final grade is. even after the class d2L page closed I still have no clue.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course IAH 241C was not a bad course. Theres not physically much work, but when there is, you have to put lots of effort into getting a 3.5 or higher. Since theres not much course work to grade, it highly affects ones grade if you do bad. Some of the novels you must read can be boring at times, but you will survive. BEWARE OF MOVIE QUIZZES!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you enjoy your sanity, do not take this class. This professor did not always communicate when things were do. Tough grader and told us what he was looking for a month after assignment was due. Never skipped class because he never posted lectures on d2l. Made us calculate our own grades instead of learning the d2l system.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Willis made this class pretty fun. Most of the assignments were watching movies and answering a few questions. The final assignment was very enjoyable and some of the most fun I've had in school. I would definitely recommend him to anyone looking for a relaxed kicked back class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor is borderline unfair when it comes to learning online. His lack of communication and very unprofessional attitude makes this class a very tough one to get through. He expects us to watch films, read books, and taking part in discussion topics during each week. With his lack of communication he fails to be a successful teacher.

Dr. Willis expects way too much of students and is unforgiving. He assigns movies to watch every two days on top of two books, readings, lectures, and three research papers. His movie quizzes are unfair and incredibly difficult even if you watch the movies. His grading format is designed so that one bad grade could theoretically destroy you.

Dense. His "lectures" consist of poorly synchronized powerpoint slides and accompanying MP3s of him mumbling into his laptop microphone with no clear movement between slides. Easy to get lost. It's barely understandable, I had to turn bass as low as it could go just to hear his voice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It an easy class, but his accent makes lecture so boring.

Mr. Willis was a good professor. His lectures were interesting if you are interested in human history. I found that he was a fair grader, and that he would be loose with the particulars of his given assignments if you can demonstrate to him that you understand the content. If you express interest in the subject he will respect you, and help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting professor to say the least. Heavy British accent, could get very dull sometimes, but also pretty funny at times as well as well as very passionate about the subject. Most of the grade is based on a paper and the final, but neither is too difficult to score well on, as he gives a lot of leeway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Although lectures are boring they are far and few between most of the class is movies based - I never went to a class that had a movie in it (like 12 days during the semester) and I got a 3.5 in the class. Great professor and really funny as well.
If you read what he provides and watch the documentaries this class is easy. He wants you to pass, but he wont just give it to you. Also He has a British accent so his lectures are the worse.

Professor Willis is a good guy, but I would not recommend this course. You're only graded on a few difficult novel quizzes. The only exam you take is the final (40% of final grade), which is cumulative and not curved. Throughout the semester you watch dozens of movies and documentaries which are all tested on the final. Totally unrealistic
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: So hard, do not choose it!

I gained nothing but frustration. He is one of the worst professors, he is cold and impersonal. He is extremely opinionated and biased. The lectures were awful,he is not a good speaker and extremely long in length. This class was very expensive, huge disappoint.  Each test is extremely under timed. No time to read questions that are long paragraphs

By far one of the most isolated professors. Tests were extremely timed. Example 10 minutes to answer 8 questions, when it took minutes to read the paragraph long question to answer! Most of the time I had to read the questions so fast I missed what was being asked. The lectures were difficult to listen to as his mouth was full of saliva, ewww!!

I liked how he did multi-week labs so that we didn't have to show up every single week, however the tedious lab reports were killer depending on who your lab partner is. There were 7total labs, and 7 written lab reports. They weren't crazy challenging but definitely took time and got annoying fast.
Great lectures. Well prepared and knowledgeable

Best professor I have had for Physics at MSU. Xianglin is very enthusiastic while lecturing, easy to understand, and leaves you excited for the next lecture. Xianglin makes sure every student in his class understands the topics that are being covered. He also asks students questions about new content to further engage the class. Amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rens class was online for me, and it was probably one of my easiest classes. You are only graded on about 7-8 essays throughout the semester, thats it. I will say however, she didn't grade anything for me for about a month and a half. But overall it was a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Xuefei Ren class. She talks a lot about urbanism and how it's related to sociology. Lot's of interesting perspectives and readings.

The entire semester is only out of 100 points so you cant miss many. The only grades were 5 short essays and 2 exams. The grading scale is really generous. The essays are easy 100%s but the exams are not.
Great prof! Class based 70% on tests, but grading scale is great! (4.0 90%, 3.5 80%, etc)

Dr. Liang is very kind and flexible when it comes to deadlines, and her lectures really help with understanding the material. The class if very easy if you have any kind of stats background, however to get a 4.0, you need to score >95 overall, so be wary since the HW is graded on accuracy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors throughout college. She made the material easy to understand. Would highly recommend taking 808 with her.
Dr. Liang creates excellent notes that easy for us to understand.

Dr.Liang is awesome!
Her EPI 808 transformed my understanding of biostatistics and inspired me to dive deeper into the field.
While she wasn't a bad professor, she can be passive aggressive for no apparent reason on times and is very harsh at grading with no consistency.

I think she is okay. But she is not understanding. She gives so many assignments and there are so many group projects. Exams almost every week. Do your homework and make sure you understand the material and you should be okay. But she is not my favorite professor.

The lectures are pretty entertaining and help you learn and understand the language, but there is so much homework. At least 4, 10 to 30-minute assignments per week. You get a lot of time off class, but attendance matters in the end. The textbook is pretty expensive, so I would try to buy it second-hand. There are also a lot of group projects.

Professor Hao is an incredible professor. Her lectures are always fun and engaging and she always emphasizes the importance of trying instead of being afraid of getting answers wrong. Mandarin is a hard language, and you need to make a continued effort, but having a professor like Professor Hao makes the content entertaining and easy to understand.

Hao Lao Shi is an outgoing professor who gives straightforward and somewhat entertaining lectures. Getting a solid grade in the class is a little difficult and she does not have clear rubrics with grading. I would recommend giving her a try, however her teaching style does not fit me well.

Yiying Tong is easily a top tier professor at Michigan State University, East Lansing Campus. very helpful for all students, and has clear grading criteria. I would take him over Borzoo Bonakdarpour every day of the week. Inshallah Yiying.

Content wasn't too hard, the professor makes the exams multiple choice and on D2L in person. Only issue I had was that he was a little too slow for my liking, so I would often just go through the lecture slides at my own pace and tune him out. Other than that, gives great examples and makes it fairly easy to get a 4.0

One of the best professors at MSU! It's evident he is passionate about teaching and wants his students to learn and succeed. The 80 minute lectures sometimes got a bit stale, buts thats the only negative thing I can say about Yiying. Looking forward to taking his higher level CSE courses in the future. He's truly an injective (one-to-one) prof.

Was hesitant to take CSE 260 because I heard the other professor (Borzoo) ran a difficult class. I was relieved when after the first few days I realized prof. Tong was completely different. He had clear lectures, reasonable homework/tests, and was accessible outside of class. He's also the reason I bought a Wii to re-live some childhood nostalgia.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I often find myself struggling to stay awake in lecture. However, he's great at answering questions on piazza and explaining the content if you can get past the monotony of the content. I recommend buying the textbook for extra credit, as it'll give you more practice and more room to make mistakes on other assignments (this class is 60% exams).
Lectures are very long and boring. If you pay for the textbook, you are better off learning from that. Not a bad class, but could be much better.

Great professor. Everything about the class was meant to be difficult, but he taught it in a very intuitive way. Fair grading, and easy to score if you study. Helpful, responds to questions fast and effectively on Piazza. 

Inspirational. Also great at Wii Boxing.

Great professor. Everything about the class was meant to be difficult, but he taught it in a very intuitive way. Fair grading, and easy to score if you study. Helpful, responds to questions fast and effectively on Piaza. Textbook not required but is extra credit. 

Inspirational. Also great at Wii Boxing.

Made discrete math super easy to understand. Grading criteria was extremely clear. Also the recitations playing Wii play motion with Yiying were some of the best class memories I've had at MSU. Will never forget the time he cleared all the levels in Wii sports sword fighting… back to back!!

As an international student and a fellow East Asian, I must say that most Asian professors are not good enough. However, Professor Yiying Tong is an exception. He teaches with true ease and enthusiasm rather than being an extremely self-centered person. Lectures attendable online, exams are strict but fair and reasonable.

Amazing professor, lectures are only twice a week, with optional recitation. You can also join lectures online via zoom. homework is not difficult, and due every other week. He uses piazza to answer questions promptly. Book is not required, but purchasing it allows you to get 5% extra credit. Prof. Tong is also great at Mario Kart & Wii Party!

Had some of the best sleeps of my life in his class, with that said, his lecture is pretty boring with the boring material and his soft and slow tones. Everything else is great though, very smart and caring and he made the class as easy as possible despite the the boring class materials. Easy hw and extra credits, would recommend to anyone.
One of the best professors I've had. Very caring, smart, professor. Would 100% take again.

He is the best professor I have ever had. He made learning exactly how it should have been with this course without overly complicating things. He is also super responsive and understanding. Everybody should definitely take.

260 can be a difficult class, but Professor Tong is very caring and gives good responses on Piazza or in-person. The sample exams correlate pretty well as long as you do some decent studying. He also gives 5% extra credit if you buy the Connect book and do the homeworks. The only "bad" thing is that his lectures are often long and he goes fast.

it can be hard to concentrate during lectures, but the professor is very understanding and is always willing to answer questions. the lecture content comes from the online textbook, which you don't have to buy unless you want to complete it for extra credit. overall, the class is a little difficult, but the professor is willing to help you succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is an excellent professor, and although some students may find his lectures somewhat dull, he is always willing to answer questions and help students who need extra support. He is genuinely interested in his student's success and ensures they have the necessary resources to excel. He is one of the most caring professors in the CSE department.
He is very understanding and responds quickly to emails and piazza posts. He has practice exams and quizzes that are close to the actual exams and quizzes which helps a lot. Overall good professor.

His lectures were difficult to understand, especially with dealing with such complex material, but if you were to self learn and master the material, he has very lenient grading and even though the homework load is a handful, it is good practice for both the exams and practical knowledge. He handled the aftermath of the shooting very well.

The lectures were not great so be ready to self-learn and search for youtube lectures. Otherwise, the class was quite fair. The exams and quizzes were all based on previous material shown in class and nothing was surprising. Quite a bit of optional XC was available up to 5% of the total grade. And the homework is also fair and self-graded.

CSE260 is a foundation building course, and professor Tong succeeds in doing that. Annoyingly the book was on Connect and cost a decent bit of money, but it was solely for extra credit points - speaking of which, you won't need them. Lectures are not the greatest, but he'll respond to queries fast. I suggest reading the slides and self-learning.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As another user said, the professor was overall very solid.  Lectures were really slow and boring, but everything else was pretty good.  Was very fast to respond to questions and did a good job organizing the course and listening to students.  All in all a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is such a nice guy that listens to student feedback and adapts the class, but he sucks at lecturing. But god bless his review videos. That is were you will learn the material, cause in lectures good luck not sleeping.

Dont take this class alongside other demanding classes. Be very intentful and careful with your homeworks. The quizzes and tests will try to trick you, so please study hard. Read the book and the slides for maximum effect. For the tests make an amazing cheat sheet. Good enough cheat sheets wont work. Find someone to work/check stuff over with.
As long as you read the rubrics carefully, this class is quite simple! Exams were clear and straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fully online class with a few exams and mini projects. The mini-projects were graded strictly, so make sure to read the rubric thoroughly. Does not curve grades. Easy class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lectures were like 8 minutes and says to just read the textbook. Super specific test questions and make sense to the textbook or lectures. The projects are super easy and probably saved my grade. The honor's option was super weird, you have to get approval from a journal to post your writing. Given extra credit but not guaranteed the full points.

I loved this asynchronous course, it was very easy and well-organized. The prof is very chill and is not a strict grader. It is hard to miss an assignment since he sets clear due dates on the syllabus. Definitely one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Highly recommend!
Funny guy. Assignments online that require reading the textbook. Easy 4.0 if you do all the work. Exams are online so you can use notes!

This was an online class and it was so easy. If you do the assignments, you will pass with flying colors. My only criticism for Professor Kiuchi is that she did not engage with us students at all. I know it was online, but some check in emails would have been nice.
Easiest class I have ever taken at MSU. Literally show up you pass
Gives lots of extra credit opportunities, 3 open book tests, doesn't take attendance every day.

I liked the class. It's not an easy 4.0 but Dr Kiuchi will help you if you email him. Just put time into it. You listen to his lecture and do the assignments. You will get a good grade. If you have to take ISS, this is the class to take.

The class was good. Just put time into it. Instead of being in a classroom for 2 or 3 hours a week, you just listen to his lectures online and do assignments for a few hours a week. If you do the work he tells you to do, you will be fine.

I don't know why anyone is complaining about this professor. I took his IAH course over the summer online and it was the easiest thing. You do have to watch lectures that take time but the book reading isn't even necessary. I would buy the books though bc you will want to refer to them for writing assignments or for the exam. Put time in. Simple!
I think he is great. I enjoy the class.
Why the hell would he do 91% or above as a 4.0? why does he has to be so different than other professors? we are not UM. So lower the expectations and just let us have the 4.0.

I am taking his ISS course right now and it is the worst! I have to say something.We have so much reading to do every week and on top of that we have 2-3 online lectures to watch. He only opens it for 4 days. It sucks. I have a life and I don't want to sit there and read his crap all day long. One of the book is not even related to the course.
I was never clear on what he wanted written there is like 5 papers back to back every one has to be 5-6 pages ( take a different WRA class)
He helps you a lot. This is the best class you could take with WRA.

Really helpful. You will be a great writer after this class. It's a required class, but he makes it as fun as anyone could possibly do. If you work a lot, he will help you a lot. I got a sense he wants you to succeed but if you show him you're dedicated, he will help you even more. He's available face to face or email. He is great.
Horrible professor. He was never clear on his assignments, and not very helpful at all. Be prepared to write many papers, 4~6 pages each.

He's awesome! Very helpful class, informative and helps tremendously with writing papers. He's funny, (at least he is to me) and finds interesting was to incorporate class lessons with things like The Big Bang Theory, or other odd things MSU professors don't usually do. Very interesting class on Race, be ready to write like a pro once your done!
amazing
Great Professor
Great Professor Best ever
Best professor ever.
Pretty easy class, got a 4.0. Helps with papers a lot
So boring and the easiest information being explained over and over for hours

Dr. Yelinek is a lovely professor, and SOC 241 is such an easy course! Your grade is made up of (open-note) exams and in-class assignments, but both are super easy. She is a caring professor who facilitates interesting conversations throughout her lectures. I strongly recommend taking this course with Dr. Yelinek - it's an easy 4.0!

It's very easy to four point her class as there's only two things that the grades hinge upon: in class exercises and exams. Both are open note and pretty easy to complete. If you're not coming to class, make sure to have D2L open on your phone or computer at least twenty minutes before class ends!! Lots of discussions but they aren't enforced.

This class was really easy but mandatory attendance (in class assignments and sign in sheet). There are no tests or finals, but one group project which is a presentation. Professor Yelinek is really nice but also lowk a talker and class always goes the whole time.

Amazing professor that presents the information in a way that makes it easy to understand. In class activities are randomly at the end of class and cannot be made up, so thats kinda an attendance aspect of the class. No homework, 5 total quizzes that are open note and not in class. Honors option is a very short in-class presentation - do it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice, and she knows what she is talking about. However, she talks for so long that time gets away from her and you will go over the end time for the class. That is really my only issue with her but this is an easy class where you do learn a lot from it.
I absolutely loved Dr. Yelinek! She is such an empathetic and warm individual, and her lectures are very engaging and thought provoking.

Dr. Yelinek was great and I really enjoyed her lectures. Just come to class as in-class quizzes are a good chunk of your grade (but they are super simple and based on the lecture you just listened to). Quizzes were online and you didn't have to come to class for them. Just go to class and you should do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelinek is extremely kind. No homework, quizzes online and not taken in class and open note. There is a book you're supposed to buy but you can pass without it. Attendance not mandatory but I would recommend coming because sometimes she has mini pop quizzes at the end of class.

Great teacher but often talks specifically about my culture (and no others usually) as highly conservative and dogmatic. As an atheist and the only person from that ethnicity in class I felt it erased my experience and made it seem like I have to represent my ethnicity/a religion i don't even believe in instead of just be a student in class.

Second class I've taken from this Professor. Quizzes are straight forward and slides were uploaded to D2L. Occasionally short, open note quizzes at the end of the class. Highly recommend if you need an easier but still interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelinek is very nice, but attendance is very mandatory and her rubrics and assignment guidelines were pretty unclear. Lectures sometimes got out early and were very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelinek seems strict but just values attendance (don't take if you can't attend classes; expect brief in-class quizzes). All exams were online, remote, and open note, but were, in my opinion, ill-timed (very brief). Lectures were a bit repetitive, but exams reflected the slides and in-class quizzes. Free online textbook.
Started off by saying she didn't believe in race. Would mark you absent even if you were there and had proof, if you had evidence of you being sick she still wouldn't care.

Already signed up to take her course next sem. Very understanding and very caring. Topics are interesting which made me participate in class willingly (and she never calls on students who don't have their hand up). Also is considerate about poor weather conditions.

Her guidelines were very unclear, and she would post conflicting guidelines for the same assignment, making it confusing what was expected. She takes an unreasonably long time to grade assignments, making it nearly impossible to know what your grade currently is. The lectures are boring and long. There were a couple of interesting assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Super easy 4.0 class. NO EXAMS - only open note quizzes (no class on those days). No homework & no projects!

Random "in class exercises" which is a short, opennote quiz at the end of class that usually has a 10 minute timer. They can not be made up and none are dropped. Sit next to the same people since we always turn and talk.

This is okay if you're taking it as an elective. If this is something you actually care about I wouldn't recommend it with this professor. She seems nice, the lectures are just so unengaging and a bore to sit through. She shows a lot of old clips from youtube and TED talks rather than explaining material herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is easy, but lectures are painful. Constant clips of outdated TED talks and other BS. Nothing too thought-provoking if you actually want to learn something. I feel like this is what the entire SOC department at MSU has become.

personally, i loved this course. exams were online, open note and typically ?s were pulled right from her slides. she does just read off slides but we also have a lot of class discussions which i enjoyed. attendance assignments are random. i took this as an elective and it was a simple 4.0 if you show up.

She uses slides made by the textbook and just turns around and reads straight from them. No expanding or teaching. She also likes to bring up politics here and there which is off-putting for some. Overall she is a very nice person but not a great teacher.

Too easy and boring for a 300-level class. Learned nothing, and Prof Yelinek clearly doesn't want to be there. Most days, we just watched videos/ movies, and random others took over teaching. If you need an easy elective, take it I guess, but if you're a soc major, you will be bored to death and have wasted your money. DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK.

Very insistent on class participation and didn't excuse the absence of students in a gas leak until people complained to higher ups about being unable to commute to class. Was very rude about her attendance policy and didn't let students do the attendance quiz while they got ready or were walking out the door. Also no sick policy without note
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was not a fan of the way this class was formatted. If you plan on not attending-- you will not pass. I also stopped using the text after the 4/5 week... She will not excuse you (despite what the syllabus says). I know a student had to come to class with a positive covid test. It was hard to talk to her as well, it was draining. Super easy though.

I took this as an elective and loved Professor Yelinek. She is so caring and considerate. Attendance isnt mandatory, but she would do random VERY easy quizzes in class that if you missed you could not retake. She had quizzes after each topic and they were decently lengthy, but easy open-note and taken from home with no class those days (amazing.).

Attendance is VERY mandatory. Sign in sheet at every class. A good chunk of the work is done in trios You all get the same grade regardless of what portions you do and what portions your partners do. Choice of a presentation or a paper as a final. Rarely answers emails. Is mostly understanding of personal events. Rubrics could be clearer.

I did not like this professor. The quizzes were online but she got crazy about attendance. She gave multiple students 0 on the in class participation even if they were in class. Not very good professionalism. All her lecture slides were posted on d2l and in class all she did was read off the slides so it was kind of pointless to go

Dr. Yelinek is a wonderful person, but her teaching style is not my forte. Attendance is overdone; she made a student come to class with covid (even with proof) for attendance points. I didn't use the textbook after like the 4th week, class can be 4.0-ed with your eyes closed. Not a lot of work, hardest part is the attendance for sure

This class is fairly easy. Classes are lectures, but all lecture notes are online. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she does do random in class assignments that are worth points. There are 5 open note, online quizzes and no exams. She also gave us a extra credit quiz at the end of the semester for up to 70 bonus points (which is a lot).

class was easy, tests were all online. Yelinek is crazy about attendance. I showed up to every lecture and completed her attendance checks on d2L. More than once she changed my grade to 0 and claimed that I wasn't in class and wouldn't change it back unless I emailed her multiple times. She is not professional AT ALL.

Don't take this class if you genuinely want to be taught the material, every week a different group has to give you a presentation where nobody actually retains or feels interested in. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not a hard class only a handful of simulations and homework. 4 exams all reasonable

overall, not a good professor. This class was extremely unnecessary. All the exams could be found on quizlet. And the hw and simulations were pointless. Good luck getting into contact with him if you are experiencing difficulties with assignments, as he does not respond.

This is one of the best professors in the world. I have never seen someone who pushes you work for everything. Dr. A you are the best teacher ever and I will never forget you. The ones who were talking smack about you were obviously lazy in class and want an easy A.

Great professor, doesn't take bull.  You will work hard so if you are looking for an easy class don't take it.  But if you are looking for a class that challenges your perspective and helps you become an independent thinker than I recommend her.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS! You will spend more time working on her assignments week by week than compared to the rest of your classes combined.  She grades unfairly and displays favoritism amoung students.
Debrenna teaches a challenging course and she is quite willing to help.
Doesn't grade fairly and fosters negativity. Students don't count.

Diversity specialization is biased and outdated and doesn't take into account the needs of many select groups and populations.  Attention is given to double standard producing outcomes when important reality focused viewpoints are disregarded.
She good
Dr. A is fantastic.  I can't think of one bad thing to say. Best class/proff here at MSU. If you can, take her class. Your ideas will be challenged and you will learn so much.  AMAZING!
Dr.A is a very kind and good woman who loves her students and tries her best to relate to everyone. She is helpful and willing to work with students when needed.
Believes her lens of the world is the only one.  Seemed to single out students at times and not in a good way. Not as openminded as she believes.
Don't take this class unless you want to enter hell

The lectures are hard to understand and terribly organized. The quizzes are extremely confusing, but exams are better because the TA's write them. There is no homework, only quizzes and exams. The class is unnecessarily difficult and stressful.

The entire course grade is based on quizzes and two exams. It's unrealistic what you're expected to memorize. You don't get missed quiz answers back to study. The lectures teach you nothing you'll have to do most of the learning on your own. The syllabus states 1% per absence will be deducted from your final grade. Don't take unless you have to.

Much more tolerable than co-professor. Would have had much fewer issues with this class if she had taught more of the lectures. Actually graded assignments as if we were college students, rather than individuals with Ph.D's- gave clear grading criteria. Overall a caring professor; however, course lacked a central theme which overall made difficult.

Made this class tolerable for me. Much better communicator, and much better at working through content with students, than Professor Craig. Easier grader, with much better communicated expectations on the work she graded.
Very nice, caring, and a great grader with gives amazing feedback on papers.

Being only an assistant prof. she sure does the bulk of the work for this class. She's very caring and wants you to do well. Makes things easy to understand and how they grade things(even though it is EXTREMELY hard for an intro course). It is guest prof. lectures with short exam responses. She is the reason I let alone passed this, main prof. bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The main professor for this class Dr. Craig is terrible. She does the majority of the work for being an assistant professor, genuinely cares about her students and their grades. super super easy to reach and always very kind and helpful.

Dr. Bennett was great in FW181! She was very easy to contact and schedule meetings with if you were confused on the content, and helped me get a great grade on my final paper and gave awesome feedback! She is one of the best teachers I've ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: MC 111 with Professor Ahlquist is amazing! The class focuses on writing about conservation and the environment. His passion makes discussions engaging, and he values participation, so speak up! If you care about the topic, you'll love it. His feedback is thoughtful, pushing you to grow as a writer. Highly recommend for anyone interested!

Ahlquist is an amazing person and very, very nice professor. He is very into expanding native rights, and is generally against the use of technology to address social issues like climate change. if you disagree with him on both those, you should think twice. As someone who disagrees with him on those though, he is still a great professor

I'm so glad I took this class. It was my favorite in my first semester of JMC. He really did a lot of work to make his classroom a community and a safe space for all his students. Discussion matters, and participation matters, but the topics are so interesting that it was easy! Lots of reading, but it's mainly online articles. HAVE to read them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I had him for MC111 this Fall semester. Super smart and caring, will help you throughout the course. It's a hard transition going into JMC, but he brightens the whole atmosphere. He creates a good environment where you can have fun, insert your opinion, ask questions, and learn. I highly recommend him for any course you choose to take.

Professor Ahlquist is the best professor I have ever met. I took MC111 with him last semester, he has been such an inspiring and caring teacher. I would not say this class is easy, BUT, if you really put in effort, you are ready to get a good grade. Make sure to go to his office hours for extra comments! recommend this class to all JMC people!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took MC111 with Ahlquist and definitely came away a better writer! He is very understanding when it comes to personal issues and is clear with his expectations for class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors! The content and discussions are very engaging. You are graded on participating and are allowed limited absences. There are a few small writing assignments and two papers. He has high writing expectations and does not grade easy. Overall, he cares a lot about his students and will be willing to help you.

Professor Ahlquist has a way of brightening the classroom, whether in-person or online. Each day he was equal parts personable and intelligent, his anecdotes about each reading made the mountains of text legible and worth tackling each class. By the end, you'll walk out with more than a polished writing style; you'll find a friend in Ahlquist.

Professor Ahlquist is my favorite professor by far! One of the most caring and genuine people in the world. He sparks an interest for any topic we're discussing and makes you excited to come to class. He is all about establishing connections and making sure that every student feels welcomed and comfortable with him and fellow classmates. Love him!

Professor Ahlquist is the best Professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He makes learning easy, not like an easy A (you have to work very hard) but in the way where he ignites a spark within you that you didnt know existed. His feedback is very helpful and he is always available to help.
I love Prof Ahlquist! He is an amazing guy! he's very passionate about his field of study and students! I Will take in again sometime in the future,
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This was my second time having Professor Ahmed and once again, I enjoyed him very much. Hes such a kind and generous professor with so much love for his students and his work. I really appreciate him and I hope to have more classes with him in the future. Hes an undeniable asset to the Department of Romance & Classical Studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Ahmed is a wonderful professor. He puts his heart and soul in his teaching and is extremely passionate about the French language. He also seems to be particularly interested in classic French literature. He is so kind, caring, flexibl. I wish that more college professors were like him. You're bery fortunate to have him.

He is insanely helpful and gives great feedback and you can definitely tell he wants you to succeed. It is a hard class for those French does not come easily to, so you'll have to put in effort. Manageable homework, short readings. Lots of quizzes/exams and a few papers. Participation is very important. You'll gain a great knowledge base in this.

VERY hard subject. While it gets easier to comprehend the various topics and understand the terminology towards the end, there isn't often enough time to write everything down during the test that they are looking for. She can also be a little nit-picky on the tests when it's hard to understand what the question is asking for.

Awesome teacher! Funny and interesting--often supplements her powerpoints with videos and fun facts. Only teaches practical things you will need to know. Involves the class during her lectures with discussion and questions. A massive amount of info to learn in this class but she helps make it enjoyable and easier to remember.

She was the perfect anatomy lab professor. Provided lots of visuals and hands-on specimens. Tried to make everything as clear as possible and genuinely wanted us to succeed. As long as you study her lectures and your notes, you will do great on the tests. Only problem was that there were only 2 tests so the grade weight on each was very high.

Its an online course so you have to participate online. When not understanding the professor is easy to email and responds quickly. His lectures were good and the reading posted was a lot, but the course was easy to manage. The final exam was easy, I only used to DSM and the clinical cases books.

This guy is a great teacher, engaging, reasonable and empathetic.  Brian genuinely cares about the students and is sincere, but expects you to work.  He makes a difficult topic look easy.  I really may not have made it with a different professor.  Highly recommend!
He is not good at giving clear directions in class.  Read and follow the course syllabus--he treats it like a contract!

Dr. Ahmedani is a great research methods instructor. This is generally a really hard course but he made it quite a bit easier. Now having said that, it's still alot of work. Just isnt as bad as it could be. Just be warned, DO NOT CHEAT. He is vigilant and will bust you (at least thats what he says).

This professor teaches a very difficult research methods class.  The class itself is a lot of work, but Prof. Ahmedani has a great deal of experience and shares this with the class, which livens things up.  He is very funny and jokes a lot.  He's often willing to help students.  He's also (easily) the hottest professor I've ever had in college.

Required gen ed but insanely hard. Wouldn't post lecture slides, recitations were brutal, assigned around 5 books, multiple midterms with 4–5 essay questions, plus random 30-second pop quizzes. Felt more like a grad seminar than a basic requirement. Way over the top and unnecessarily stressful.

reviews.comment: Would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst class I had at MSU
Never take this class
terrible experience

reviews.comment: Achebe is super passionate about this class and it's super interesting. If you don't show up to lectures you're screwed. TA's don't really know whats going on, but assignments weren't that bad as long as you follow the rubric and go to class. She gives you literally 30 seconds for pop quizzes and doesn't share her slides so take some notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super interesting lectures, Dr. Achebe is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. She expects those who take her classes to learn a lot. Not a lot of assignments, but the assignments that do exist are big ones. Be prepared to read quite a bit and beware of random pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very invested in her classes and is very passionate about her classes, but do NOT take her if your class is online. There are constant pop quizzes that are not representative of the content of the course and they follow the format of in-person learning (i.e. 3 minutes to take and submit it). I'm sure it's great in person but online was bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is absolutely horrendous. TAs are not on the same page. The syllabus is not specific at all. They give pop quizzes and allot us only 1 minute. The syllabus is not specific at all. The teaching staff is extremely technologically challenged. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gives pop quizzes that are 60 seconds long, does not care about students grades. All she does is lecture with very few lecture slide: impossible to take notes. Projects are ridiculously long However she is very passionate about what she teaches and you will learn so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved IAH 205 with prof Achebe! She is one of the most passionate profs I've had and offers lots of extra credit. If you are willing to put in the work then the class is an easy A. She teaches from her experiences so if you don't go to lecture then you're out of luck. I'm hoping she will be teaching my ISS course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult class but great professor. Three extremely difficult papers and two blue book exams. Tough grader but very generous with extra credit. Random pop quizzes so gotta show up to class. I found that no matter how hard i worked on the papers my grade was always substandard, but the extra credit helped me earn a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Went into this class thinking it would be super boring but it turned out being my favorite class that semester! Professor Achebe is very educated on the information presented and makes each lecture entertaining. Midterm and final questions are short answer and given beforehand! Very glad I took this course

Honestly, Achebe is probably the best professor for this course. She's so passionate about the topics that it's basically impossible to fall asleep. There's three big paper assignments throughout the entire course and six(?) pop quizzes so attendance is basically mandatory. Very hard grader though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is an amazing woman and the class an amazing course. She speaks with such dignity and strength and passion you're forced to be engaged. She teaches from her heart and has an immense amount of knowledge. The class wasn't too difficult, many projects and a lot of reading. The exams were pretty intense but weren't graded too harshly.

I respect her more than any professor Ive ever had. She is passionate and her work and life experiences are truly incredible. Ive gained love for Africa and my knowledge came from someone so close to it (shes from Nigeria). Perfect English and to the point. The projects are spread out and you get time. There is nothing wrong to say.

Not a bad class, but definitely a lot of work. Lectures aren't mandatory, but there are 5 random pop quizzes in class throughout the semester, so you kind of have to go. TAKE GOOD NOTES, you'll need it when studying for midterm and final. Mandatory recitation on Friday's, so hopefully you get a good TA. I had Janelle Edwards who was fantastic.

I also took her IAH 205 course, and totally loved her. She is passionate, brilliant, and by far  my all-time favorite professor. If you show up, do the reading, and actually participate you will do great. In her HST class we have deep discussion, amazing stories, and she promised to cook for us at the end of the semester. Take both classes!!

The class covers a very wide range of African topics including religious and traditional history, modern culture and economic system but the tests are Blue Book essay tests that ask 3 or 4 very specific questions and leave a lot of the lecture material irrelevant since the tests are not cumulative. And recitation is mandatory with group presenting.

This class is really hard. There is a lot of writting and high expectations. The exams are brutal, long essays, and map quizzes. She is very nice, funny, and passinate about what she's teaching. But sometimes too passinate, like yells into her microphone until it hurts your ears.
Excellent professor, very helpful, enjpoyed her class, learnt a lot!!!
Loved this Professor!! She seemed intimidating but when I went into her office hours she was completely down to earth and we ended up talking for two hours about non-class related things!!
Great teacher; Great clothes.  Passionate about what she teaches; cares about her students.  Hard class but you'll learn a lot

Excellent professor! She really knows her stuff. I would highy recommend any serious student to take hher class. She is one of the best professors they have in history and she is serious about her work! You will learn a great deal in her class, slackers need not apply!!
Beware to be accused of AI plagiarism if you are a competent writer. Beware.

This class wasn't well structured, and it wasn't all Acevedo's fault. She's very caring, kind, and energetic, but the class activities, assignments, and projects weren't the best in my opinion. Attendance is mandatory, but she's a flexible and caring professor.

Dr. Acevedo is kind and clearly cares about her students. The class is easy, with grades based only on four projects, including one group assignment. However, she often goes off on political rants and shares personal stories about past students that probably shouldn't be repeated. Different views don't feel welcomed or tolerated in her classroom.

Dr. Acevedo was extremely kind and always willing to read your essays and gives amazing feedback on what you should add or take away from your essay. Class is mandatory but she understands if something comes up. I would 100% recommend taking WRA 101 with her especially if you like to mess around. Dr Acevedo likes to keep things fun and is genuine!!

Talk about deranged. Denise had a political meltdown every other lecture. Always complaining about the administration has absolutely no respect for students who share other beliefs. Avoid her at all costs!

Love her!! It's clear she loves her job and adores her students — very flexible and willing to work with you. Highly recommend, her class was very educational while maintaining a fun, relaxed atmosphere :). Takes student feedback into consideration and actually applies it to her curricula. Highly recommend!
I absolutely loved WRA 101 with Dr. Acevedo. She cares about the success of all her students and goes above and beyond to help. Definitely one of my favorite professors at MSU.

A very nice person who cares for her students. An Hour and 50 minute lecture is way too long and it shows but a very easy grader and understanding as well. There are four projects and she gives you a lot of time to work on them. My only complaint is she isn't very clear with the projects and it's almost like she changes her mind mid way through.

Dr. Acevedo is the best. She truly cares about her students and thats reflected in her class. Assignments are easy and so is the grading but if you're stuck with a group that doesn't help then let her know and she'll try her best to help. Shes also absolutely hilarious and brought in ice cream for the class.
Taking WRA 101 with Dr. Acevedo was pretty easy. You have 4 projects throughout the semester and you get lots of time to do them. Some projects are with groups. I'd recommend taking WRA with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Acevedo is the only prof I've had that cares to get to know you. The 4 projects in this class are a little odd, but the reflective essay at the end of each one isn't hard. You definitely have to like writing to really enjoy this class tho. She talks about her own life a lot but is super funny so I like listening to her stories. Grades easy too.

Dr. Acevedo is a great professor who genuinely cares about her students and their success. The projects in this class are a little insane, but it makes it interesting. Highly recommend taking WRA 101 with her.

Prof. Acevedo is super easy to get along with, and is super fast with answering messages and questions about assignments. She's understanding and assignments are straight forward. The class isn't super hard but theres a lot of writing but she gives good feedback and will read papers before you turn them in if you ask.

Imagine every white narcissistic vain egotistical teacher you had in hs and amplify it ten times. Dr.Acevedo has no sense of her own classroom and the students in it because no one has ever walked out of her course having learned anything or smiled once. Please do not take wra with her because you will not enjoy one minute of your time

Dr. Acevedo is a really good person but her work is a little insane. This definitely wasn't treated like a 100 level course. This class did 4 different group projects and then after each project we wrote a reflective essay. So be prepared for writing a lot of essays. Her grading was pretty easy though, I got a 100% on all my essays.

The entire class is doing group projects which is a pain, and she overcomplicates things for no reason. I found her to be culturally ignorant with the latino culture as well it was quite uncomfortable. She was very nice, but if you missed a peer review she would automatically take off 30 points, and if she didn't like your peer review she dock.

I took IAH 231B with Dr. Acevedo online in the summer, and she is one of the best professors I have ever had. She actually reads and responds to each student, and her assignments are clear. You can tell she truly puts effort into her class. Would recommend :)

Absolutely loved her classes! I had her for WRA 101 as well as IAH 206 and received a 4.0 in both classes. She grades super easy, the only thing she asks of you is to attend class and participate in discussions. She is super sweet and very caring towards her students. Highly recommend taking any of her classes!
The best professor in WRA!!!
Best prof ever! Super sweet and cares about her students immensely.

That is very good professor in MSU
Best

Professor Acevedo is such a sweetheart. The best way to do well in her class is to show up in office hours a few days before a project is due, and she will honestly help you edit the entire paper as long as there isn't a line of people waiting. You will do well as long as you turn your discussion posts etc. in on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Due dates and assignment instructions are poorly formatted in a way that requires more work on your end than necessary to find them. Late work is not accepted for credit, no forgiveness if you mess up, even at the beginning. Class is listed as asynchronous yet we still had 5 required Zoom lectures. My grade did not reflect my effort at all.

I recommend her as a prof. I had her for WRA 1004 and WRA 101 and she was the best (I received an A in both courses). Participation matters in her class, but the assignments are not tough at all. She is very caring, understanding, and willing to help you out if you need it.

AWESOME professor. Class is relatively easy and she gives great feedback. Super friendly and available outside of class. I can't say enough good things about her honestly. Hearing "aha moment" all the time over the semester got kind of old but that's about the only complaint I have. I really enjoyed this class.

Dr. Acevedo is an amazing professor. She cares for her students as if they were own children. The class is beneficial as well. Participation is key to passing her class. If you need additional help, you can go to her office hours, give her a call, or just text her. I would definitely recommend to have her as a professor if you can.
One of my most favorite professors at MSU.

If you have the option to have Dr. Acevedo as a teacher, DO IT!! She's an amazing teacher! It is not hard to do well in that class if you do the reflections, go to class, and participate! Would 100% take another class with her!

I would recommend this professor to anyone and everyone. Dr. Acevedo is an AMAZING person and professor. Her class is enjoyable (as every class should be) and she keeps every lecture interesting and engaging. As long as you put forth your effort, participate and show up to class, you'll get a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved WRA 150 with Dr. Acevedo! She's one of the only professors I've had that truly cares about their students. Participate in class, go to office hours if you need help, and if you have any questions ask!

The only professor I've had who actually seemed to give a damn about their students. She makes sure she gets to know you and you know her back. She's always there to help with whatever you need even if you're not in her class anymore. I really enjoyed her class because she makes sure you understand what to do and how to get the best grade possible.
She was sooo nice! LOVED HER! take war 150 with her! i got a 3.5 on most my essays. she was so easy and nice

Dr. Acevedo is one of the most caring educators that I have ever had in my entire educational career. She absolutely LOVES her students, and goes go out of her way to get to know them better. She is always encouraging students to come to her office hours or text/call if there is anything that they need, academically-related, or not. Very loving!

Ackerman tries to make class fun. If you care about your grade, show up, and put in the effort outside of class, you will pass. He will never cancel a class, even if the weather is really, really bad.

You genuinely have to put in effort if you want a good grade. If economics is not your strong suit, you might want to go to office hours and the help room to get better. The professor is really nice and helpful, but only if you ask for help. The grade range of a 4.0 is larger than the stereotypical 90-100%, but it can still be challenging.
He makes the class entertaining and interesting, I recommend for EC201/202.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: THE GOAT.🐐LeBron James in the lectures should say it all. He is also the GREATEST 3rd grade girls soccer and basketball coach to never win a game! (Please include me in your syllabus week lecture)
On the first day of class, he will talk about the similarities between himself and Lebron James. This is Ackermann teaching students that he is, in fact, the GOAT.
if you're not a business major, i highly recommend you take this class in person. very difficult concepts that are hard to grasp and the exams are very math-based, which can be a struggle.

I truly do not understand the complaints about Dr. Ackermann or his class. His lectures were entertaining and actually explained the material rather than rushing through it. The tests were very similar to the homework and practice tests, sometimes having identical questions. An 88 is an A and the lowest three homeworks and lowest test are dropped.

Ackermann is a funny and nice guy, clearly loves what he does. His lectures are good, nothing amazing, but the weekly homework assignments are lengthy.
