reviews.comment: professors nice, her lectures are the opposite. this class should only be targeted for majors focusing on kinesiology or nutrition. otherwise, if you were to take this as an elective, get ready to cram. the class overall is interesting, but her teaching style makes it boring. i'd only take her if you plan on going into specific fields as mentioned.

Prof. A is a very sweet lady, who is very passionate about nutrition. She loves her job/students. However, I found the exams pretty difficult, and she does not provide enough resources to help you study. Her lectures are also very boring, and way too complicated. She tells you more info than you need to know, so you dont know whats important

I had a hard time learning in class at all. All the things I learned I had to teach myself. She talks about everything but the topics we are learning about and crams in the things we need to know. Lots of boring assignments

Her lectures could be condensed more, the course is interesting but grades being primarily based on exams, it leaves little room. There are multiple different forms for these exams she gives out too, which leads to some of the "same" exams being much harder than others. She usually makes these exams the night prior too, so expect random material.

would rather eat crayons for an entire semester than take this class again

doesn't finish lectures, exams have multiple forms; meaning some exams are MUCH easier than others,

also, has not graded any assignments SINCE WEEK 4. 

so, unless you need to take this class there's probably something else better for you as an elective!

I've never been so confused with a singular class. All she does is rush thorough a very intense lecture about things that aren't even on the exam. Most of the time she is yapping about something not even related, her lecture are very confusing and this class is unnecessary for a 150 level class. Don't take this class unless its required.

I have never had such a hard time understanding a professor in my life. She tries to cram in SO much information into each lecture (majority of the time she doesn't even finish the slides, but it is still on the exam). Exams are hard, so study a lot. I took this class as an elective, would not recommend unless you need it for your major.

For a 100 course, the workload is ABSURD. Should definitely be a 300 level, as to not rope in freshmen into failing out their first semester. Get prepared to write the length of a 25-page essay for a project a week before an exam, and review 200 slides a week for said exam. If you're planning to take this class as an elective, I would drop it.

She is ok I guess. The tests were pretty hard and you had to study a lot to do good in the class. Make sure you do every extra credit possible as it helps a ton down the road. She is super nice but the class is pretty tough. If you are taking this class as an elective, I'd avoid and take a different class as you'll have to work really hard.

She goes on long tangents. Don't get the textbook. 1 Go to class pay attention and get iClicker points, 2 complete assignments, and 3 complete extra credits: these 3 things are easy points. Tests rely on rote memorization, if you pay attention in class and look at the HNF 150 quizlets, you can guarantee yourself decent exam grades.

The content you learn in HNF is very useful and entertaining, but somehow Professor Alaimo tends to make the lectures difficult to follow. Not sure how to explain it, but my classmates last semester would agree. The exams are kind of hard, but very doable if you study hard.

You probably don't need to buy the textbook. This course is very test heavy as they are each 20% of your grade. My advice is get a 100% on everything outside of the exams and do the extra credit opportunities so you have room to get some stuff wrong on the exams. Go to class to get iClicker points and use quizlet to study for exams. She's annoying.

Class is lecture heavy and it will get boring very quickly. There is a ton of memorization that goes into studying for exams and I feel like exams were kind of difficult. There are a lot of free points with homework and extra credit, but you will need to do well on exams to 4.0.

Professor Alaimo is nice but overall, the class was a waste of my time. She goes on random tangents on unnecessary topics and we almost never covered all of the material in class. As long as you do the EC and understand the concepts of the LO's, you should do well. Class is primarily on memorization - READ THE BOOK!
It is a hard class, especially for being 100, but Dr. Alaimo cares. Exams are pretty hard as well for a 100 level, so be ready to study. It is an interesting class at the end of the day.

Dr. Alaimo was amazing! She was clear about what we needed to know/learn. She is passionate about what she teaches. Great applications to real life. No homework. Tests were exactly what she taught us/prepared us for. Lots of extra credit!!
The class is not that bad, but she goes on and on about SOIL!. I cannot stand it anymore. I feel like I'm going crazy.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. 

For this class to be a 100 level, the workload is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Always due the videos early to get extra credit. everyone does bad on first exam but they get easier. my class was online so i never saw or even contacted her. its A LOT of information its crazy. i wouldnt suggest anyone to take it just cuz its hard

online asynch class, but in-person exams. yup, worst combo. 3 exams, worth 20% each -- so yes, super exam heavy. if you keep up with the lectures, you should be good on the exams -- just know there is a LOT of information to learn in this class! if you are interested in nutrition, then take it, if you aren't, then don't. lots of work, but cool info

For being a 100 level class it is very demanding, I found this class harder than my 400 level classes. There is so much content covered that it is hard to keep up and she does not help simplify the material for the exam. You are told to study everything rather than her eliminating some of the unnecessary information. I do not recommend this class.
I learned so much from this class and I think its really good knowledge for anyone to have. Professor Alaimo was interesting to listen to and genuinely wants her students to learn.

The amount of content you cover is insane. I'm a nutrition major and even I had a hard time with all the material. The exams are bad because there's so much to study. The assignments aren't terrible, discussion posts and weekly quizzes. DAA part 2 takes forever so don't wait to start until the last minute. Bought the textbook and opened it twice.

Despite what a lot of people are saying, this class with Professor Alaimo is manageable if you do the work. Quizzes were open note and as long as you follow instructions on assignments you'll be fine. Exams were a big part of the grade, but study for them that week and you should be fine. Not a blow-off class, but not as hard as it sounds.

It does have workload and yes, the exams are in person, but It isn't TERRIBLE. It reminds me of the avg high school class. Quizzes are open note, studying the slides can be enough, and reviewing some days before exams can be enough. Your two lowest quizzes and your two lowest PeaPods are dropped, along with opt. final exam. This class is v passable

This class was the worst I've ever taken since I got to MSU. I took an asynchronous section, however she forced us to do in-person test or would have to be taken on a lockdown browser and could get points off for dumb things like TALKING TO YOURSELF. She makes everything extra and complicated. A lot of material has to be memorized. DO NOT TAKE!

I thought it would be a easy blow-off class. Wrong. This class was harder than my level 300 classes, you can do all of the readings, watch the lectures and still fail. Nothing of meaning was taught in this class and I dreaded all of the assignments. The Peapod things suck, the dietary assignment is awful. Please choose a different class.

Hnf 150 with Alaimo your freshman year will make you want to drop out of college in the nicest way possible. Professor Alaimo is sweet but her lectures are lengthy and boring. Assignments are terrible we have videos we have to record for this class every week and not only are they hard to upload but they require so much effort. AnD ExAmS R BRUTAL!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Halfway through the semester you do a dietary assessment that analyzes the food you eat, which in my opinion is not beneficial for students mental well-being. I struggle with self image and my eating habits and this assignment made it worse. She offers an alternative but I did not know the extent the DAA would go, so I did not think I would need it

Professor Alaimo's class would be really easy if it weren't for her exams. The homework is super easy and can get done in under an hour. There are a few longer projects to complete but she gives extra credit if they are turned in early. The only issue is that the homework will not prepare you for the exams. These exams are graded HEAVILY.

Dr. Alaimo is a very nice professor and will make special accommodations for students if needed (she allowed me to push back an exam by a few days because I was sick). However this class is NOT an easy A, you will have to watch all lectures and study for all exams to get a 4.0 because the exams are proctored online. Only take if required/interested
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Alaimo is very kind and the workload was not too heavy. I enjoyed the discussion posts and having to cook with topics covered during the week. She dropped a few grades which was relieving, however as long as you pay attention to the lectures and stay organized, the class is an easy A. Exams were proctored online.

HNF 150 was not the best, but not the worst, took it for a PA school prereq. Dr. Alaimo was an okay professor at best. One good thing is that she is willing to compromise with students. She makes you do a lot of work for the level of the course, so be ready to work and comprehend the material. HNF 150 is not a blowoff, that is very important.

Dr. Alaimo is probably the best prof I had this semester. Her class taught me lists of life skills and she was so kind. It relied mostly on lectures and reading material however, the lectures were easy to watch and not boring. She often pushed back due dates on large assignments to accommodate for students. Very nice lady!

Taken online due to Covid. Must buy the book and a dietary program. You have quiz's (called problem sets) every week with 2 tries along with discussions in which you must post a picture of the food from that week. Exams are all lockdown so expect lots of time to study. Optional final that can replace your lowest exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: My worst nightmare. She has crazy rules for exams and makes it almost impossible for you to do well. We had expressed many concerns and she dismissed all of them. This class was a 100 lvl and felt more like a 300+ lvl. There were probably 250+ terms per exam and all the exams were 50 questions but different questions per student's exam. DON'T TAKE.

I wouldn't recommend taking this class if you are looking for an easy A filler class, but if you are a nutrition major or interested in nutrition I learned a lot! You have to put in some work though. The first exam is the most difficult, after that it is pretty easy. The notes are disorganized but I just fill out the notes with the transcript.

This class might as well have been 5 credits. The homework load is ridiculous. She thinks her class is the most important thing in the world, and, despite student feedback, she doesn't change the workload or the testing procedures. We did a lockdown browser, and we couldn't even use a blank sheet of paper to write our thoughts down. Unresponsive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Treated her FULLY ONLINE, 100 LEVEL INTRODUCTION COURSE like it was an in-person, graduate 400+ level program. No regard for the mental well being of her students. An absolute nightmare. I will never take her classes again.

Professor Alaimo is a very, very nice lady and seems to have good intentions. However, with this being an online semester she has made exam taking ridiculous. You cannot go back to questions on exams, you cannot wear hats, and you cannot talk to yourself or read anything aloud. We have talked to her but have seen nothing change. Very disappointing.

Professor Alaimo really missed the mark with this class. I find myself spending more time on this introductory nutrition class than I do for orgo 2. Her skeleton notes are disorganized, in the online format we're basically teaching ourselves, and the amount of material she requires us to know for the exam is absurd... would not recommend.

wasnt the biggest fan. took it for my stem class as a poly sci major & it was unbelievably hard. other people i know who are nutrition majors also had a hard time. she goes through lecture very fast & its hard to keep up. weekly discussion posts & quizzes. dont take unless youre a nutrition major/super interested. worked my butt off for a 3.5
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: dr alaimo is fantastic! so nice and caring. her anecdotes are great and she has very good lecture slides. use the study questions/outline to study for the exam and you'll 4 point no problem. her final is optional; if you take it your grade can only improve. i'd take her class again, she's very interesting and a great prof

Dr. Alaimo is very caring and understanding and clearly knows her stuff. However, the lectures are boring and the exams are difficult. Book is not needed. Study the learning objectives and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You have to work hard for the tests because they're a majority of your grade and they contain a lot of material. Her lectures are fairly long and drawn out, but she at least tries to be entertaining (unlike Ekstrom). She also goes on tangents about things that aren't on the exam. Just know whatever is on the learning objectives and you'll be fine!

Dr. Alaimo is a very great professor. But she did talk from the second we started class, to the very end. No breaks and those seats are not comfortable. The class was just so much material you had to remember. One helpful thing was that she did give us a sort of "study guide." My grades for the test did improve over time thanks to a TA I saw.

As a non-science major, this class is NOT easy! Prof. Alaimo does an amazing job providing resources for her students, but there is a lot of challenging material in the class. Don't take this as an "easy 3 credits." You'll get the most out of the course by showing up to lectures and paying close attention. Attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you plan on being a dietetic or in the health field, then take this class. If you aren't then good luck. Alaimo is a good prof. She's very sweet and caring. Not much hw. Lectures aren't too bad to sit through. The issue is that I was told this class was the easiest STEM credit and it was NOT.

Prof. Alaimo is one of the best professors at MSU. I was going through a family issue back in the fall which required me to miss about a week of school and prof. Alaimo was very caring and and tried helping me in any way that she can for me to catch up on the stuff that I missed. She even let me take an exam that I missed whenever I wanted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a very caring professor and genuinely wants all of her students to pass. However, she rambles a lot during lectures about random stories or things she finds interesting, but then they aren't on the exams. The learning objectives are necessary to know as well as all slides inside and out. Should be an easy class, but it really isn't.

LOVED this prof! Her lectures are long but interesting and she keeps lectures fresh by including little stories and having food tastings. She counts attendance, but you'll want to show up anyways because if you don't, you will miss a lot. Exams aren't bad if you study a bit, overall would recommend this class to anybody in a health related field :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: a lot of homework, but none of which are difficult at all. tends to ramble off during lectures and offer information that is irrelevant to the course and exams.

Alaimo's a really sweet lady, and her class is not difficult. She does her best to make it fun, and she really cares. iClicker points everyday, but I skipped a lot and still got full credit because so much is dropped. Definitely an easy 4.0. Spent two hours max studying for each exam. Good way to get the natural science gen ed done!

I was warned when my advisor put me in this class that they push it on transfers and freshman because theyre not aware of how hard the class is. I wish I wouldve listened to them instead of online reviews of Alaimo and the class. I had to drop it due to the level of difficulty. She seems sweet but this class is ridiculous. Save your money!!!

I honestly did not like the way this professor teachers. She seems very sweet, but her lectures will put you to sleep. Also studying for exams is so hard because the questions on the exams are worded in very confusing ways. Not very hard to 3.5/4.0 if you put in the effort. Did not enjoy taking this class & would not recommend.

HNF 150 can be an easy class. Just do every homework assignment during class. She drops one of her tests, so the final is optional. Memorize everything for the exams and get an easy 4.0. She seems nice
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Doesn't finish on time. Write down things you don't think you need to.  Very sporadic.

Prof Alaimo was one of the kindest professors I've encountered. She's truly a sweetheart and wants every single student to pass; that being said, she's more than willing to help. Lectures are engaging and well-organized. Alaimo breaks down complex topics (such as the biology behind digestion) in a way that anyone could understand. Wonderful human.

I loved this class and Professor Alaimo! You can definitely tell that she is passionate about what she teaches, and she shows genuine concern for all of her students, which is impressive given her large lecture sizes.  I would highly recommend this class for anyone, regardless of your major.  I learned a lot, and it was a very fun elective!

Dr. Alaimo was a wonderful professor and I really enjoyed  her class! I learned a lot of new  information about nutrition. The iClicker is used for participation and there are weekly assignments/quizzes to help solidify the material. Exam questions are based on info found on the learning objectives so be sure to use them for your studying!

Alaimo is one of the best professors I have ever had! She genuinely cares about all of her students and is willing to help in any way she can. Lectures can be a bit boring, but she tries to make them more interactive by showing videos and stuff. This class is an easy 3.5/4.0 if you are willing to put in some effort.

iClicker is used for participation points during classes. Exams are relatively easy. She has a soft voice in lecture than can be hard to hear. She is super nice tho. The class can get boring after awhile. Posts powerpoints on D2L. Study the learning objectives online and you'll be set.
Talks to students like they're two. Easy class.

Annoying at times but is helpful when you need her. Book is really important if you want to do well since her lectures come from it. Do objectives and lecture outlines and you'll get a guaranteed 4.0.

really likes to talk... kind of treats students like elementary schoolers.  You have no idea what is on the exam because she loves to talk about things that she finds "interesting" but aren't actually important.

She's a great prof, although sometime kinda boring, but her lecture notes really did help me when studying for exam. Also, her lecture objective guides are a great guide at studying for exams, cuz all ques from exams come from there. A very fun and meaningful class about the right way to eat and keep a healthy body.
Boring class.

I had Professor Stanton for the 2025 Fall Semester PR 225 Writing class. I thought I took a lot away about the basics of writing in the PR world and found it to be a very helpful introductory course. Professor Stanton gave great feedback, cared about how her students did, and was not a harsh grader. I would definitely recommend taking this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Professor Stanton for the 2025 Fall Semester PR 225 Writing class. I took a lot away from the class and was a really good introduction to writing in the PR world. Professor Stanton gave great feedback throughout the semester, was not a harsh grader, and showed a lot of care for her students work.

The class required a lot of writing assignments, and she was slow getting our assignments back to us. But she really cared about the class and about helping us build a PR writing portfolio. She wanted us to participate. We did a lot of partner exercises in class that made the class more interesting. I liked that she walked around the room so much.

Don't be discouraged from her class. She's attentive and engages, so anticipate her walking around n asking questions. Workload is manageable. She goes out her way to help best she can. Stay after class if u have questions; she addresses them transparently and guides u step by step. There's a textbook & subscription, but u can pass w/o if u engage.

Great professor! She's very transparent, approachable & sets clear expectations while still being supportive. She encourages participation, stays after class to help & ensures everyone feels heard. I loved how she taught us to use AI ethically and modeled project expectations. You will get from this course what you put into it, so show up & engage.

Lectures were long, not really her fault,(6pm-9pm) class. Feedback takes a while to get back. I thought she did her best. You could tell she cared about preparing us for the workforce and reflected that through the assignment she gave us (you build a portfolio throughout the semester. Final is improving the work you already did from her feedback.

Just don't take her courses. Waste of time literally. Got quite an attitude with me multiple times when I would ask questions. Rambles about NOTHING. Uses chatgpt to grade and give feedback. My group never showed up and she didn't care. Just doesn't care about her students honestly. Hope she does some reflection after this semester.

Lectures are impossible to follow- class material is unclear in how it correlates to assignments (and there are a lot of them). Assignments are time consuming, and feedback is fully AI generated. Also spoke condescendingly to students often. Nice enough, just extremely frustrating to work with.

Lectures are extremely boring and hard to follow. Used the required textbook one time at the beginning of the semester. She also requires you to get chat gtp premium and i think she uses AI to grade. Sweet lady that definitely means well, but so so disorganized and scattered.

I'm still thinking about this class a year later. The way we were "teamed up" was so chaotic. She separated us vaguely by interest, then just threw us into a group of like 12 ppl to try and find 2-3 ppl to spend the next 10 weeks working with. My group was awful & her grading was merciless. One of two classes I didn't get a 4.0 in my entire career.
Graded us with chatgpt because most of her rubrics were wrong so that was nice. her feedback didn't even follow our assignment sometimes.

Makes grading so difficult for a beginner-level course on grant writing. I have never done grant writing before and have never been graded so hard for something I have never done before. Be prepared to have unfair grading, a lack of care from her, and overall one of the worst experiences in a classroom. She also has an unfair grading scale as well

Such an awesome prof. Very kind and resourceful. I took this class without knowing anything about grant writing, but her lectures were great, and she gave very helpful feedback on assignments, so this wasn't an issue at all. If you have to take an upper-level writing course and this is an option, I'd 10/10 recommend you choose to take one with her.
Dr. Wachuku's class was very easy, for someone who didn't use the textbook, I still got a 4.0

Don't take it if not required. Many quizzes have small numbers of questions but are closed-book. There is too much content to retain each week from the textbooks. The required books are too expensive. The professor is not clear on assignment instructions. I haven't learned anything that I already know from this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Wachuku is nice but is seriously a tough grader! And the grading scale for PH 101 is outrageous - to get a 4.0 you need a 95, and to get a 3.5, you need a 90. Don't take this class if you don't need to. There's a ton of papers for this class too, but don't expect anything higher than an 80, because prof is such a harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, he wants the best for each student and makes compromises when people didn't like things that were in the course. The labs are fine, but poorly structured. Exams cover a lot of content, but cheat sheets are allowed. Overall funny, nice, and a good professor.

Great professor. He is very passionate and wants students to succeed. One thing I think he could be better at is being consistent. For example, We had an exam review only for 2/3 midterm exams. And for our final exam he didn't post a review video until the night before.... The exam was at 12:45pm the next day.
The best professor ever, super kind, caring and flexible. Actually helps us get through the course.

Great professor. He focuses on learning the material in an engaging way rather than just strict deadlines and difficult exams. The material covered in the 410 course is very relevant to the packaging industry in the real world.

Dr.Joodaky is a very good prof, in the words of the esteemed American physicist Richard Feynman, If you want to master something, teach it. Dr.Joodaky has mastered this balance, thus leading to a rewarding class for his students that is constantly evolving to become better.
He is very caring of the students. wants them to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hes a nice teacher and seems like he knows a a lot. The lab reports were time consuming but graded fairly. Exams were in person and kinda hard, but he had some drops and extra credit at the end of the semester. There was also weekly hw but it didnt take long most of the time. Overall i liked him
Great professor. Helpful feedback and listens to students. Also very willing to help his students.
come to class because pop quizzes are done during class for attendance.
He was awesome! Very understanding and loved student feedback.
The class was hard, but he is very caring and does everything he can to help students succeed.
One of the better packaging professors.
Good professor who is understanding and willing to work with the students to make it better for us.

He was great. Super understanding and helpful when communicating with, and was willing to help whenever he was needed to. Explains everything really well, but the class material is difficult and requires time and effort to understand the information.
He was awesome! He loved student feedback, and was very understanding!
Very engaging professor. Test and lab heavy with a good amount of homework. If you go to class you're good.
Class was hard, but he is very caring and does everything he can to help students succeed.
Awesome, funny and is very thoughtful when it came to late submissions.
Great professor would love to have him again in the future.
very friendly and personable, Lab TA's make this class very easy because they give 100% on everything
I love this guy, wish he was my dad fr man.

Weekly long lab reports and no extra credit even if a class average on an exam is 40%. One time I stayed after class to ask a question about the homework and he just had me stand there and google it. I just wanted to know if it was explained in a previous lecture. Definitely the kind of prof who is there to do research & teaching is an afterthought

Dr. Joodaky is one of the best professors in the school of packaging. PKG 410 is a difficult class, but he wants to help you succeed. He is funny and caring about his students. Outside of class he will help explain things and he encourages you to get involved. I did a research project with him and it was a great experience.

This class is so easy. One assignment a week. Attendance is mandatory but it's only worth five points of your overall grade so you're fine if you don't go. Exams and quizzes use lockdown browser but she moved every one to taking it remote so it didn't matter. Easy ISS to 4.0.

Her class is not difficult in the slightest, with quizzes and exams being open-note.

Assignments are straightforward. 

She has a midterm which covers the first textbook and a final that covers the second; her final is not cumulative.

Unfortunately, her lectures are not all that interesting. I often found myself confused in certain sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant has been my favorite professor at MSU so far. I took her class to meet a school requirement but found myself actually interested in her lectures and the material. The textbook is free and though attendance is mandatory, she is very understanding. She wants you to do well!

Super nice professor who cares about the material she's teaching and cares about students. Very straight forward and easy class. Every quiz question was bar for bar from the combined lecture notes SHE would provide and let you print and take to the quiz. Not possible to fail. Also canceled class or finished early many times. 10/10

She is one of my favorite professors at MSU. She genuinely is passionate about the material she teaches and that reflects in her lectures. She also cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The quizzes and exams are open note, so you can actually focus on learning the material during class rather than memorizing. Take this class!!
TAKE THIS CLASS FOR UR ISS REQUIREMENT. SHES SO CUTE I LOVE HER AND CLASS WAS SO EASY AND SHE IS VERY CHILL AND TEXTBOOK IS FREE!
Amazing professor and very passionate about teaching. She somehow made every lecture interesting. 100% would take again
super sweet!! i loved the class its easy and workload is not heavy at all. exams are open note lock down browser. hws super easy. book is free!
Dr. Bryant is the best professor at MSU. Even though the class was just a general requirement, I was interested in learning.
dr bryant is so caring i would highly recommend
Dr. Bryant is one of the best professors I've had at MSU. She is very caring and compassionate. She let us use open notes on all of our quizzes.
Good professor, open note quizzes and tests makes things very easy. She posts all lecture notes and slides, doesn't stray much from the notes on quizzes and tests.

I had her for iss 210 and this class was very good. As long as you do the discussion posts and do good on the tests you will get a good grade. The tests were open note and you can print out the lecture notes she made and the tests were very self explanatory. I would 100% take this class again

Professor Bryant is admirably kind, charismatic, and understanding of student circumstances. She is very passionate about social issues and the content her class teaches. Her effort to maintain unbiassed perspectives while being educational about the topics she lectures about is evident and appreciated.

She was an extremely easy class but it was definitely the most pointless class and the biggest waste of time. Her lectures just go over the readings basically word for word so you really only need to do one or the other but she makes attendance mandatory for some reason. Easy class but such a waste. She also gives short notice for canceled class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant was such an amazing professor, the work load was very light in this class. We had weekly discussion posts, a few quizzes, and exams. But for all the quizzes and exams she allowed you to use notes and she had lecture notes available on d2l that had the exact answers to the test. Attendance was taken but not graded.
Probably the best professor I've had by far, the class was enjoyable and I learned so much.. She is great with grading and I have never dreaded doing her work. 10/10
Easy class, easy grade. Would definitely take her class again!
Very easy class, I highly recommend taking it.

She's such a sweetheart! During her first lecture, she said something under the lines of wanting all of us to get A's (which she said was 100% possible) and she hoped to be able to interact with all of us. Her feedback to our online papers/responses shows she cares about our performance, and her lectures are easy to navigate.

Super sweet professor who actually cares about students. She's really understanding and literally designs the class so you can get an A. It's so easy, everything is open note, and you don't even need to read any of the books to pass. 10/10 recommend as an easy ISS if you need one to take.

By far one of my favorite professors so far. She cares more about you asking questions than the grade you receive. Class is super easy, and every quiz and exam is open note. She is an amazing professor, and this class challenged me to question my views!

Very easy class, every exam and quiz was open notes provided by her. Attendance isn't mandatory but her lectures are pretty interesting and really easy to reach outside of class. I would def recommend for anyone.
Dr. Amber Bryant clearly understands students and does everything possible to help them succeed in her class.

Absolutely LOVE Dr. Bryant. clear, easy-to-follow lectures. The only downside I could see is the pace can be a little fast for notetaking but the tests and quizzes and exams are NOT cumulative! So you have lots of little breaks.

Dr. Bryant was a very good professor. She is very understanding of students and truly wants to see them succeed in her class. Tests we all open-note, so as long as you prepared yourself well, you could pass. Overall 10/10.

The first half of this class is super easy, she sends you a notes packet to print out and you can use it on the exam and the exam is word-for-word from the notes. The second half requires you to do the reading, but the exams are taken at home so... The lectures are a little boring but Dr Bryant is very sweet and friendly.

Professor Bryant is the best. She is kind and lectures are actually pretty interesting. Attendance isn't mandatory to get a good grade and there is minimal work in the class. Open note on every quiz and exam, so the easiest 4.0 ever. I actually learned a lot in this class as well, so I highly recommend taking this class with professor Bryant.
I really really enjoyed her as a teacher!!! I would recommend everyone to take her class. You can tell she really loves what she is doing.

TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSER. The best and most understanding professor I've ever had. Everything is open note and there are only weekly discussion posts. Lectures aren't required, but I would go because the class is so interesting and gives a different perspective. Definitely would take it if you want a 4.0.

Dr. Bryant is an amazing professor, she is very kind and likes to have fun in class. The class is made up of 4 quizzes, a midterm, a final, and discussion posts every week. All of the tests are open note and she gives you her lectures notes, where she pulls the quiz questions from. This is a very easy class and also very interesting.

Dr. Bryant is an amazing and understanding person. Her lectures are very beneficial and prepare you well for quizzes. The class's only reading is really only required during the second half of the semester and its relatively short, but MSU should really have more professors like her.

Amber Bryant is one of the sweetest professors I have had at MSU. She is super understanding and wants you to succeed in her class. There is extra credit. Open notes quizzes. If you pay attention in class then you will get a 4.0
Very laid back and cool.

Dr. Bryant is a great professor. The lesson plan is clear; you have similar weekly assignments, which helps create a schedule. As long as you show up to class, pay attention, and do the work, you will get a 3.5. She and her TA are available out of class in case of any problems. I would definitely go out of my way to take one of her courses again.

She was chill and even told us that she understands that we are all in different situations and it's okay if we can pass the class without going. Loved her, tests are open note and online, and she posts the combined lecture notes so you can just go off of those

Dr. Bryant is a great professor, is caring and always willing to listen; allowed me to turn in late assignments as well which not all profs do. Simple class, show up twice a week and take notes/pay attention and you will bare minimum 3.5 this class. Would highly recommend as it is straight forward, no trick questions or pop quizzes. Take this class

This professor really cares and wants to see her students succeed. Her lectures were interesting and she made sure to incorporate a variety of teaching methods to keep students engaged. She also provided many opportunities for extra credit and resources such as lecture notes to help students learn.

Bryant is super nice and the class was very easy. Everything is open note so you just have to print out the slide shows and guided notes. I recommend lectures as it makes the quizzes easier to take, but all the notes are available so it's fine to miss a lecture. Pretty boring, but I did learn some interesting and useful things about education!
Lots of discussion posts, quizzes and readings. Some info on slides was confusing. She was a very good teacher though and I would taker her class again. Just show up to class and you'll be fine!

best professor by far, if you attend the lectures and go through the notes you will 100% pass the class. She also is very kind and passionate about what she teaches. I loved her energy. The quizzes, tests, midterm, and final were open notes! please please take her class i am so glad i had Bryant as my prof. she has a very kind soul.
This course was really easy with not many homework assignments at all but the lectures were very boring and not engaging but an easy A. We also got to leave class early most days so that's a plus.

A great lecturer. She makes the class very simple and interesting. Often the tests are open notes. She is very willing to work with you to get you to the grade you want. She provides a lot of extra credit opportunities. She wants what is best for her students.
I enjoyed this class and Dr. Bryant was a great professor, you could tell that she is very passionate about her job which makes learning just as enjoyable.
My favorite professor so far she was easy and helped me get a 4.0 highly recommended
My favorite teacher EVER. She was so understanding and would give me extensions whenever I asked. So many opportunities for extra credit too!

professor bryant is a pretty good professor and seems very knowledge on the topics taught during class. i enjoyed having her as my professor and would definitely recommend her for as a great ISS prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Eh

Very good down to earth, relatable professor, that is also a good teacher, workload was good and the quizzes and tests I felt very prepared for ( and most of them were open note). Class wasn't any harder than it needed to be and having her as a professor was fun, and I would definitely like to have her as a professor again.

Dr. Bryant's class was very nice. All of her tests and quizzes (including midterm and final exam) were open note. As long as you take notes, you are almost guaranteed an A. There's one discussion post per week and she also offers 3-4 extra credit assignments. She's a very sweet lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: All her quizzes, the midterm, and the final are open notes. Make sure you know how to use your notes and can find things easily. Textbooks are required but you can make do without reading them.
Loved her and would definitely take her class again! All quizzes and tests are open note, and she gives you both lecture notes and guided notes for all, if not most, of them. Class was pretty easy!

Dr. Bryant is amazingggg! Not only is she a great teacher but she is very kind and understanding. The class is not bad at all you have two textbooks that you cover throughout the semester. Each week you have discussion posts, and most tests are open note. 10000000% reccomend.

Super lecture heavy, but if you didn't go most of the time you wouldn't understand what was happening. She is kind and when she isn't just reading off the slides and gets us to participate it's a fun class and she's a great teacher. Also all exams and tests are open note.
So kind and accommodating! You can tell she is passionate about what she teaches. She keeps lectures interesting and fun. Only a discussion post a week and a few quizzes. Definitely recommend.

The class was based off two textbooks where you would read 50-75 pages a week. Lectures would primarily go over what you read/learned about within this reading. If you show up to class/read you are basically guranteed a 4.0. She gave a decent amount of easy extra credit as well.

She is absolutely amazing! She gives clear expectations, tells you how you will succeed in the class, gives phenomenal feedback, and answers any questions we have. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is helpful to be in class to hear what she says that aren't in the slides. Overall best professor I've had this semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant is very kind and caring and wants to help you succeed. Quizzes and tests are open note, and homework is usually a discussion board due once a week. I find the material very interesting, and I would definitely take one of her classes again!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is amazing, she is so kind and will answer all your questions, she give you information that you probably never knew you needed. Her quizzes and tests are easy (open note) and she shares her lecture notes. If you go to class and pay attention then you will pass, a lot of people don't read the textbooks but I did and they helped me a lot.

This professor is extremely easygoing. Lots of lectures but they are interesting and engaging. Minimal assignments and open note tests, midterm, and final. If you pay attention to lectures and copy notes you won't need to worry about reading the textbooks.

She is an amazing professor who cares about her students and the information that she teaches. She makes the content interesting through her lectures. If you just show up for class you should be able to pass no problem. Open-note tests, mid-term, and final.
Overall a great teacher, she loves feedback from students.
She really cares about her students and is such a sweet person. A lot of reading but it is easy to keep up with and tests and quizzes are open note.
Allowed to drop grades. Open-note quizzes. Takes the time to help individual students.
Good professor, teaches well.
Easy class, just do the discussion posts and check the lecture notes for the quizzes.
All exams and quizzes are open notes, so definitely an easy A class as long as you take good notes. She made the lectures as fun and as interesting as possible.

She is awesome! Quizzes are online, open notes. She posts all of her lecture notes in case you want to look through. No projects, just quizzes and worksheets. Content is interesting and she is easy to listen to.
Super nice and understanding, take good notes and show up when you can because it will help you.

This class was easily my favorite class of my first ever college semester. Professor Bryant really did a wonderful job easing us students into the college curriculum and managed to make the class engaging and productive.
She was really easy and laid back. A couple books read but open note quizzes and exams, fairly easy class and fun.
Lecture heavy, but a great class to take! She is very straightforward with information and the level of difficulty is more on the easier side. Extremely respectable and understanding.

I really enjoyed this class with Dr. Bryant! She was very very sweet, you can tell she deeply cares about her students and those around her. Her classes are mostly lecture based on 2 different textbooks. She makes the class more interesting by including documentaries/movie days, and she gives out extra credit quite often. Quizzes are open book too!

Very easy class if you show up to her lectures and keep up with readings. Quizzes are not difficult and she gives you good lecture notes. Not many assignments a week only discussion posts that are very easy to answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant was a great professor! While some lectures were heavy with material she often used tools to make them more engaging, such as google polls or other ways to get class opinions on the content. Lecture notes are also posted weekly for important ideas and to help on open note quizzes which personally helped me better understand the readings.

I would definitely recommend anyone to take this class, it was really informative and laid back as far as workload. I feel like I really gained a lot from this class but also didn't have to worry about it.

Easy A, some interesting lectures, great person, very caring, I learned a lot in the course and did not struggle with grades. Although the lectures sometimes feels like she is just reading off a sheet of paper rather than being an expert on some of the subjects.

Although the course is lecture heavy, she finds a way to teach the lecture in a chill and conversational type manner. She gives you her own lecture notes before a quiz which are super helpful and she lets you print them out and have them during a quiz. Overall I would highly recommend taking her course because she is very down to earth.
she was a very good professer made the material intresting and lectures while being a little dull she would add non graded inclass activities that made it easier to understand and more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant is a passionate professor, you can tell she cares about what she's teaching. Attendance is not mandatory, and for the most part, everything covered in lectures is posted online. Exams/Quizzes are all open notes, which are also posted online. Overall, the class was very easy and I would recommend it!
Great professor, just take notes on the lectures and all quizzes will be easy. She is very straight forward and understanding. She wants her students to succeed and puts them first.

Very caring and passionate professor. She would help you out if you reach out to her personally. Coming to class is not mandatory as everything is on the lecture notes. All exams are open notes and just print out the notes she gave you and earn your easy A.

Overall very easy class. You will do well if you read the notes, which are posted. Going to class can be helpful since she goes over her lecture notes a little more thoroughly but it is not mandatory. Quizzes and exams are all open note and you will do well if you print out any resources given. Professor Bryant is very likeable in general.

Easiest ISS you can take at MSU. She lectures from a note paper that she posts online. The tests are open notes so you can print off the lecture notes and take the quiz. The answers are almost word for word what is in these notes. She tells you to read the book however it is not necessary bc she talks about everything that is important in the book.

Prof reads off of a script for all her lectures that obviously aren't written by her. Class is quite easy - only major homework is discussion posts and she posts all the lecture notes on D2L so going to every lecture is unnecessary. Don't bother buying the books unless you can find them for free. Overall pretty easy A which is nice for a gen ed.

She's very understanding about any issues if you just talk to her in-person. I recommend going to the TA's office hours regularly because her slides are hard to interpret on your own, and her accent makes long lectures hard to understand. All quizes an exams are on D2L asynchronously. Concepts are easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: All quizzes and tests are online and open book with no lockdown browser, and she offers enough extra credit. If you want an easy 4-point, Professor ALZ's class is perfect. But if you want to actually learn, don't take her. She's pro-AI and the class is so easy that it would be hard to learn anything unless I was REALLY interested in the material.
Very easy class, every assignment is out of class and online. Plenty of extra credit opportunities, and slides are super helpful for studying. Would recommend, seems nice and class is easy.
Dr. ALZ is an amazing professor and prioritizes the learning of her students. She offers a lot of extra credit which had me prioritize my learning over worrying about my grade.

Dr. ALZ is a Wonderfull professor! She is a very fair grader, and she goes through the lectures at a steady pace. She brings in a lot of guest speakers and gives out many extra credit opportunities. She also does demonstrations on certain types of software that students often have trouble navigating.

I really enjoyed this course. The professor really cares about the students and will often be very lenient about assignments and quizzes. She also gives a bunch of extra credit opportunities which can REALLY help boost your grade. The only downside to this course was the TA.

She's very sweet, but unfortunately often hard to follow during lectures, and the slides themselves can be a tad confusing. Dates for quizzes weren't really communicated until the class before or the day-of, and I flat-out missed one or two of them. That being said, there's TONS of easy extra credit to be had; I felt clueless and still got a 4.0.

I knew this class would be tough when she started the semester offering 40 points of extra credit. She ended up offering over 80. I earned 60 and still only got a 2.0. Her accent is horrendously difficult to understand and her lectures are not very clear. Weekly quizzes on random days of the week, and the assign

I often found myself very bored in this professor's class because she reads straight from the lectures that can be accessed online. Attending this class often felt like a waste of time, however, attendance was mandatory, but she allowed 5 absences. She also offers a lot of extra credit, more than any other professor I've had before.

Professor Ligmann-Zielinska does not teach well and only reads off PowerPoint. She covers stuff we can easily memorize instead of going in-depth on how to do the math and coding the course requires. I am giving her a good review because of how much extra credit she gives. I failed almost every quiz and got a 4.0 truly amazing.

This prof is fine. Sometimes it's difficult to understand her point when she can't find the right words, especially for such a technical class. There is so much extra credit that even if you have no idea what's going on you'll be fine. Very sweet lady, kinda funny. It's easier to pay attention to the recorded lectures so you can go back and listen.
Terrible prerecorded lectures. She does not know how to teach online. I want to pull my hair out listening to her stumble on her words during recordings.

This was all online and she was a professor that didn't understand how to teach online. All lectures were pre recorded so if you were confused you would have to figure it out yourself, which was almost always. But easy quizzes and not stressful course load, just wait to take in person if an option.

Nice and funny professor. The quizzes and exams are all online and you have 24 hrs to take them. Although she said that you don't have time to look at your notes during them since they're timed, you do. I used my notes for every exam and quiz, so have good notes from the powerpoints. She offers reasonable extra credit too.

She's nice but not very understanding at all. You have to read the textbook to begin to even understand the lectures and the textbook is so dense that it's very difficult to grasp the concepts. If you miss a class, you fall way behind and good luck catching up. The lectures are also dense, and you are fighting desperately for participation points.

I dont get why we are letting foreign people become our future professors, its so hard trying to communicate with them and be on the same note. They dont like taking criticism and also think they are always right and not wrong. Simply does not understand how to operate an online class, should stick to lectures irl and be more clearer in the future

I wouldn't take this professor again or recommend her class to anyone. The class instructions are extremely vague and the professor doesn't handle feedback or questions well. Simply giving a 1/5 feels complimentary.

This is by far the best experience I've had with a professor at Michigan State both during not during COVID. The way her MI360 class was structured, I was able to get the work done when I needed to, and I always felt respected and treated like an adult. The textbook is required, but it's honestly good. 10/10 and would definitely recommend.

Kept changing the class rules during the semester; used TA's to walk around marking points; group assignments were awful; class participation was cringey and felt like a fight for points. Overall, great class on how to not teach a class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is a professor who genuinely wants you to be successful, but you will have to show up, participate, and do some studying in order for it to happen. She is very clear with her expectations and sets you up to do well. The quizzes and exams rely very heavily on the built-in quizzes in the online component of the text book. Study those!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: not helpful at all

Professor Arnold is a fantastic person and an excellent teacher. She really cares about the students and wants us to succeed. Attendance is very important, and there is a lot of work, but she grades very generously, and as long as you put in a little work, you'll succeed. She is very understanding and provides excellent feedback on all papers.
Awesome professor! Would totally take this class again, so grateful for professor Arnold. She genuinely cares about all her students and she's extremely passionate about teaching !

She was an amazing professor. She's super caring and respectful. She does a great job of teaching the course. It's extremely easy, you just have to show up. It's basically 5 projects spread out over the course and they're all super easy. She's an amazing teacher and I am so sad that the class is ending. An easy 4.0!! Love her!!!
Beware. This man is a sex offender and got charged with aggravated assault... got found with CP. Great guy though.

professor takes attendance on certain days but tells you at the beginning of the semester. homework is super easy as long as you review the in class assignments. exam is harder, but graded relatively easy. final project is the most difficult and is based on everything you do in the semester, but no final exam.
Amazing professor. Truly about students educational and personal success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He's fine tbh

I originally made a bad review on Professor Gupta. After further consideration, I understand him a lot more. He comes from a great place, definitely has a few issues to work out in the coursework, like the Quizzes being super heavy, and in my opinion drastically different from lecture. Not at all a bad man and really does want to see you learn/win.

Hes not that bad. "Coding on chalkboard" is good because it feels like he is writing it with us and easier to follow. "Errors" that he makes while writing code are very small like spelling something wrong. Grade is based 60% off of weekly quizzes. Lots of extra credit. Sometimes he is grumpy and crashes out most of the time he is pretty funny

A lot of the hate could be mitigated due to his first time teaching. Yes, he can improve on the lectures, and yes the blackboard is tedious. More than half your grade is basically free, all you have to do is the projects and the labs. The quizzes are definitely difficult, and will require thorough reading. Not as bad as they say if you just work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not as bad as ratings say. I've you've taken a coding class before this class should be easy, if not, it'll be a lot harder and you'll have to do a lot more out of class to learn the material. Quizzes are worth a massive chunk of your grade for no reason. Use the TA's to teach you cause they're the most helpful.

Wasn't as bad as people say. Projects and labs were free points. Chalkboard's annoying, but he gives class-wide extra credit for catching his mistakes. Quizzes are tough—I got 60–70s but will still 4.0 thanks to the end of semester bonus project. Not the best prof, but easy to pass.

Pretty chill and lenient with grading. Ok at lecturing SOMEtimes, but often easy to get lost. Homework & lab relies on figuring concepts out on your own and if you have no coding experience that's essentially impossible. TA teaches more in 5 minutes than he does in 40. Extremely disorganized & clearly an inexperienced professor. 

"Oh dear" indeed

About half the grade comes from weekly quizzes, which can be tough if you don't read the recommended textbook. Isn't the greatest, but isnt as bad as everyone says. He isnt too organized, and uses a chalkboard. He makes mistakes, but when pointed out, he gives the whole class extra credit. Really isn't that bad, but def learn on your own. Use chat!

Attendance is not mandatory, only gives bonus points. Labs are mandatory (highest you can get is 50% w/o attendance). I like the chalkboard, it's like he's writing the code with us and lets us learn by catching mistakes. Quizzes covers textbook content. Those who say that it's on stuff he hasn't taught just haven't read the textbook.
Very test heavy and not clear on what tests will be on
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a computer science class, Gupta loves to NOT use his computer. He writes on a chalkboard that's barley visible, commonly gets his own examples wrong, and he takes attendance via a piece of paper that he usually forgets to pass out. The quizzes don't cover what he does and I hope I never have to take another of his classes again.

BEWARE if you take this class, be ready to read code off a chalk board. Ayra, is so funny that he sometimes he doesn't know his own answers. He also has weekly quizzes that everyone fails because the quizzes are topics that he doesn't even cover. Attendance is also mandatory with a piece of paper that you need to sign and he forgets to give it out.

Professor Gupta is quite the guy. Mandatory attendance, and if you miss two quizzes you receive a zero in the course. We didn't have a syllabus until the second class and since then we've had 6? iterations. He is not very good at lecturing or explaining, you won't be able to see his code and even if you could you wouldn't be able to read it. GL!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ashley is caring, fun and genuine. I loved her class and woukd definitely take one of her classes again. She is very understanding and down to earth. Beautiful soul.

I loved Dr. Moore, and I had her for TE101. After reading negative reviews, it seems that people are upset due to the difficult discussions that were had in class, but Dr. Moore was always respectful to everyone while sharing her thoughts, and I never felt attacked or judged. She can be quite opinionated, but once you're used to it, it's all good.
Removed a student from her class for difference of opinions, the TE 101 and 102 classes are a complete joke and waste of time and content.
Had us turn in a rough draft, and then graded it on accuracy. 0/10, wouldn't recommend, would choose a different teacher.

I liked Ashley! She was super sweet and cared about our personal lives, would ask a group question at the start of every class. Class is only 50 min but flew by. Last 6ish weeks are student led presentations. Didn't ever really want to skip this class. Easy homework and the papers aren't bad at all. Would take class with her again any time!
Dr. Moore is a caring and accessible professor. She can be nitpicky with assignments but gives great constructive criticism. She pushes students to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Moore was an amazing professor. I would recommend her class. She grades kinda hard, but she makes the class fun and makes everyone involved.

Strongly recommend having her as your professor for TE-102. She makes the class feel like a community, allowing every student to speak and feel heard. She is very caring and understanding and is willing to give students extended time on any homework as long as they communicate. Amazing lectures, if you plan on taking TE-102 soon, take it with her.

Dr. Barnes Lee is kind, but the class needs improvement. We focused almost only on racism against African Americans without covering other groups or discrimination (sexism, ableism, etc.) and human development. Lectures were mostly her reading slides and the book. Discussions weren't guided and became personal/therapeutic rather than academic.

Dr. Barnes-Lee is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had. The discussions she facilitated were wonderful and productive. She was caring and relatable. Completely unrelated- but she has impeccable style. LOVE HER.

I took her 310 course in Fall 2023. Every time I left this class I felt refreshed and relaxed. She can be a harsh grader, but if you truly believe you deserve a better grade, then she is more than willing to go back over the assignment and see if there were any mistakes in grading. On one assignment, I bumped my grade from a 72% to an 89%.
He could care less if your writing was "good" or not, he just wants you to try your best and write something. Just don't turn in things late, he doesnt like that.

He assigns a ton of work, but he is very nice and grades pretty easily. There were so many different writings/assignments that I stopped trying 3 weeks in. He takes attendance but you have 4 skips. Rambles a lot during class  time but if you  just do the assignments you'll get an easy 4.0.

Professor Astle is an easy grader and likes participation. As long as you complete assignments, you will get a great grade in the class. A lot of busy work, but honestly, it just helps your overall grade in the end. I would 100% take a course with Professor Astle again.
Very good professor, super understanding, very compassionate and super willing to give extensions.

Although he rambles during the lectures, he's very caring and pretty laid back. The class is paper heavy, with not too much time in between papers. There are occasional group projects. He gives VERY detailed feedback. His grading style is weird. Each assignment regardless of size is 2 points, but you can fight for your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's super chill, the lectures are always very fun and while he does ramble a little bit it's usually entertaining or thought-provoking. You will often get out 15 minutes early or be doing individual work for the second hour of the class which I liked. Not a harsh grader and altogether the class is an easy + fun honors credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Astle has easily been the best professor I have ever had. The classes are long but all WRA101 classes are going to be long. He has a great sense of humor and extremely caring to all of his students. Definitely take your writing requirement through him if you can. He is amazing.

Dr. Astle is probably my favorite professor this semester. He gives insightful comments and will gives full credit if you show effort. The only thing is to keep an eye on assignments because there's a lot, especially in class, and you could miss some. He doesn't always remind students of due dates for writing projects so be on top of it.
Way more work than other WRA profs. A lot of unnecessary busy work.

Dr. Astle showed obvious care for his students with his assignments and deadlines. His lectures were philosophical in nature, and honestly had nothing to do with his papers, but he was very kind and thoughtful. You don't really need to go to class to pass, but always keep an eye on assignment deadlines. All assignments are posted online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Astle is a very caring and helpful professor. He gives good and detailed feedback about your writing. We had a lot of mini writing assignments that I think were kind of unnecessary. He also talks a lot during lectures. Classes usually ended pretty early and the exam was stress free.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The professor graded clearly and specifically, but he is very generous. Even though the amount of work assigned was heavy, finish all of them and you have got a sure A. The lectures do not really relate to the work, but they are not mandatory, so your choice. He is also very kind and understanding, accessible and helpful outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a really great prof who grades pretty easily and gives great feedback. As long as you do all of the assigned work you should get a good grade. The course has a heavy emphasis on reflective writing and he focuses a lot on the concepts of intelligence and learning as well. There can be some abstract thinking but I found it to be worthwhile.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is essentially a ton of busy work. The lectures aren't super important, and they are long and boring. As long as you put in decent effort and submit all your assignments on time, then this class is no big deal. Dr. Astle is nice, but he doesn't hand out extensions like candy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: 99% of the class is writing a million mini essays on one topic, which i dont hate at all. the assignments themselves were relatively easy but this dude talks for a very long time while saying so much nothing. 7/10 since class ends early most days
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome class got B+ the only reason why was because I scored 77 on a major assignment but overall great professor . Take this class!!!!!!

Professor Astle was overall great. Did a good job organizing the class and was always willing to help the students. The course work can be time-consuming, but as long as you work hard, you should be solid for this class.
Awesome teacher very caring if ur a freshman highly recommended. If ur not the best at essay he really works with you and cares.
He grades really easy. this lectures don't really matter, and you don't have to take notes. 10/10 would have hime again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really great prof. He gives really good feedback on all assignments and grades pretty easily. Highly recommend him for WRA 101. He really cares about his students and wants them to do well.

I really enjoyed his poetry class, I learned a lot about poetry. Class was built around reading and in-class discussions, with some on-demand writing/annotation exams. I would definitely recommend him as a professor, he clearly knows what he's talking about and is easy to listen to.

Great guy! I took his Gothic course back in freshman year, and it was excellent. Definitely some work, but he's an enjoyable professor who really cares. Sadly, I think he stopped teaching the Gothic IAH course, but he's still a very good and passionate professor. The work and readings can be a lot, but it's manageable.

Professor Arch is a great teacher. He really cares about his students and the material that he teaches. Sometimes it isn't clear as to what parts of the exams or assignments will look like, but it's nothing that should cause a huge issue if you read the books and participate in class. There's a lot of reading, but the books are very interesting.

I have him right now and he is one of my favorite professors I've ever had! Very accommodating and present during class. Makes lectures fun and engaging. I was stuck at home during a snow storm and emailed him and he marked me present for emailing him and told me to stay safe! Cares about shaping the future. I hope he holds off retirement!!

People giving bad reviews probably didn't attend lecture and you guys hating him for no reason. Yes you have to read books and he gives you "2 weeks" but dates has been in syllabus since the beginning. He also changed it a few times because the class changes; mainly people who exploit him. He decided what to change in the syllabus a week before the exam,till now we have had 3 exams and 3 different syllabuses.

reviews.comment: This guy is great. At the start of the semester I thought this would be a boring pre rec but it was actually pretty interesting. The lectures are very interesting and easy to follow. There isn't to much work and as long as you go to lectures and do the assigned reeding the exams are pretty easy.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He gave us 300-page book to read before the finals. He changed the syllabus so many times, with multiple exams. His lectures are so boring and I felt like his lectures are just boring overall. The poetry analysis session was the worst. I felt like the TAs were doing everything in recitation. I was unsure of what he was talking about in his lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He can be funny, and I appreciate how vulnerable he often is. His lectures can be a little boring at times, but he has some really thought-provoking moments. reviews.comment: This was the best class I have taken so far at MSU. Loved the class and the professor even more. He makes everything straightforward and clear as well! Would 100% recommend taking it!

Great insight into literature, but harsh essay crique. He told me he gives a slightly lower grade than deserved so that students will revise. Not a ton of reading for an English class, but when you do, it's a lot at once. Fun lectures and held a pizza party for our last class. Just make sure to do well on the essays as there's not lots of grades.

He picked a lot of texts that were actually enjoyable to read and made it fun. There was a quiz every day but they were pretty easy and he gave most of the answers in the lecture. Honestly, I only read about 50% of what was assigned and got a 4.0. He was a good professor and I enjoyed having him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Taking IAH107 with Professor Arch was a very positive experience. At first, I was nervous about taking a class about gothic literature but this class was exciting! Attendance for lectures was optional but there were 10-point quizzes only available during them. There is a lot of reading but most of it is short stories. Overall, it was a great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: just get ready to read. main grade is quizzes given during each lecture but he pretty much gives you the answers in class.

Great professor, the class has a lot of reading but it's good material so if you enjoy reading you'll love it. The class itself was rather difficult (at least for me) since literary analysis is not easy, and the writings are tough but each has the option for revision and Arch gives great feedback. Mostly discussion & participation based class.

reviews.comment: Professor Arch was a very engaging professor who used many forms of media to keep students interested in the class content.
