reviews.comment: not a bad teacher, but his lectures are boring and the readings are long. sparknotes is your friend. put effort into your essays. overall; boring, but nice pro tip: ask him to draw a map of europe. you will not be disappointed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: As long as you have a general idea about the readings you will do well in the class. Lectures can be boring at times, but slides do have useful information when it comes to the midterm and final. Overall funny guy, and great class.

I did not like this class very much. My TA was very bias and opinionated. His lectures are possibly the most boring thing on this earth. Going to recitation helps a lot. TAs of all the grading. class is mandatory due to the 7b unannounced quizzes over the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Burns was an okay teacher. He had a lot to say about small details and was always going off on tangents that did not make sense. He is an easy grader, but the homework is definitely not easy. Long readings and difficult prompts. Very difficult to understand and is often not helpful when it comes to group work or homework.

Says cool a lot - which automatically makes him cool. I recommend actually reading the material so you know what you're doing. Grades all details and challenges you to improve. NOT AN EASY CLASS YOU MUST WORK FOR IT! Extremely helpful teacher. I recommend taking this if you want to improve your English skills:

Had him for a year, he likes to ramble about small details which maybe mean something to him but not to the class, cares about the content rather than the grammar, digresses into irrelevant topics, wasnt really clear at all, easy A if you use sparknotes to help you get the main idea, using his analyzations in papers  usually gets you an A.

He does seem like he knows the material pretty well, but he repeatedly interrupts group work with random anecdotes and stories that ramble on. He's an easy grader and seems more focused on content than nit picking the grammar and structure of a paper which i like. Can be funny at times, and is way better when you're one on one with him.
Topic was Frankenstein. Was an ok class with a solid professor. No complaints.

I came into the class without any interest in poetry. However, I managed to get a 4.0 because he is very clear about what he wants in the papers and very willing to answer questions. The quizzes were another story, but if you do fine on the papers, it's not hard to do well in the class.

It is very obvious that he knows his stuff. However, he is not very good at coming across clearly to students. Class consists of 1 hour and 20 minutes of rambling information and disorganization. He frequently ignores student questions and is vague on expectations for tests and essays. One of my worst experiences at MSU this far.
He tells you exactly how to get a good grade. If you do those things you can't go wrong. Good teacher.
He tries to make his class fun. Class is very easy if you do what you're supposed to i.e. papers, midterm, and readings. I got a 4.0 and didn't study much.

Although the class itself was boring, the professor was VERY helpful. You could tell he really loved his job and was willing to do anything he could to raise a grade. The downfall was there were 4 books and they are all necessary. He is an easy grader and a funny guy.
Wouldn't recommend taking this class.
Good teacher and willing to help out. He is VERY specific with what you should get out of a poem on tests.
He is a nice man, but very confusing!  It is hard to decipher exactly what he wants from students.
Very Light workload, would definitely take this again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Made writing less harder than it is. So very understading.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is genuinely super easy. I promise most things are completion based and professor burns is great, she is the nicest person I have ever met. Trust I am not the smartest person and I thought it was easy.

Professor Burns is such an incredible human being inside and outside of the classroom. She genuinely cares about your success and mental health. Extremely flexible with due dates and grading. Lectures can be a bit boring but if you try your best, and thats all thats all that matters. Easy 4.0 for sure.

She is nice, but the workload is heavy compared to lot's of other WRA profs. Easy 4.0 as long as you turn in work on time and actually show some effort. Can skip four classes without it affecting your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Burns is a great professor.  She is very understanding and cares about all of her students.  Definitely would recommend!

Absolutely lovely professor that cares deeply about her students. You can tell she is passionate about her teaching and she made me comfortable to explore writing in a way I never had. You are graded mostly on completion but her enthusiasm makes me want to try.
Very thoughtful professor, she cares about all of her students. The class is really easy as long as you don't fall too far behind.

Professor Burns is a breath of fresh air. Not your standard writing class at all. I took the honors option and could not recommend it enough. Really cares about students and is kind and super lenient. You don't need to worry about writing the perfect paper, honestly just try your best and you'll be fine. Take this writing class.
Class was well structured into five units. Lots of group work, peer review, in class instruction. Overall was an easy class and I was set up to succeed.
they are amazing. get ready to be in one of the best proffesors' class in MSU. its an easy 4.0 if you have good relations with the professor. i was in her honors section.

Gave really good feedback and commentary on each project/essay. Her class was very organized and the grading scale was very clear. Would take another class by her. Very considerate of each of her students. 
Projects were not too difficult and was given plenty of time to complete.

What an amazing person, and fun class. I recently took this class as one of my prerequisite classes thinking that it was going to be boring and a chore. What I didn't realize was how good Prof. Burns is at making a "boring writing class" into something enjoyable and entertaining. I 100% recommend her to anyone that needs to take this class.

I took her class over the summer asynchronously but you end up interacting with her a lot. She gives lots and lots of really good feedback and is very accessible outside of class. The projects are pretty deep so be prepared to write about yourself but don't worry, there is so much breathing room for what you can write about. Overall GREAT Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a sweet person, very understanding and open to suggestions. She always makes sure you understand and will help you with anything. Class is smaller so definitely more group work/collaboration during class compared to lectures.
She is accommodating and nice. And if you ever need anything, she is very open-minded, especially with projects and deadlines.

Least unit work per credit for any class I've ever taken. However, it gets hard sometimes because you are supposed to write about personal topics. That's the only thing I hate about this class. It has to be about you. What if you hate yourself right now, but want to become different in the future? You will be reminded of your negatives.

since the class sizes are similar to in high school, she is able to get to know her students a bit better than other professors and gives great feedback on your papers. Most of your class time will be spent on your writing assignments so there is basically no homework outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor never has a clear schedule or assignment list. You have to use four different websites for content. Tophat is used for mandatory attendance. She is passionate but demeaning.

I greatly enjoyed Dr. Burnleys class, I don't understand her low rating. Get to know her and you'll do way better in this class. It is lecture heavy and we use a ton of different websites, but the pop quizzes you can do with your friends. And beware of group work! Plus all the movies we watched were great!

Burnley is a kind and approachable professor. She grades generously as long as you carefully follow the rubric. Attendance is required through Top Hat, and her lectures are heavy. Most days she'll talk for the full time. All quizzes are online and unproctored, but group presentations make up a significant portion of the course. It's a an easy 4.0

Easy class, boring lectures. Get a good group together, and you will receive the easiest 4.0 of your life. Be prepared to spend some money on software to do attendance and some work with (tophat). The lectures feel excessively long, and as previously stated, are boring. She is a very lenient grader, follow the rubric and you will do very well.

She seems like she is very nice, but the overall class is just VERY boring. If you hate group projects, you are in for a ride. Majority of the class is just sitting through the most boring lectures ever, and attendance is mandatory... If you have a good group then the work is fairly easy, but be prepared to read and watch things outside of class

This class would be interesting if it wasn't so mind numbingly boring. No one pays attention in this class and it is only easy if you have a good group, its all group work. She gets off topic easily and is really opinionated. Attendance is mandatory so you have to go to her lectures which is irritating because you don't learn much from her.
Extremely boring and long lectures I honestly sat on my phone the whole time but it isn't too hard of a course I got a pretty easy 4.0.

Sandy is lovely, class is...not. The 3 platforms are super confusing and if you get a horrible group like I did- get ready to WORK. I definitely could've done better if I actually showed up to class but the lectures are mind numbing. Great content, poor execution. Would take again knowing what I know now, but take a different ISS if you can.

Class is hard to follow. The use of 3 platforms is very confusing and hard to keep up with. No one in the class know what is going on. She's nice but wouldn't recommend as a professor. You aren't told when you have homework or a quiz you're just expected to magically know when you have it and when it's due. I would recommend avoiding this class.

uses many diff websites for work in every class it was confusing and annoying, would post many discussions but never a prompt, hard to know whats expected. participation is heavy and lots of quizzes, she was a nice women but got off topic sometimes, engagement was hard, over all the class was easy but an 82% in the class is a 2.0 grade. no tests.

Lecture was boring more often than not and the 3 different platforms for assignments were annoying to keep up with, but I barely showed up to class and still managed to get an A. 
As a person, Professor Burnley is a delight once you get to know her! As a professor...I'd pick a different ISS if you can. I'd take it again if I had to though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. I am typically a 3.8 student, and this class ruined my gpa, the professor uses 3 different platforms and the questions on all tests are confusing. Not to mention lectures are long and boring.

Class is easy but very boring, but caught Burnley and her TA literally laughing at my group's presentation we were doing, while we were doing it. "they clearly don't know what they're talking about" Um... it's a 100 level course and I am literally doing a presentation about coal right now. Nobody in this room knows what they're talking about.

It was a really easy class, an easy 4.0. It was very lecture heavy, but she wasnt the worst teacher ever. There are a lot of group projects that are graded by your classmates, so you want a good group. The lectures are just really boring and hard to pay attention too, and you have to go because she takes attendance.

Very easy class, you watch movies then discuss sociological issues depicted. The idea of the class is interesting, but the lectures are very boring and they rarely relate too much too the movies. Ideas are not revolutionary, despite being treated as such. Easy class, but not terribly interesting.

She wasn't a bad professor but she wasn't particularly good either. the lectures are extremely boring and the topics are simple but she acts like they're revolutionary. The group projects are the worst part especially because the way others rate you on it affects your grade and if you come to her with problems in the group she barely does anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Main thing is TONS of group projects. The content itself is very strange, kinda tries to focus on too many things at once. Overall, the weekly quizzes are pretty difficult, but her grading of the group projects is lenient. ATTENDENCE MATTERS! Essentially, it comes down to if you get a good group, your set. If not you're in for a rough semester.

Very easy and straightforward class. Lectures were boring, quizzes are open note and online. You get weekly discussion submissions on PackBack. There were two big group projects. My main horrible experience about the class is the people in my group. They always procrastinated and I always had to push them to hurry and they never spoke to me.

Very very sweet, but was incredibly boring. Theres two group assignments worth most of your grade which is annoying. Attendance is mandatory and you only get three unexcused absences. Honestly just slept in her class every day.
the class was alright....only thing i despised was packback and the group projects other than that professor Burnley was cool

A lot of people on here don't like this professor, and I don't really understand why. Her class was pretty chill. While I do give some people benefit of the doubt with her quizzes because those are hard to get a high grade on, the rest of her class is pretty easy to pass. All you have to do is show up, do the pack backs, and you get an easy 3.0 :)

This course is extremely unorganized, and the grading criteria is never clear. The quizzes are always about something completely different than what we discussed in the lectures. I would not recommend taking this course with this specific professor.

I am not sure why she is rated so poorly! I took ISS 215 and I loved it. Despite if you like the material or not I think she was a great professor and had a lot of personality! The class was a pleasure to take. At times the material could seem a little silly but I wont reflect that on her because the class is a university requirement. Easy 4.0.

Since ISS is a graduation requirement, people with no interest take it and then rate her low. She is not a bad professor and truly cares about what she teaches. The class was super easy, so it can get boring sometimes. The quizzes were annoying, and the final and midterm are both group projects, but you'll be fine just do your work.

I had Professor Burnley for ISS215, she is very enthusiastic and I found lectures to be interesting! However, you'll work in a group for your midterm and final. My grade ended up relying on people who never came to class, never communicated, cheated, attempted to steal work, etc. If you have a good group you should be fine, but that's up to chance.

This class feels like having a mildly annoying friend who's really passionate about something you could care less about. You want to be polite and listen but it's really hard to pretend like you care. But the class is pretty easy and at least she's nice.

Every time i went to the class i had no idea what is going on. Most of the whole class is talking about actually nothing, projects are all over the place, and as well as the d2l page is not good either, i don't recommend this Professor at all.

Professor Burnley is a decent professor, the work is not super hard, but it is tedious, and the material is pretty useless. The final is not super hard like everyone here is talking about, but it is really oddly made for a class such as this. Everything before the final is mind numbingly easy and you can get away with skipping most lectures.

Idk what these other reviews are talking about. This was the easiest class ever if you don't slack. It was confusing at some times just because the topics don't go together, but that doesn't matter. It's interesting nonetheless. There are 3 or 4 group projects and a few quizzes that are open note, so make sure to take notes in class. She's so nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes that had questions we did not go over the class, group project and most students don't care.
Dr. Burnley lectures are very long and heavy. Her explanations are very confusing. The class is extremely project heavy! Take notes in her lectures because you will need them for the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most confusing classes I've taken. Nothing makes sense, the lectures are so boring, the quizzes are hard, and have questions that aren't from the slides. All the projects are group based, so be ready to have lazy group members. She was very nice and is highly intelligent, but her forced opinions and grading is awful.
Horrible

Horrible professor. Could tell she tries to hard to be liked and 'woke' but it comes across as forced. She will make her opinions known and argue if you disagree. Class material was disorganized and confusing in terms of order. Heavily group projects, which can be good or bad. Lost all respect from the class early on. Do not take her if you can.

I don't know if these people took the same course I did because I had a completely different experience. I will admit the lectures were sometimes a little time-consuming but the course is what you put into it. Professor Burnley always tried to make class fun and enjoyable. Quizzes are a bit challenging but overall it was a good class.

Very irritating class. The lectures are useless and not important to anything relevant. Very easy work except she grades the midterms (all projects with a group) pretty harsh. Biggest issue is she makes it impossible to know what is due and when. Everything is hidden in her wreck of a d2l. Unbelievably frustrating.

Do not take ISS210 with professor Burnley. This class is a complete waste of time and jumps around so much I'm not even sure what I was supposed to learn. She is very opinionated during her lectures and makes sure everyone is aware of that. Also the majority of your grade is based on group projects so if you get a bad group you're screwed.

My experience with Dr. Burnley was a good one! I always found her lectures very interesting and she was always good at keeping us focused. She asks for students' opinions on topics and persuades us to engage with her. The quizzes can be a little tough, but they are open-note. Overall, a really nice lady and passionate about  her teaching!

Most of the people who dislike her honestly are just lazy or don't like what she is talking about. I found the class super interesting and easy. My only complaint is the class is super group project-based and a lot of times your group members don't pull their weight. Other than that I really liked this class and Ms. Burnley.

The course is easily 4.0-able if you put in some effort. Very group project based, so be prepared to work with others. Despite what others were saying, I found the final relatively easy as the professor makes a clear template of what lines of code were needed in the website. She is an enthusiastic professor and I would take a course with her again!

Burnley is an okay professor, I didn't understand why her quizzes were set up to have one correct answer when during lectures we talked about multiple point of views. The final group projects (theres a group project for every midterm and then some) was coding a website which didn't make sense for the societal issues and this being an english class.

Didn't have a problem with Prof. Burnley, her lectures were okay and nothing special really popped out. Class has a bit of busy work and group project based. Quizzes had unlimited attempts and overall should be a 4.0 if you just but some effort in.

This class was all over the place. Good luck on the quizzes. She doesn't try and hide her views and her lectures are very opinionated. Lots of class discussions that don't really make sense. 
But, the course is easy as long as you show up (required attendance) and enjoy group work because that is all you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: My experience with Dr. Burnley was a good one, on contrary to all the other reviews. Her lectures were well put together and genuinely interesting. There was a lot to learn about the REAL world and why the world is the way it is today. I recommend this course. The classwork was easy and this course is easily "4.0-able". Overall very positive!

Course was pretty organized for the first part of the semester. However, after the school experienced a tragedy, the course became disorganized, and some projects were likely given due dates that were extended a little too far. The university offered the pass(take credits) or fail(class won't count towards GPA), but course organization still helps.

Do not take this ISS!!!! Unless you want to struggle the entire semester. Hardest class, the readings did not make sense, she did not post slides until before the exam and talked very fast. The last project was CODING??? In a ISS? Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her class was all over the place. Made us buy a book just to read only 10 pages of it. Her class is so unorganized to the point I don't even know what I learned from this class. She absolutely cruises through her lecture slides so you cannot take notes. Coding and creating a website was the final and it was impossible. Avoid at all costs.
was worried going in to the class after seeing her ratings but i honestly enjoyed the class besides the final project. very stupid and had no relation to the course

This course was all over the place. It was not structured at all, half the time I had no idea what we were talking about because it jumped back and forth so much. It was manageable up until our final project where we had to CODE our final. Also there were lots of notes and long quizzes that barely had to do with the material on the slides.

This class was so Woke and her opinion is the right one. It's never a discussion. She isolated me on one side of the room to take shots at my opinion and this is common, where she splits the class into two opinions, picks her side, and destroys the other hopelessly. The other is anyone conservative, right-leaning, or white. Heads-up: retaliation
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is nice, and she knows what she is talking about, but the assignments did not really make sense with the curriculum. There are a ton of assignments with your group, in which was only switched two or three times throughout the entire semester. The final involved coding, which does not make much sense as this is an ISS class.

There was so many projects that we had to do with out group which were okay because you aren't struggling on your own. But what really bothered me was our FINAL was a coding project. As someone with no coding experience this being the final was incredibly difficult, and coding was not taught at all.

This class is not only incredibly useless and only taught as a university requirement, but boring and hard to follow. The many group project and bs assingments get old fast. Straw that broke the camels back was the final requiring coding experience, and she does not even teach how to do it.

From the beginning of the year there was barely structure to the course, the syllabus only gave information regarding the course. You are only assigned projects and quizzes. She gives useless assignment sheets that don't explain the project and the information on quizzes is barely taught. Do not take this course if you want organization.

She is obviosuly a very smart person but it is literally an entry level ISS class that i am pretty sure everyone has to take. Each lesson did not connect to the next and our final project is literally creating a website which also had nothing to do with the class called Society and the Individual so do not take this class it is a pain.

Professor Burnley is a very intelligent teacher which makes me wonder how her class is so bad. The entire class feels like a social experiment to see if anyone has the courage to take the stand against her beliefs. Basically, if you don't agree with her, you're wrong. Also, the lectures are extremely boring and the topics are taught terribly.

Dr Burnley is clearly very intelligent, so the terrible course curriculum seemed intentional. This women spent two full lectures teaching the class HTML so we could make a website. This class was called Society and the Individual, and we spent a week coding. I swear everything she did in this class was apart of some psychological experiment.

Burnley has a good personality but I would not recommend her as a professor. Her class lacked structure and would often go on time-wasting tangents. Very group project heavy and assignments have unclear requirements, purpose, or relation to lectures. The final tests you more about coding websites than about the overall intention of the class.

She overcomplicates every activity and lecture that we do in class, every lecture is about different things/not related, quizzes are hard and there is lots, answers for these quizzes are not in the lecture slides when she promised they would be. Gave us so many projects that had nothing to do with lectures. So much unnecessary work.
didnt learn anything way to much busy work that wasn't beneficial what so ever

Lots of group assignments, groups are made off the CATME surveys. Quizzes are online and she gives unlimited attempts. Easy grader, I've gotten above 90% on all my assignments unless they were late. She likes class discussions but will never force you to speak. The Midterm and Final are both group projects with 10 people in a group.

Save yourself the burden and find a different ISS class to take. Most of the negative comments I read were true, especially the part about her own biases and opinions in the lectures. On top of that, the lectures are often unrelated to work assigned. I only took this class to fulfill a University requirement and though I got an A, I don't recommend

Although she has a good personality and is nice, her lectures are confusing and don't make any sense. In turn, this makes the quizzes and group work pretty hard. The content of this course is beyond boring and is full of woke topics. This has probably been the most pointless class I have ever taken. I don't recommend this class or professor.

+ Good personality, bubbly, personable, has that more casual and down-to-earth style of teaching, lots of open discussion, makes you think, class is pretty easy overall,

-  *Lots* of group work, directions and grading criteria can get to be pretty vague, kinda disorganized at times, 

I'd give the class like a 6.75 out of 10 overall

Absolutely loved this class! The bad reviews are from conservative business major frat bros mad that they had to take a class requiring critical thinking. Prof. Burnley explains complex social issues extremely well and in a concise way. My only complaint is that the course has a lot of group work, which sucks with a bad group.

Thought the idea of the radical left teacher was something overplayed by the conservative media until I meet her Nothing but group assignments and she typically will award a random grade with comments that have nothing to do with the work Received a C for a project we worked hours on and then an A on a project we completed 5 mins before it was due

Almost every single assignment is a group project, sometimes switching groups. The lectures are long and dont really relate to the course / quiz content. I would not take this class again. Although I liked Professor Burnleys personality, the class was not great. I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Horrible professor I would personally never recomend to take. She is irritating, entitled, not understanding, and seems to prioritize her ideals over the success of her students. If you are taking her class, be prepared to mirror her opinions back to her if you want any hope of an A
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't like to read, don't take this class. It's made up of readings then discussions about the readings in class. Not much lecture, and held stimulating discussions. Well informed and a nice lady, I would probably take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not too many assignments and he grades really easy. I didn't do any of the readings and I passed with a 4.0. As long as you show up to lectures you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was very kind and understanding. Be brought candy/snacks in the mornings. He thoroughly enjoys his work and the conversation.

Dr. Burgess was amazing, he brought us snacks for our long lectures and was very understanding and attentive. He cared about his students and about the material that we were learning. Lots of content to engage with though. I would not say it's an easy A, but you will grow as a student and as a person. If you have the opportunity, Terrance is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Burgess is a good professor, but doesn't make this class interesting. We have talked about the same thing for the past 10 weeks. I have always wanted to be a teacher, but this class has made me want to try a different major. There is readings every week but I have never done them and been fine.

Professor Burbatt is a nice teacher, and cares about the success of her students and the college of engineering. However, EGR 160 as a class is generally boring and is filler content to go alongside EGR100. Just show up and you'll pass
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very Passionate and focused lectures coupled with genuinely helpful information for being successful in a STEM environment. Would recommend to anyone looking to increase their knowledge or networking/communication skills in the STEM field.
Extremely difficult to fail this class, nice teacher, and easy assignments. You can miss a lot of the discussion posts and still get a 4.0 because of the easy extra credit activites.
She is very nice and can be very flexible with you and is very friendly. Very great professor and she basically made it impossible for you to fail her class.
This class was very easy, minimal work. And the instructor is friendly.

This professor is honestly one of the greatest professors I've had at my time at MSU. She is incredibly laid back and funny and knows what she is doing. One of the easiest 4.0's you can ever get. In her class, you literally have to TRY to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Bump is overall a great professor! You can tell he really cares about his students' success and I would say to get a 4.0 in his class, all just got to show up for peer feedback and presentation days. His class is definitely designed to encourage creativity and work on skills you already have, as he doesn't set strict project or grading guidelines.

Dr. Bump is amazing, one of the best professors at the university. He was always amazing in class and available outside of class as well. The grading criteria was always very clear. If you can take wra101 with Dr. Bump.

My favorite professor/teacher of all time. I love Bump. Super down to earth and my favorite class of my first semester. He immediately learns your name and goes around the class each day to check in on your life outside of his class. Extremely flexible. Assignments are hefty, but are easy if you follow the rubric.
very interesting man, once ordered pizza for the whole class. Liked him but if you're very introverted and shy I wouldn't recommend, it's a very social class.

This class is completely about you and your experiences. We wrote "stories" about our life and the work in this class was more about outlining the assignments more than the assignments themselves. Bump is the most laid-back professor you will ever meet who takes the time to connect with each student and truly cares.
Very good teacher actually cares about his students and makes each class fun. Treats his students as equals and if you are open and honest he understands. 10/10
Prof. Halbritter was one of the best professor I've had. As long and you meet the paper requirements you will do well. If you get the chance to have him as a professor, take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Believe me when I say that Bump is the best professor I have EVER had! He is truly the man.Most of the grading in this class is completion. Bump is the fairest most reasonable professor I have ever had. The best part about Bump is that he talks to you and treats you truly as a friend. You will 4.0 this class as long as you show up and do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Uncle Bump was my first professor at MSU two years ago. He is so caring and wants his students to succeed. I had done so bad on one of my papers and despite the deadline, uncle Bump gave me extremely good advice and guidance and let me turn it in late. His goal is to much sure you succeed. Don't think twice about enrolling in one of his courses.

I don't usually do these but Dr. Bump is by far the most caring professor I've had at MSU. He is one of those professors that genuinely loves their job and wants nothing but the best for his students. I highly recommend him because he's truly impacted my life and I didn't even care about writing prior to this class. Best class I've had.

Doesn't ask hard questions on the weekly quizzes, just make sure to pay attention in lecture. He definitely knows what he's talking about, and you'll get a lot out of his class.

It has been 4 years since I took this class, but it's still the first that comes to mind as my favorite. Cesario is a fantastic lecturer and the class is so engaging and entertaining. I wish I could take it again, no joke.

The only grades in this class are weekly quizzes and a final exam. Professor Cesario is a great lecturer and makes the concepts extremely clear. He keeps you engaged as well. I skipped a lot of class and still four pointed. As long as you study past quiz questions for the final exam, you'll be fine. It was a fine class, Cesario is a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: All you are graded on is weekly quizzes and a final. I'm a bad test taker so this makes it hard to be successful.

I'm a psych major, so going in I knew this class was going to be important to me. Cesario made lectures interesting and easy to understand, which made coming to his class even better.  Show up to lecture and you're set. He also gives out extra credit for those who attend lecture on random days.
Amazing lectures, very funny professor.  Gives many extra credit opportunities, content is fun to learn about.

Great class and subject matter, super fascinating and great for learning about the world. Teaches it well and genuinely cares about material. All lecture, lots of time to ask questions, no mandatory attendance, and does offer some extra credit. Grades based on open note online quizzes and a final. Reading not really necessary. Not too difficult.
One of the best professors I've ever had.
Really gets you involved and interested!
Cant say enough about Prof Cesario. Great guy. Lectures are usually entertaining and fly by. Exam questions are pulled right from the lectures, and assigned readings.   Highly Recommend
Super cool guy and gives interesting and funny lectures. Great professor!

I loved this class! If you show up to lectures and take notes you should be able to pass easily. He is super funny, he cares about his students, and his lectures are easy to understand. Plus he gives extra credit and drops your lowest exam! He really relates content to the students. One of his GA's made a big google doc before exams that helped too

I really enjoyed having professor Cesario as a teacher. He made the material very easy to understand and was clear. His lectures were generally pretty easy to stay engaged in and he employed many real life examples. In addition, on many occasions he even engaged the class in different optional participation experiments to provide the class withdata

He is HANDS DOWN the funniest/most inspirational professor/teacher I've ever had. Every single lecture is full of funny real-world examples of concepts that make 300+ students laugh. Everything is very applicable to your own daily life, and this class allows you to understand yourself and your life on a deeper level that VERY few classes do.

The method of teaching was a lot of doing all the learning outside of class then coming to class to do practice. Her method of teaching just did not click with me as a student who needs in-depth explanations for difficult topics. Not a super hard class but if you want in-depth explanations I would recommend trying a different professor.

I had her class when jamboard was used. Course was flip model, so we worked on materials during class and learned the stuff at home. It was lots of team involvement so pray you have a good team. Most of her exams was very hard since she was picky with the answers. She is seriously one of the harder prof for first years taking intro to chem.

I had Dr. Cass for both chem 2 and my senior seminar, and she is such a warm and caring professor. Her grading criteria is very clear and she is willing to make exceptions when necessary. She encourages thoughtful conversation and engagement with course content and going to her class was always pleasant.

Dr. Cass really wants her students to succeed and if you put in the work, you will be able to 4.0.  Exams can be hard but there is enough extra points with HW and other assignments to cushion your grade. She has really good lectures and explains things well! Very helpful outside of class as well.

The exams this semester were insanely difficult and always had questions we never saw in class or on the mock exam. But there were retake opportunities to bring your grade up which I really appreciated. Got mad at class when everyone did bad on a question instead of realizing that the reason we did bad was because we never saw a question like that.

Exam heavy, lectures are mandatory. Some of the exams were super tough and included material that was briefly covered. There are far easier professors in the Briggs program that offer tons of extra credit and aren't nearly as exam heavy. If you aren't a good test taker don't take this course!

I had LB 171 with her as well and I don't know what changed but class genuinely class began to feel hostile, I know she had personal issues but I do not believe that is grounds for yelling at a class who got low grades (consistently low grades is a teaching problem not a learning problem). Take LaDuca if you can (he guest lectured a few times).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't get me wrong, Cass is not a bad professor at all. She has years of experience in chemistry, however exams can be something else. If you haven't taken AP Chemistry in high school , I would try to take CEM 141/142, which is the natsci sequence. Taking LB chem it is implied that you have a very good understanding of chemistry from high school.
Dr. Cass is the best professor at Lyman Briggs. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Her lectures are actually helpful and her teaching style is top tier. Highly recommend.

Even though the content may be hard, 3.5/4.0 is easily attainable if you put the work in. I will forever preach Dr. Cass's name--she is the best prof in all of Briggs. Take her for any class possible. Her lectures are engaging, she teaches you well, and she is an amazing person. No hesitation, choose this prof.

She is a hard grader on exams, and even though she says that it's based on the work you do, not the answer, she's most definitely lying. I've lost a ton of points because I got a first question wrong, and the subsequent questions were based on it so I got zeros for those, even with the right process. You can do it, but good luck.

Dr. Cass is a great professor who really cares about her students. The course is team-based, so your experience depends a lot on your group. Take advantage of her office hours - they're super helpful. Unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for exam prep.

Although Dr. Cass wasn't the right professor for me, she did everything she could to help the people in class that needed it. She always recorded her lectures and posted them. The exams were heavy, but Dr. Cass always had plenty of prep material posted so you could prepare as much as you needed

This woman made me rethink if I am worthy of an education. She acted so biased towards the men in my class and I truly had no problem with it until she used my womanhood to undermine not only me but also my education. I never expected this from a university professor, nonetheless a woman in this day and age. Frankly disappointed and flabbergasted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is a hard grader and tests are tough, but don't be scared! She is AMAZING. You will not be confused and if you are, she is extremely accessible and will do everything to help. Homework is pretty light (there's not a lot; it's mostly completion grades) and it's never just busy work. Every time I thought I wasn't going to be prepared, I was wrong
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass definitely knows what she is talking about. She is amazing at answering questions and explaining in a way that is understandable. Her exams can be difficult and very comprehensive, all written/no multiple choice. If you study hard and go to class you will be successful. Would take her again.

I loved Dr. Cass's teaching style she genuinely cares about whether her students understand the material or not and is often available for office hours. She provides lots of content for exam preparation and allows for exam retakes at the end of the semester to attempt to improve your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass definitely knows what she's teaching. Very approachable and transparent about expectations. No final- you can retake up to 3 individual exams- that being said you do have to take team exams which cannot be retaken. Recitations are mandatory. If you cannot make it to class she has annotated slides and lecture recordings. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass is a great professor. She definitely knows what she's doing. It's best to go to lectures because you have a group, but she posts annotated slides and lecture videos. Recitation points are attendance-based and groupwork. The class is test-heavy, but instead of a final you can retake up to three individual exams, but not group exams.

I would consider her a good professor, but she is very test heavy and homework heavy, and does not really cover what is on the homework in class. The most inconvenient thing about her is that she is a harsh grader, and makes you meet for 6 hours with the ULAs who are rarely available.
Overly demanding requires you to spend 6 hours with peer mentors over the semester, which makes sense until it gets messed up and you have to do double the work. I do not recommend it it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass is a good lecturer; I would advise to go to class even though she posts videos, because you will work with your group. You will have individual exams as well as a group exams. Exams are very comprehensive and math heavy but I felt prepared most times. The pre-class activities are worth actually attempting and not skipping over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass was great! She really tries to help all of her students succeed and makes it possible to do so. The final exam gives you a chance to retake up to three previous exams which is very helpful as well. She does a great job of explaining content in lectures, and will take time to meet with you outside of class if you need extra help.
Dr. Cass is a great prof but the class is very team based so that could make or break your experience

Dr. Cass is an excellent professor! Course is really team-based heavy, so pray that you have a good team for the team project and team exams. Make sure to attend her office hours because they offer amazing tips and insights for exams. If you took AP chemistry, this course will be a breeze for you. Those who didn't, ask a lot of questions.
This was one of my favorite professors!
One of the best professors I have ever had. Really cares about student wellbeing and teaches content with passion. Totally recommend!

Dr. Cass is a very strong lecturer and she explains things conceptually. This is reflected in her exams which tend to be very concept heavy. Overall, she is a great professor to take chemistry from. Definitely recommend for LB 171 and LB 172.

Dr. Cass was one of the best teachers I have ever had. Even though during the middle of the semester I had around a 83%, I had brought it up to a 4.0 by the end because of much she helped. Her lectures are so helpful and the preclass is helpful at times. If you had to pick a teacher for gen chem, pick her. I took her again for chem 2.

Dr. Cass is an amazing professor. She makes herself available for help often. Her syllabus and expectations are very clear and easy to follow. It can be a lot of work, but it is well worth it. No busy work that made me think "Why am I doing this?". Aside from being an amazing professor, she is just a very kind and funny person.

I highly enjoyed Dr. Cass. She is a great lecturer and gives lots of time during class to work with groups on practice problems so you know what you're doing. If you do all of the free points, it is very realistic to 4.0 this class. Also, there is no final and you can retake other exams. I highly recommend her, definitely the best LB 171 professor.

Best teacher for Chem 1. Lectures were extremely helpful to explain the concepts in the preclass activities. Very friendly and easily reachable for questions and help over email and during office hours. Difficult tests but retake opportunities during finals week made them easier. ULA office hours made concepts easier to understand.

Best professor for gen chem. Students from other professors would skip class to come listen to hers because she taught so well. Super funny professor and is very understanding and reasonable. The tests however are very hard, you just have to find a study strategy that works best for you.

Dr. Cass is one of the best chem professors at LB. She posted lectures and had available zoom office hours in D2L. She deeply cared about the students and often stayed after class to elaborate on lectures. Chemistry is hard enough so ofc this class won't be so easy. Mock exams aren't really similar to real exams, so study with other resources.

She was a great lecturer. Explained things very well and by far gave the best education for LB chem. Exams are SO tough tho. So fast paced and tricky. But overall a really quality job teaching and provides more opportunities to practice than many other profs. Take her if you want the best foundation for all other chem classes. Great person overall

Doctor Cass is a great professor for chemistry. She is someone that is great at teaching Chemistry at lyman briggs. She is the best one by far. The class is very challenging however, you need to put in the work in and study a lot to do great in her class.

LB171 was way too difficult for an INTRODUCTORY chemistry class IMO. Exams are harder than in class work and pre-class videos are useless. If you're up for a challenge or love chem, take this Prof's LB171. If not, take gen chem. It ultimately still counts for credit in Lyman Briggs - even if your advisor tries to imply otherwise.

She makes you watch youtube videos for the pre-class and that is how she teaches. There is useless workshops that are REQUIRED and a total waste of time. The entire lecture time is doing jamboards with your group. This class is the reason I am dropping out from Lyman Briggs. Don't even think about asking a question because she is passive aggressive

She is a good professor when it comes to teaching, however you need to pay attention because she moves fast. Exams are really difficult, so be ready to study a lot. I would study 15 hours per exam and get 70s. Try to pay attention and ask questions if you need help.

She was nice but if you need ANY test accommodations, tell her way ahead of time. I had to take a group exam on my own due to a doctors appointment(even with a VISA, I couldn't get the exam taken a different time.) Lots of extra credit. She's very approachable with questions and isn't judge-y at all.

pre class activities are not good and dont help with learning. youre expected to know the content when you get to lecture. spend 70% of lecture doing group jam board problems that aren't helpful. extremely hard exams nothing like the practice ones from class.

Dr. Cass is awesome!! Pre-class activities are where a bulk of learning happens, so those can be a little tough, but she always goes over the material in class and gives us plenty of practice. The tests can be hard, but I would say she prepares us well for them. She is one of the best profs I have ever had.
Cass is awesome but her tests are so hard. Ive heard a lot of people saying that it makes later chem courses super easy but not sure if it is worth it yet...

If you do not have a good foundation in chemistry, you will most likely have a harder time since the basics are taught through short preclass assignments and she goes over harder material in lecture. Go to office hours, she goes a lot slower there. Expect hard exams. Grading is fair and you can earn many points to make up for bad exams.

A really good and easy to follow teacher. You can tell she is passionate on the topics and making sure her students succeed. Attendance isn't required but I heavily recommend going to all as the topics can be hard and you can fall behind easily. Exams can be pretty hard so expect a decent amount of studying.

Dr. Cass is a strong lecturer which is reflected by her hard exams. Exams are a good part of your grade, and deeply understanding concepts is crucial (1 exam and 1 group drop, including final exam). Extra credit awarded if you do all pre-classes and recitations. Studying after class is a must, she goes quickly. A 4.0 is achievable with good effort.

The only way to 4.0 this class is to put in a lot of work outside of lecture each day. The exams were difficult, and not similar to the mock exams. To prepare for exams, rewatch her lecture videos! She does drop two exams (1 individual and 1 group exam) and offers 15 points extra credit if you do all pre classes, and attend all recitation.

Avoid if at all possible. Exams were extremely difficult. Many out of class activities were much harder than they had to be because of a lack of explanation. Cass could sometimes be quite rude with students. If you're not a chemistry or bio major, check with a Briggs advisor about taking CEM chem rather than Briggs chem; it's likely much easier.

Professor Cass's class was the highlight of the week! Her teaching style and ability to engage students in class made learning easy. Her willingness to help students in and outside of class is amazing. The exams will require many hours of studying, but mastery of the material is definitely possible if you pay attention in class and ask for help.

Cass is a great teacher with an amazing personality that keeps everyone engaged throughout her lectures. The tests are difficult, but all the material is covered in class/mock exam. You also get a drop exam which can include the final! If you attend office hours and put in the effort, you will get a good grade.

I came into this class already taken a year of honors chem and AP chem in high school, and struggled in this class. Her test are much harder than any of the other teachers that teach this class, and she thinks that a 70 is "good" on tests. If you do not have a GREAT understanding of chem from high school, DO NOT take this class.
Prepare to learn all of the material by yourself

Cass is such an amazing professor. She truly cares that you learn and are able to apply the knowledge you learn. Although she is a great professor, her exams are honors exams so they are much more difficult than the other teachers.

DO NOT take Cass. Her Rate my prof reviews are old, class is much harder. She goes over the material very fast and is extremely test heavy. Her tests are very hard, and she admitted that she makes her test really difficult. She wastes 2/3 of the class with useless Jam-boards. Be prepared to put in 10+ hrs of work outside of class each week.

She is very loud during lecture, and is very test heavy. She claims in class that a 70 average is good on exams. She also admitted that she purposely makes her exams more difficult. She goes over the mock quiz the day before the exam and got upset when another professor went over the mock days before the exam. She expects you to know the material.

I came into Cass's class hearing that she did an incredible job, and although she is a decent teacher, her exams are unfathomably difficult. Other professors have exams that have been deemed easier and more fair, but Dr. Cass is a difficult grader and her exams do not help. I have never been more frustrated with a class in my life.
Super personable and helpful

-Exams are more difficult than what is on the mock exam/most of the lecture slides and practice problems.
-There are concepts/problems that students weren't taught ot made aware of until the mock exam came out.
-Mostly self study
Definitely a great professor as her explanations were clear. The work is challenging but La's and the prof are always there to help.

DO THE PRECLASSES. Cass is great at explaining things, class is split half lecture half group work. this year we had quizzes every other friday, where we took a 40 min individual quiz and a 20 min group quiz, so hope for a good group. go to recitations, the LA's answer your questions and you get free points.

Cass is a really nice professor, but a little overrated. Pay attention to the lectures and the preclass materials and you should be fine. Quizzes were very fair. She definitely cares about her students and is easy to approach.

Dr. Cass is the best chemistry professor at Lyman Briggs. Her quizzes are comparatively easy with most questions from mock quiz. She is a good explainer and is willing to re-explain things during office hours. She is very approachable and would always make sure the material is understood. I will definitely recommend her.

Doctor Cass is truly wonderful! She cares about her students, and she is always responsive and engages the class well. Content is definitely difficult, but Dr. Cass teaches in a way that everyone can understand. I had her for LB171 and LB172, and she was my favorite professor of both semesters! Take Chem with her!!

Dr. Cass is a very kind professor. Lecture was beneficial, but you should expect to study outside of class. Although there are lots of quizzes, expect them to be difficult. Office hours are also helpful. Overall she is a great prof but the class is hard in general so expect to put in some work.

She is a very sweet teacher and answers questions but is also really loud during lecture. She also is very messy when teaching, is confusing, and does not really teach well. Her lecture seemed all over the place this year with a lot of low averages for quizzes because lectures were not clear. Be prepared to spend hours studying outside of class.

I absolutely loved Dr. Cass and would definitely recommend her.  She is very easy to talk to and does an excellent job of answering questions. The class was also very organized and her lectures are interesting and easy to follow.  LB 171 is a challenging course, but she does such a good job of helping students actually understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cass is a pretty good teacher for LB 171. She does lecture a lot and there is a lot of content to learn but she is very clear when she lectures and offers plenty of resources to help her students. She is very good at explaining things in a way that her students will understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Cass is fine. I felt she wasn't as straightforward as I'd like. When I took the course FS2020 lecture time was mainly group work which wasn't super helpful but that changed halfway. Her lectures are fine but she takes her time getting to the point. Fair grader and fair quizzes though. Mock quizzes are the best prep.
She is such a good explainer and is willing to re-explain things during lectures. She is very approachable and would always make sure the material is understood.
Dr. Cass is phenomenal. Lectures are very helpful and grading is straight forward

Cass is pretty strict, and the class is super group heavy, so you work with your group a lot on practice problems; at these times I would prefer more lecture so the concepts can be clear. If your group is bad, you're going to be relying on yourself. I would say Cass is your best bet in how she teaches, but just don't annoy her. Content is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Cass is super understanding and flexible. She's one of the most understanding professors I've had and deserves so much! She is a great professor and made chemistry so much easier.

Dr. Cass is a great professor. I struggled quite a bit with some of the topics, but she explains them well, and posts all of the slides and notes used in class. My only complaints are her office hours are crowded, so don't expect much individual help through them. Also, her online quiz windows were weird (8amFriday-5pmSaturday), but not horrible.
Homework is always way harder than what we learn in lecture; also, Dr. Cass does not have good communication with the lab prof for the lab portion of class. Nice teacher though.

Dr. Cass is a great professor! LB 172 is definitely a challenging course. If you don't put the work in, you won't do well. However, Dr. Cass truly cares about her students' success. She is always willing to answer questions and do everything possible to ensure you succeed. Like I said though, you have to be willing to work hard to do well in class!

Dr. Cass is a great choice for LB172 or LB171. Be prepared, LB172 is harder than 171, but Dr. Cass makes the Cass VERY manageable. Her exams are not cakewalks and you need to have a good idea about what you are doing. There is not really that much homework for her LB172 class, I would HIGHLY recommend taking notes for pre-classes 1 week early.

Dr. Cass is a great professor. The class was fully online and she did really well. Her practice tests and office hours are super helpful and she gives really good feedback. She is also very good at making sure everyone's questions get answered and will spend extra time going over the hard stuff in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really good professor-lectures were easy to follow and she was really good at preparing students for the quiz. Really easy to contact her as well outside of class as well for any concerns or issues.
Cass was a great professor, she is extremely thorough in lectures and great a giving test prep materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Almost every single class was put into breakout room groups to work on new concepts with little explanation of the concepts themselves. A nice professor but I definitely wish we had more time as a class to go over things and ask questions instead of having to wait with a raised hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Chemistry was pretty hard for me but Dr. Cass is great at explaining concepts. Don't be afraid to go to office hours for help and make sure to do any practice work assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I don't even have Dr. Cass, but I watch her lecture videos instead of my own professor's lectures. She is very informative and straight forward. She can make complex units seem simple and easy to understand. She is also a very nice person and seems to really care for her students.

Cass is difficult to understand at times, so going to office hours and every recitation is super important to understand content. Chem 2 was by far, way more difficult than chem 1, so be prepared for that. Cass also hand writes all her notes on the board so if you don't write super fast, chances are you'll miss content & it won't be covered again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: LB 171 is a difficult class as it is. Dr. Cass makes chemistry interesting, and she cares about the subject. She requires lots of work but getting a good grade is very possible. I wish she taught LB 172 when I was there!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass is a great professor. You need to attend office hours and thoroughly comprehend the material to succeed in this class. Missing one class is very tough. Dr. Cass is always willing to answer your questions and truly wants you to do the best you possibly can. Put in the effort, you get results.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass really has a passion for chemistry. LB171 is a tough course, no doubt, but if you want to have a professor that will go in depth about the concepts this is your prof. She does a nice job of connecting everything together and always asks if we have any questions after finishing explaining a topic. Her online office hours are also helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cass is a good professor and her exams are well organized compared to Barnards. Cass tries her best to explain concepts, but it is her personality that annoyed me. In my opinion, she's annoying and too loud.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass is the BEST prof anyone could ask for! She is always willing to help clear anything up and is always looking for student success. Chem is definitely a super difficult class but she makes it well worth it. She also makes it very clear what you're doing wrong through feedback! If you ever get the chance to take Cass DO IT!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: IF U TAKE LB171 U WANT TO TAKE IT WITH CASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I recommend you dont take her ever!!!! N She expects you to understand conceptual knowledge of a topic on her level and yet never goes over any conceptual concepts. Toughest grader and tests, and your whole grade really depends on them. If you expect to get a 4.0 towards med school take a general chemistry class. Taking this class is a mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Go to office hours. They help so much. Study. Study. Study.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass is the best professor of the Lyman Briggs chem profs. She is so nice and willing to help you if you reach out to her. The class isn't easy, but I found her exams fair and she never tries to trick you on purpose. I would definitely take Dr. Cass again and I wish I had her for chem 2!!! If you can take her, I would recommend it !!

Dr. Cass is the best teacher I have ever had in my life. She is very kind and will be willing to help you as much as she can. She has a Motherly approach and truly wants you to succeed. The class itself is very difficult. Be sure to do your work and practice practice practice.

Dr Cass is absolutely amazing!! As everyone has stated, this class definitely makes you work for the grade. The material is tough, the class moves at a fast pace, don't compare this to the typically CEM 141 class-- we cover more material than them. Dr Cass is very approachable, is always open to offer help, and her lectures are straight forward!

Dr. Cass is one of the best professors at LB. She is very clear and will explain topics to the best of her ability. Highly recommend office hours, even if you're not struggling. The class is difficult but she has a genuine interest that her students do well. Highly recommend her.

Dr. Cass is definitely the best prof of the LB171 lecturers. She is very clear in her explanation and it is very apparent that she cares for her students. This class is really difficult, but if you go to her for help she will be there for you. She does her best to make chem interesting and easy to follow.
LB171 IS A TOUGH COURSE, BUT CASS IS A REALLY GOOD PROFESSOR AND LIGHTENS THE MOOD. YOU WILL STILL HAVE TO PUT IN EFFORT AND STUDY BUT THANKS TO CASS YOU SHOULD UNDERSTAND EVERYTHING CLEARLY.

If you read before coming to class the lectures will be easier to understand, but Cass lectures very well also. Pay attention and take notes because it will be extremely helpful to study them for tests.
She is the best of the lb171 teachers. She is very helpful, cares about her students, and funny. Don't buy the text book or share with a friend, I never opened mine.

Chem is just a hard class. Everyone likes LaDuca, but I prefer Cass. Although L has a fun lecture, sometimes he is hard to understand. Cass writes everything on the board for notes (you need to be there for them) and uses visuals when you need them. Answers questions during class and has regular office hours. Not above and beyond but pretty good.

If you're struggling with writing notes or understanding fundamental chemistry, Dr. Cass is the instructor that you want to have. She writes EVERYTHING essential up on the board, takes time during class to answer all questions, and always is there to schedule an individual meeting after office hours.  She is awesome and I would recommend her!

Dr. Cass was a really good professor in that she knew what she was talking about and she seemed to care about student learning. The class LB171 though will probably be one of the hardest classes you take, you really have to work for a good grade. Overall, she's the best chem prof you could ask for though!

Cass was very passionate about chemistry and was very straightforward. She was very helpful in office hours. Knows how to joke around. Decent amount of clicker questions. The book wasn't really necessary but definitely helped as reference. Tests were exactly like the mock-exam review.

Dr. Cass is a GREAT prof. She is always willing to help her students and is eager to answer all of your questions. You WILL have to put a lot of time into this class, but its well worth it. She is awesome and as long as you study and ask for help when you need it, you will do fine. I do warn you however, this class is not easy.

Dr. Cass was one of the best professors I have had here at State. She was a great lecturer and really cared about her students. If you didn't understand something, she was really good at making sure you eventually did and offered a lot of outside help. Definitely my favorite professor so far. I had LaDuca as well and liked Cass a lot more.

I've had her for two semesters for LB171 and LB172 and she has been consistent throughout. She knows her stuff and is passionate about what she does. Going into her office hours the first time I was thrown off because she was yelling as she was explaining something to me, but I soon realized she wasn't mad, she likes chemistry.
Not an easy class, but Dr. Cass is a good lecturer and offers lots of help outside of class.
Exams are very straightforward, exactly what you'd expect.  The homework helps you understand concepts.  If you attend class, you'll do fine.
none

Very VERY hard class, but she is great in her office hours. For being her first year she wasn't that great, but in 3 yrs she'll be a great teacher. She enjoys teaching and is in a good mood most of the times, but some kids tried to take advantage of her by talking alot. She was good but nothing Great
Great professor, easy to understand.

Great professor, made chemistry easy. Exams can be difficult, so study hard. Textbook is never specifically used, although it has answers to some of the online problems, so see if you can borrow a friend's book. Come to class: she takes attendance with the CPS clickers, but she will be able to recognize your face and know that you aren't there.

Cass' exams are very challenging, overall the lectures are not. This makes studying essential to do well on the exams. In lectures she strives to make the content clear to the class and constantly askes if everyone understands the ideas.

This class is entirely online and consists of completing assignments through McGraw Hill. There's very little additional lecture material or instructor created content beyond what's on McGraw Hill. The workload is around two hours a week, but it feels more like busy work than meaningful learning. If you want to be taught something, do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was very enjoyable and I learned a lot. It is online asynchronous and the course was broken into three different modules and he gives you lots of time to complete each module. There is also an exam after each module. It is through McGraw Hill and I have had no complaints about this class whatsoever and would absolutely take it again!

A great class. Though everything is done through McGraw Hill so if you don't like that website this might not be a good class for you. It's broken up into 3 modules and you get about a month to do each one. They all have about 5 chapters in them. Very easy and enjoyable class to pass as long as you do the work!

Dr. C was my favorite professor. If you miss a class, you can make it up by attending office hours to get credit for the missed class. If you miss an assignment due date shes very chill about letting you turn stuff in late. I personally liked talking to her during our office hours, and she was always lovely and greeted everyone who entered.

i loved her she was so sweet. Pretty much all WRA101 classes are set up the same so theres not much u can do about the content of the class, but she made it easy to handle bc u get so much time in class to work on the assignments. I went to every class and rarely had to do anything outside of class. i had a 8am but it was worth it to me
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely sweet human and great professor. Gives a lot of time for the work to be done and has extremely clear requirements. She knew every student by name and seems to actually care for them. Very easy class with a very good professor if you even put in like 60% effort you should have no struggle getting a 4.0 this class. Highly recommend

Dr. C is one of the most caring professors I have met at MSU, she is truly interested in your journey as a writer and wants you to enjoy class and learning in general. Also very open to assisting with honors options, or any projects that are of interest to you.

My favorite professor ever, never meant a teacher who cared more about her students. Always would help and wants her students to get a 4.0. If you do the work you will 4.0. Do anything in your favor to get her!
Kind, inspirational, and wise.

Prof Ceaser is very sweet and helps every student. She was also very understanding considering all classes are online right now and made sure each student succeeded in the class. 1000/10 recommend for WRA 101.
Very nice and sweet, will do anything to make sure you have the opportunity to pass the course, makes sure you're doing okay outside of class so she knows why you are struggling (if you are).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: gooood

Excellent instructor. This is not an easy subject and he knows it well. Furthermore, his tests do a good job of determining students' mastery. Unfortunately, many of the students that do poorly in has class lack adequate math/engineering skills/aptitude to take the class and have bad experiences. More unfortunate, many of those students graduate!
He is a very good prof.
His exams are difficult and requires advanced math. He is very helpfull during office hours. He knows his subject very well. Overall he is a good guy.
his exams are difficult. very helpfull during office hours.
The best professor I have ever seen.

I don't understand why he always looks impatiant in class. Always use very difficult exams to show his smartness. After taking one semester of his class, I have to acknowledge this is the worst prof. I've seen.

I had him in the summer.  I rarely went to class but when I did he wasn't very good.  The tests were very difficult but he passed me because it was the last class I had before I graduated.  I guess he's helpful in office hours but I never went to any.
He is just an unreasonable person. He is not even a mechanical engineer! Also his face is full of frowns:( JUST DONT TAKE HIS COURSE!!!
Try your best to avoid this guy. It is a nightmare to take his course.

Ce is a great professor. He speaks in a very slight accent, so it can be hard to understand him at times but it's not that bad. He clearly knows what he's talking about and is very passionate. He goes very slow and can go over the same stuff a lot, but his lectures are still interesting. As long as you pay some attention, you'll pass.
Very engaging and allowed notes for exams

Class is very exam heavy however the midterms are pretty easy. It was the final that was very hard however. He also allows cheat sheets on the exams. There are weekly HW assignments that can be kind of long. Attendance is mandatory because of Clicker but lectures are really boring. He also curved grades for us(cutoff for a 4.0 was a 83%)
Would not recommend. Didn't teach well and practice test did not correlate to exams

Professor was very kind and caring. He rounded up the grades at the end of the semester even though he said he wasn't going to. Homework was easy, lectures were packed but he posts them. I struggles and still passed. Would take a class by him again!

Ce Liu is very efficient in how he runs the class. There are 2 attendance points per class, 1 homework assignment a week, and 3 exams (excluding the optional exam.) The exams are worth roughly 70% of the grade so study up! I am already bad at economics and his teaching style just wasn't for me. He is not very good about answer emails either.

Ce Liu wouldn't be a recommendable professor if economics comes harder for you. On exams, I got a 75% when I played Papa's Pizzeria in class, compared to when I actually listened and studied, I got a significantly lower score. His lectures are very confusing as he spends too much time on the easy questions and too little time on the harder ones.

Liu is a nice guy, and I found his class to be very easy (spent more time reading my emails than anything else in the lectures). The lecture hall is tight for fitting so many students in, and Liu can sometimes not explain things well. But it was an easy class and I would take it again. 4.0 is an 85, so the cutoff is fairly generous.

He seems very passionate about what he teaches but micro is just hard to grasp. I went to every lecture, did all the homeworks, and still scored below a 65% on every exam with each exam being 23% of your grade. Its also in a huge lecture hall and the seats are usually taken up pretty fast, nothing else to note.

Need an 85 to get a 4.0, not as easy as it sounds. Liu's lectures are tough to follow, and I basically had to teach the entire class to myself. Exams are worth about 70% of your total but exam class averages were around a 65% and there was no curve. If you have minimal experience in econ prior to this course I would consider a different professor.

He was pretty good but his lectures made absolutely no sense i studied so hard for this class and went to every single lecture and it just lowkey made me more confused i would take a different professor if you don't understand econ easily
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor, does genuinely care about students understanding the material and pretty fair. I showed up but barely paid attention and still got a 4.0 easily but as long as you pay attention and keep up with homework (which he gives more than enough time for) you have nothing to worry about.

Getting a 4.0 in Micro is hard, even when the grade distribution is 85% to reach it. The professor was great; he went over everything pretty slowly, which was a downside, but it didn't affect my learning. Just the overall content is pretty difficult, and if I were to retake this, I would try to be more attentive.
