Often shows she is confused about content. Shes a nice lady with good intention but not a good instructor. TAs grade harsh, ive had questions wrong that I did with the professor.

Be ready to become a linguistics master(on your own time)Lectures and textbook were usually unhelpful, you HAVE to go to office hours/help room + be cautious of due dates bc they are easy to miss. The exams weren't horrible, and I managed to get an A after studying a TONNNN. You will cry over this class. Try to do homework early so you can get help
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is very disorganized and not the best at explain the content of the class. Her lectures are also not structured, making them hard to follow and understand. However, she did offer a lot of extra credit on the final (added up to 20% to midterm exam grade). Her intentions are there but her lack of organization makes the class difficult.

Good professor, you just have to pay attention. It's harder when you're not interested in linguistics, but as long as you focus up in class and ask questions when you're confused, you will get a good grade. The TAs are also really helpful.

I will NEVER take this class with her again. Try to take this class in the spring with a different professor if you can. Lectures were unorganized and I lost points on the homework for problems she helped with. Make sure to go to the TAs instead (they grade them). D2L course was also never updated with lecture material, so you have to go to class.

This was by far the worst class I have ever taken at msu. The assignments took an extremely long time to complete and she graded extremely hard. I also spent majority of the time teaching the material myself. The ta's weren't any help. I wouldn't recommend taking this class unless you absolutely have to.

worst class ever. almost cried tears of joy when it was over. not even sure why I took it. assignments graded extremely hard and nobody ever knew what was going on in the lectures. she is nice but seriously does not know how to teach. spent majority of the time learning the material myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: So hard, I have never struggled so much in a course. I got a C on a take-home exam. It truly was such a hard course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cristina is a very nice person but her way of teaching made it hard for me to understand the class. Notes were all over the place and it was hard to understand what she was saying in the lecture. The TA's helped me more than anything, and help-rooms were my best friend. The format of the tests were unbelievably hard to understand, hence my grade.

While she is a very nice person, but her lectures are extremely spotty and barely seem to follow a coherent plan. She expected you to read out of the textbook to know what you were doing, but would vaguely mention what reading was assigned, and then would only somewhat cover that reading. The homework was a lot to do and was graded harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was all over the place. I was stressed during every lecture just trying to figure out what was going on.

While Dr. Schmitt knows her stuff, she doesn't know how to teach someone who has not had any exposure to the material. My entire class was lost the entire semester. The homework assignments often had nothing to do with what we were learning in class and we were graded harshly on things we had never been taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I've taken 3 classes with her and have been in her lab the entire time I've been at MSU. She is amazing, super accessible, and always willing to help you out. She works hard to make her classes reflect the interests of her students.

No textbook but a lot of scholarly articles. She is not definite on her projects. She does not give a rubric or any specific information. She is very learned on her topics. If you read the articles she posts at the beginning you will do fine. There is only two exams and a few group projects, no homework. Graded on class participation.
Lectures are easy to understand, homework is pretty easy, takes attendance regularly.

Class structure is well taught. Majority of the material is being able to read and interpret graphs, basic econometrics but not rigorous whatsoever. Professor is willing to meet if you are having issues, attendance is not worth much. Don't let the other reviews deter you this class is a much better option than other ec 400 classes.

It isn't said anywhere, but you should definitely take EC420 before this class. So far it is very regression heavy. The slides are the worst part of the class. Poorly made, spelling and grammar errors everywhere. Midterm is coming up and it is so hard to study if you want to read the slides. To be fair, the subject is pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Knows plenty about education economics but not how to teach. Would read off poorly made slides that he refused to even post on D2L which makes it incredibly hard to study. Had no clear learning goals or objectives for each unit so I didn't know what to learn. What is actually on exams or his in-class essay is a mystery and I often was blindsided.

Professor Craig is a very good professor. He is quite anti-technology, so beware of that, but many of the PTCD faculty are. He is overall a great teacher though and makes himself very available. Not an easy professor, but if you pay attention in class and do most of the readings, you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is taught by different guest lectures which is made clear in the beginning of the course. I really found this class to be interesting and enjoyed it thoroughly. I found Craig's lectures to be really engaging and funny. I didn't ever talk to this guy 1 on 1 but he seemed great from a distance, The exams are very hard though so be aware.

Dr. Craig is very knowledgeable and his lectures were amazing. The class has different guest lecturers and topics each class, all of which were interesting. But, the exams were very difficult as you're given little to no grading criteria and the answers they're looking for are very specific. Grading is tougher than a 100-level course should be.

If you're a PTCD major this doesn't apply to you, as I am sure he is a great PTCD professor. Taking MC201 with him as a freshman was absolutely horrid. Very harsh grader. If you are someone who is not interested in political theory, and you were planning on taking him for any other type of class, don't.

He's a fantastic professor and one of my favorite's within the PTCD major. He's extremely understanding and realizes that people often have circumstances that can affect their in class performance. I recommend him to any PTCD student, especially for this class. However, if you are not in JMC, I do not think you will like his teaching style.

I've taken both MC202 & MC270 with Craig and I can confidently say he is by far my favorite professor. His lectures are entertaining and really help you understand the reading material more. He is always accessible outside of the class for office hours and is a helpful and caring professor. He's a tougher grader but the feedback is super helpful!

Was ok overall.Guest lecture topics are interesting. Tobin & co prof are caring/will help if you reach out/attend office hours.class is designed to make you think independently & intellectually. Participation is req. to be successful- in class and to every office hour. Grading is very particular. Exam is written responses about guest lectures only
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Craig was honestly one of my favorite professors this semester. He truly knows his craft and lectures well. If you choose his class ensure you go to his office hours for participation. There's a lot of reading in this class however, participation in class discussions is highly encouraged but not forced. He is a hard grader however.

The worst professor and the worst course I've had at MSU. Every topic is unrelated to the last and it's a new guest lecturer in almost every class even though there are 2 professors for this course. They grade incredibly difficult and have absurdly high expectations for a 100-level introduction course that is run so sloppily. Do not recommend it.

Professor Craig is a spectacular lecturer who cares about his students and their understanding of the material. His lectures don't just rehash what you read, they add context and deepen your understanding. The number of papers is reasonable and he's somewhat of a tough grader but going to office hours and taking notes in class is all you need!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Craig is a very intelligent professor who uses a lot of big words, which can be appreciated. I was always very excited for class; lectures were very engaging, make sure you take notes There was a normal amount of papers for a JMC class. He was a tough grader and I often didn't improve on the papers. But in terms of his class, it was very good.

He likes to use big words and speaks for long periods. Participation matters but not really when he talks the whole time. If your class is longer than an hour, you likely won't get a break, this isn't purposeful it's just because he talks a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Incredibly tough grader with little to no criteria of expected responses. Waited until over two and a half months into the course to grade any assignments. Poor communicator with both students and co-professor. Every class was taught by a guest lecturer, in which the entire mid-term and final (both of which were essay response exams) were based off

This class is based off of guest lectures that do not relate to each other most of the time. The class has no central theme and all of the students are always confused, the exams are also all written response questions. This class is harder than any class I have ever taken in college, which is insane since it is an introduction class.

Incredibly hard grader, looking for overly thorough responses. Horrible communicator. I miss a midterm for an excused class, and poorly communicates with me and the professor he co-teaches with. He eventually scheduled a time with me but didn't tell her. He also mocked her for going easy on exams. We also have to write some of the exam questions.

Dr. Craig co teaches this class with Dr. Bennet, however it seems like everyone else does more work than both of them. Nearly every class has guest lecturers, the exams are all essay response, the grading criteria is unknown and if you don't give a PHD level response you get a 0/10 on the question. I would not take this class again, nor the profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Craig was very unhelpful and not responsive to emails. We had to write a 1,100-word paper and I was going through a difficult time (which I had previously explained to him) and my paper was 1050 words. Because my paper was under the word count I did not "complete" the class according to Craig. He is an awful lecturer and a hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed my class with Craig. He can definitely be tough on students, but he is overall very fair and willing to explain things in office hours. If you do anything in this class, you should ask questions and go to office hours. Everyone who did well did both of those things.

I had him for my MC201 class I would never take him again it was so bad half of the things he said in the lecture you couldn't use in tests because he would mark them incorrect. my class had twenty freshmen by the end only ten even stayed in James Madison.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I believe the negative reviews are mostly people being angry that didn't try their best. I agree he grades tough but it's fair. I somewhat understand the unresponsiveness to emails but he's always at his office hours. I was engaged the entire time in his class his passion for what he does is clear and spreads to the students. I would recommend.

Craig is the kind of guy you need to know if you want to do good in the class, however if you are somewhat intelligent, you can get a 3.0 a-ok. Biggest things you need to know is that he really wants definitions for words you have to use in your short answer blue book style papers, or else he'll give you a low grade. Speaking from a 2.5 in MC111.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Whatever you give will never be good enough, he gives terrible feedback, no grading criteria and his lectures are nearly impossible to follow

This is a 'co-taught' class with Dr. Bennett, she's great and helped me let alone pass. Craig on the other hand could care less if you do well in the class. Exams are short essay response and their desired answers are very specific to their own thinking. You'll get a 0/10 if responses don't match. Guest professors every class provide no struct add.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams are entirely short-answer questions and have no clear grading criteria. Every question is entirely up to the professors' judgements with subjective "implied rubrics" and there is little concrete material to study from. He never gives straightforward answers to questions, making it very hard to do well in this class. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is smart, but has trouble explaining to people who don't have PhDs. He is willing to help, but you have to track him down after class. When the class did poorly on midterms, he did a more in-depth review for the final, but couldn't get much done on it because people who did poorly kept arguing with him about his grading, wasting everyone,s time.

He does not answer his emails and is not ready to take criticism about the course. Course is based on lectures given by guest speakers. The exams are almost impossible to study for because many of the topics are not based on what we go over in class. All questions are short answer and they do not give you a rubric so you have to take your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You can tell Professor Craig enjoys what he teaches, he's engaging, however, it's almost as if he's showing off what he knows. He refuses to respond to emails and can be hard to track down. Students asked weeks before if we could have online class the day before Thanksgiving, he waited until the day of to move it online which was rather annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dont take FW181 with Craig if you want to fail because he does not care about you succeeding. He is not willing to take criticism or suggestions; he'd rather argue with you why he's always right than cooperate to find a solution. Exams are all short answers and ridiculously long. Theres not a slightest bit of direction but false hope for this class

Professor Craig is kind. He is funny and he makes an effort to have entertaining classes. He is a hard grader but he is fair. He will also be understanding of struggles outside the class. I enjoy class with him despite rather boring content sometimes.
Professor Craig was wonderful for MC270, but BE READY TO READ.. Fast paced, but lots of great discussion and lecture from Professor Craig.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Absolutely NO direction and makes exams way too obscure and impossible to study for. Doesnt care about students success whatsoever. Treats the 100 level like a 400+
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class has the worst structure and it feels as though the professors would rather have their students struggle than strive. Every class is a new lecture and it could be able ANYTHING, even if it does not relate to the course. If you were to ask me what the course mainly covers I would have no single answer for you. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have ever had. He definitely created the structure of the class to get out of teaching and grading as much as possible since only guest lecturers speak every class and your grade is based on ONE paper (although he makes you write 5 of them), midterm and final, and attendance. Beware he is VERY VERY ARROGANT.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amazing and funny man. He definitely knows his stuff and he knows it. If the subject is not his specialty area though he will have a hard time helping. He is a super strict grader and difficult to find outside of class unless you go right after. Be ready to be very frustrated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Entertaining lectures. Not my fav JM prof. He often flaunts what he knows rather than teaches. Flashy. Less organized than other profs. Needs more substance less flare. Hes not bad and I see why some may like his style but I would prefer a prof whos voice was consistent with the course material in order to eliminate confusion.
Wonderful speaker and an incredible person. Never been more interested in his lectures.

I could honestly listen to him speak all day. Hilarious, super nice guy that cares about his students' progress. His classes are engaging and he is always willing to help. (His tie collection is also pretty impressive)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Craig is one of the most interesting and engaging professors you will ever meet. His classes are run by using the Socratic method so you are really challenged everyday. If you take philosophy to hear, Craig is the professor for you.
Excellent, engaging professor. Definitely one of the best I've ever had.
He is the hottest teacher at this university and he dresses extremely well.  He is funny and entertaining which makes his class great to go to.  I highly recommend it
SHES AMAZINGGGGG

I actually took Karenanna for TE 432, Learning Through Movement, and she was incredible. One of the few Education profs that have taught me applicable, real-world lessons and examples. She was so sweet and so fun to talk to, also extremely accommodating. I highly suggest her for this class.

She is super nice and easy to reach out to. I would send her my assignments to look over and she would always respond very quickly with helpful feedback. She lets you redo any assignment with a low grade even if it's from the beginning of the year. She makes learning fun and creative. Totally recommend her for Learning Through Drama.
Love her! Recommend 10/10 for the Learning through Drama class!! Easy to talk to:)

Professor Crosson is the greatest thing to ever walk into a biology classroom. He is super nice and very eager to help students understand the material. The class is flipped, which takes some getting used to, but he always does a recap at the beginning of class, which is very helpful. Also he had a little texas accent so he is fun to listen to.

Dr. Crosson is a thorough professor and is good at what he does. He is very knowledgable in the content and is super caring/understanding! The book is required, but it does not really help that much and the main content is in the lectures/ICAS. Extra credit opportunities are offered for exams 1-3(1 point each). I recommend him!

BS 161 was a very difficult and consuming class, but Dr. Crosson and his TAs/UALs were phenomenal. Without them I would have failed this class without a doubt, but they did an amazing job of helping every student who needed it and explaining the why behind the processes. Dr. Crosson is truly a great professor, and I wish I could have him again.

Hard class, but great professor. You get used to the stupid schedule, but it's a flipped classroom, so you teach yourself everything, then recap with questions and examples in class. Lot's of homework and studying. Iclicker questions also count for a grade. Crosson is great at answering questions in depth, so try and you'll be fine.

Class itself is all group work with online lectures. Crosson is really cool and knows the subject well, but the in-person sessions are really boring if you don't have a good group. Exams and quizzes are online, open note. DO NOT buy the textbook unless you abosultely have to, they "require" it but didnt buy it and I never once wished I bought it.

Dr. Crosson is probably the best BS 161 professor you can find at MSU, however, he only teaches every 2 years so be mindful when you are scheduling for this class. Every other BS 161 professor needed to be switched out in the middle of the semester except for him because he was actually knowledgable on the topic unlike the others as I hear it.

Dr. Crosson is a very nice guy. He's laid back and clearly loves biology. The class itself is a "flipped classroom," which means you watch the lectures outside of class and do groupwork inside of class. There was a quiz with a retake allowed each week and iClicker questions each class. Overall, the class was hard but the professor made it worth it!

Honestly, he was not a bad professor. He does really care about the future of his students and constantly would bring up opportunities and opened himself up to help guide students which I thought was really nice. The exams are a little hard but if you show up to class you will understand whats going on. The group project was pretty easy too.

Crank is a piece of work. Easily one of the worst professors on campus, but is a God in his own mind. Never take this man, as he will make your semester 10x harder than it needs to be. (He is also the type of guy to read all these negative views on him, and conclude everyone but him is the problem.)

William Crank, is a misunderstood professor who just wants to push his students. He provides many opportunities for career readiness. He is a bit strict with grading, but if you participate and give your full effort you can succeed. The tests were pretty hard though.

This professor constantly changes the syllabus and is very disorganized. Likes bragging about himself to the point where any material you're quizzed on has something to do with him. Quizzes were also phrased to trick you and usually had little to do with the material covered in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yea so William Crank got cranky and made me stay after class to give me a lecture on being on time. I also was surprised by how much he bragged. He would  brag about things way off topic all time. If you tell him you know something he might argue you or brag he is better at it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: William Crank made my semester a living heck. He would constantly brag about the most insane things, like how he taught his dog to do a backflip. I asked what this has to do with the class, but he completely ignored me and continued bragging. He also farted during his lecture and pretended like it didn't happen, even after I called him out.

The worst professor I have had at MSU and I am going into my senior year. This guy will make your semester terrible, if you see his name of your schedule run as fast as you can in the other direction.

Crank was mostly just disorganized. His lectures were all over the place. Nobody seemed to be aware of what was happening, and he would constantly change dates on the syllabus. He didn't give out a ton of homework, but when he did, the instructions were usually pretty vague. Brought in a few important guest speakers. The class was a waste of time.

Don't take this class. Professor Crank is the WORST professor I have ever had. To start, he did not stick to his syllabus and constantly changed the dates of things. He loves to talk himself up and talk down on his students; very obvious that he is extremely insecure. His quizzes and final exam were extremely difficult for a basic skills class.
he is very unorganized! he doesn't stick to his syllabus, sends last minute emails about important things, test and pretty difficult with way too much info on them. and he always brags about himself

Crank is a horrible professor, he does not teach he just talks about things he's worked on and brags. He gives no instruction for projects and assignments, then gives you a 60% at most when he grades it. Only reason to take this class is because it is required for pr major.
Goes off topic, doesn't explain assignments at all, gives 50% on every assignment, talks about weird things that do not relate to class, many people dropped because its so bad, do not take this class
extremely disorganized; will change due dates often. he will go off topic during lecture to talk about himself. many assignment directions are unclear
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am currently taking PR 305 with him this class is easily the worst class I have taken at msu He does not make any assignment clear every assignment he will not provide exact details of what he wants us to include. Most of the time he just talks about himself & prides himself that his exams r 15 pages single spaced & that they are not passable.

I have never felt the need to come here and rate any professor until him! I went as far as to even report him to our school. Please just find a different professor! He called students "a joke" to their faces, made racist comments, and his teaching was disorganized and honestly weird. I questioned him a few times and was not responded to kindly.

I had Professor Crank for ADV 486 as a capstone class. It was a perfect class to end my time at MSU. I learned a lot and got to work with a group of my classmates to help solve local business owners' problems in the area.

This professor deeply cares about his student's success. He provides his phone number to students to text or call if they have any questions regarding an assignment or help on the exam. This is something that few professors are willing to do. As long as you try and use the resources he provides, he is happy to help.

The single most disorganized professor I've ever had, assignment and quiz dates that were told in class almost never matched with the syllabus. Spent more time hearing stories about his life than learning the course content. He cares about his students and goes as far as to provide his personal cell phone # if needed, but he is just a bad prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: PR305: Extremely disorganized with exams being worded to trip you up (%s ranged from 33-88.) Assigns papers with no explanation on how to write them. Syllabus and rubrics often unclear/messy. Had to beg him to post slides which he flies through. Sometimes he's fair, but that's largely clouded by his inability to run a class or make things easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I appreciate that he used his own experiences in the business in lectures, as that gave applications and context to lectures. However, that's how he gave lectures. Almost purely through his own experiences. You have so few opportunities to earn a grade, so every little thing matters. This course caused so much stress. If you can, avoid his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Other reviews are definitely harsh, I was shocked to see his ranking was so low. He's super unorganized but admits it and is lenient with students in return. The lectures are engaging and he relates class materials to things we all experience. He gives you 4 absences, but otherwise you have to go to class. I honestly like him and he makes me laugh!

While I understand some people frustrations with professor Crank I feel he's being criticized too harshly. Professor Crank provided us all with his PERSONAL PHONE NUMBER. This is an extremely large degree of trust to endow all of his students with and that resource was the main reason I passed the class.
I strongly recommend you don't cause yourself the stress and anger of taking any of his courses
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mitch Crank was incredibly ineffective for PR 225; he just read off slides and talked about himself but no real learning was done. He's also incredibly disrespectful towards students and cannot respond to questions or concerns without making students feel inferior. I refuse to be a PR minor because of him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was the most unorganized teacher I've ever met. Currently in PR 225, (ADV 205 is my only option to select) and our assignments are like kindergarteners but we have 2 quizzes. Both quizzes were impossible and looked like they were put through google translate 3 times. This course is a joke.

Never met someone who was as rude or as angry as him. Possibly has short man syndrome. Tests had little relation to the lectures or textbook/homework we did. Also had a poor note-taking method in which he'd make students "fill in the blanks" on PowerPoint, which seemed to make it harder to follow rather than taking personal notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Straight up says racist and inappropriate things and doesn't take criticism well. Confusing the way he releases assignments and quizzes.

He uploads every lecture and the presentations online for his students, yet he still expects you to come to class.  He is very stubborn when students express questions or troubles they have in class and does not like to listen very well.  Also his attitude towards the class is inappropriate and unnecessary for students in a gen. ed intro class.
Very stubborn and expects too much from an intro class. Will not listen to students recommendations and problems

This semester is his first time teaching ADV205 - Gen. Ed. He talks too fast to accurately take notes, and doesn't give enough time to adequately cover lecture slides. We had an open-note quiz, in which most students scored under 4/10. Despite studying and taking notes, I scored a 7/10 due to poorly worded questions. The attitude on this guy.......
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hes super funny and very laid back. He likes to help students succeed
Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bob is a great and funny guy. The class he teaches is pretty easy. As long as you show effort, you'll get a good grade. The only problem is that he talks a lot. His lectures can go on a very long time because he goes on long tangents and repeats himself often. Other than that he's very helpful and nice. His lectures can drag but he's still great.

If you want a professor who genuinely cares about you, Mr. Cummiskey is your guy. He is super considerate and is willing to work with you if you communicate. Great teacher, would definitely recommend for WRA 101.

I loved Dr. Bob! He made a gen-ed writing class very enjoyable. There are only 5 essays, or "projects" that you have to complete over the course of the semester, and as long as you stick to the rubric you will be fine. On top of being hilarious, he also gave me really good feedback that I could put towards my future essays.

Love this guy. I had a mental health crisis halfway through the semester and went from being there everyday to missing most classes. He was super understanding and had no problem accommodating me through that time. Also a super light grader as long as you put effort in. I would happily take this course again if I had to, great GPA boost.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super chill professor and you get like 6 free absences, he gives quality feedback on your papers. Final is easy and you can do it early. Super easy class.

Cummiskey is a nice guy but the class was super disorganized due to him being absent and also the nature of the course (white guy teaching about hip-hop). Super easy though, only graded on five things and one is attendance. Lectures were boring, showed loads of movies. Easy grader too, but grading criteria is not clear

Prof. Cummiskey is very casual and a great guy to interact with. If you show up to class and participate, he'll remember you and be more likely to help out when you need it. Class was very easy, mostly documentaries with writing projects throughout the semester. Very easy class to take for the IAH credit, plus it's a very fascinating subject.

If you ever have to take WRA 195H definitely take Dr. Cummiskey. He's so understanding and caring and always ready to give extensions when needed. He's also so chill with grading and as long as you fulfill the assignment guidelines you're guaranteed a 4.0. class doesnt require much work either.

He was an amazing professor, but my only complaint is that he did not grade any assignments until after finals, so I worried a bit about how he grades. All the assignments are very clear to complete and he allows you to turn in assignments late. Not a harsh grader, got a 4.0 in the class.

Really nice and caring guy. He just wants you to show up and participate. Do the work and you'll get a 4.0. Overall super easy class with an even better professor. Highly recommend taking this course with him.

He is a really nice guy and if you participate a little he is super willing to help you and be accommodating. He does not put grades in which sucks but he gives you a lot of time for each project and gives really good feedback. Just show up and do the work and you'll be fine. He says attendance is mandatory but you can miss 2-3 times.

Doesn't put in grades until last minute BUT it's a fair and good amount of workload, if you miss one class you're fine. You get 4 absences through the semester. He's very very very caring and understanding and wants you to learn and understand course material. He is an amazing professor and very passionate of what he teaches.
Every class, you get homework assignments after working fully for the whole hour and 50-minute class, the homework is always long and pointless

Great class, just a lot of busy work outside the classroom. Don't take the syllabus too serious, he doesn't really apply any of it (like attendance or turning things late - he's flexible) besides the schedule. Also, he graded EVERYTHING the last week of class…

Curtis is an entertaining professor who cares a lot about his students, loves his job, and grades easily. That being said, he also assigns a myriad of homework at times, but he is very flexible with due dates. His lectures often have groupwork, and many assignments are peer review, so beware if that is not up your alley.

While I thought Curtis was a good professor, he did not grade a single thing the entire semester until the last two weeks. This was incredibly frustrating, as I had no idea how I was doing in the class until the very end. There was also a boatload of homework due every class, much more than my other classes, which made it hard to keep up.
Such a easy going professor with a super easy course. If you enrolled, just know you got a 4.0.
Great professor and very chill. Sometimes a little disorganized, but he is always open for questions.

One of my favorite professors I've had so far. He makes it very clear that he loves teaching and cares about writing, which makes class enjoyable. There's only 4 major papers, and a few in class assignments that encourage group participation. Take his class if you want an easy A and good writing feedback/experience.

For a terrible GenEd class, Prof. VanDonkelaar makes this class way more enjoyable. He rarely takes attendance and is very understanding on any assignments. Feedback for your papers and knowledge about the writing process are outstanding. He didn't care so much for grammar and other specifics, but the writing itself. Overall I highly recommend.

Had him for IAH231B but that's not an option on here. This professor was great, he was really funny and cared for his students a lot. It was a really interesting class as well, I'd love to have him for another class in the future.

Take this professor for wra! He's such an easy going guy who genuinely cares about his students. His class basically consisted of us writing for projects that we would have been doing outside of class anyway. And if you need more time on assignments he's very flexible. The papers are easy cuz they're mainly about your experiences. Highly recommend!

Prof. VD is hilarious, committed and super helpful. He puts his students first, and genuinely cares about the contents that he teaches about. No exams, 4 papers, classwork most of the time, and sometimes short groupwork in the class.

Easy class, he put in grades really late into the semester. You can skip a couple classes each semester and u should be fine. He tends to talk a lot so class wasn't super fun and I thought he tended to teach us things we have learned in 9th grade english class. Overall he's a good guy.

I like this prof a lot but he is an extremely slow grader, which is difficult to deal with since there are SO much work for this class. Expect 3-5 assignments a week, but don't expect grades until the very end of the semester. If you reach out to him though he will provide stellar feedback on your work. Best suited for CW minors, not as an elective
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Definitely recommend him! Although he doesnt grade many assignments, he gives very clear rubrics and is very easy going. Genuinely one of my favorite professors!

Dr. Eve was an amazing professor that taught a very well structured English class. He was very caring to all students and grades pretty leniently. Do your work when assigned and you should be able to easily get a 4.0.

He claimed that my paper was done by ai, which it wasn't and gave me a horrible grade. There was nothing I could do cause it was the end of the year. He is ALWAYS late to class and will cancel it 10 min before it starts when everyone is already in the classroom. Unprofessional and expects a lot when he doesn't hold himself to the same standards.

Professor Cuevas is an excellent teacher. He's fun, helpful, and genuinely passionate about teaching — something that's increasingly rare these days. A professor who actively engages with students and truly wants them to learn already goes above and beyond. Show up to class, put effort into your projects/peer reviews and you'll 4.0 this course.

Professor Cuevas is truly one of the best professors I have had at MSU. He is so laid back and understanding. Communication is key in his class and despite any sense of intimidation you may have, there is no way to fail unless you are simply not even trying. Always always communicate with Cuevas and your results in this course will be great!

Eve was a very good grader and seemed to actually care about each student. I noticed that I would consistently get the perfect grade I needed to keep my grade at a 4.0, but I'm not sure if that was him looking out for me or not. Either way, he is a very good person and an above average professor.

Professor Cuevas so far has been the best professor I've had. He's genuine, real, and understanding. I had him for a WRA hybrid class and sometimes if he didn't feel like going in, he'd make it a zoom (and nobody was complaining). The setup of the course is super simple. Daily journals, around 4 projects, and peer reviews and reflections for proj.

Prof. Cuevas is very caring and very kind, Im not a huge fan of writing and I took it due to University requirements but he was able to make it interesting. Very easygoing. Would totally recommend him as your writing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, better person. Flexible guy, doesn't grade overly hard, clear rubrics, very personable. Actually cares about his students. This guy is awesome.

Professor Eve is amazing. He makes WRA 101 so interesting and takes the class a step beyond a graduation requirement. Professor Eve ensures that the content covered in class is diverse and conversation provoking. He works with his class to develop grading scales and makes the criteria very easy to understand. If you participate you will do well.

Mr Eve gave weirdly long readings but mostly graded them for completion instead of correctness. He was very open minded and didnt rely on the standard English way of writing. Instead he focused more on writing in your own way. He graded everything very late, I got my scores for all my projects on the last day of the semester. He was very laid back.

He is a great professor this semester. However, he may have had a rough semester as his grading was super late. The last four projects were graded in the last month of the semester, so you'll be unsure what your grade will be all semester for the most part. But he's super chill and low-key, and the work is very laid back and easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Eve is one of my favorite professors. Hes super laid back and his lectures are really interesting. He gives really good feedback on writings and is very genuine. I would highly recommend taking his class.

I really recommend Eve, he is a great guy along with an amazing teacher. Attendance is required for this class by the school, and the class is graded based on 5 projects/attendance. You should get a 4.0 if you show up and put in effort into the projects/online posts. The only thing that sucks is the grading scale used by the school - 94% is a 3.5

Currie made an easy class way too difficult. She explains things well but doesn't set you up for success. Her lectures miss a lot of important info and her exams are almost impossible to take. Her lab assignments also seem so useless and set you up for a low grade. If she wants students to do better she should redesign her slides and assignments.

She never adds any of the important points during lecture into her slides. If you want to succeed in this class, you have to heavily take notes which is almost impossible. Her exams are so bad and impossible to study for. She also does not set up assignments very well. If you miss one thing, you are not allowed to complete other requirements.

Professor Currie's lectures are long and have a lot of confusing info, I found it easier to not attend and study it at my own pace. However, she gives few extra credit points for attendance. The labs were frustrating for me as the pre quizzes were hard and you dont get alot of time. The lab TAs dont really help you for the lab reports either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material is interesting. The class would be so much better with a different professor though. Great person. Not great at explaining things. Some student have done really well. I am not one of those students. The material is confusing and she confuses me more with the way she explains things. Overall, this class sucks but you can do well in it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory. His lectures covered what would be on the exams, also the practice exams were similar to the exams. But the class is almost entirely based on exam grades.
Very passionate in his lectures. Participation matters a fair amount regarding iClicker. Practice exams are extremely similar to the real exams.

His lectures were interesting and easy to follow. You can tell he enjoys teaching. Attendance is required and he uses iclicker to check the grades. The test study guides he makes are important. If you can do those, you can do the exam.  He has a generous extra credit policy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cuncic is very passionate about physics. He is helpful and responsive to feedback. He is exactly what I would hope for from a physics professor at MSU. I am happy with how things turned out in this course and I would take any course with him teaching.

He was a good professor, however he most certainly did not give out a ton of EC as another review claimed, he legit gave out one extra credit assignment and the iClicker questions are also considered "extra credit." I would not say the exams were easy either, not at all, especially considering the average of the second exam was failing.

He was pretty good. Lectures were hard to understand at some points but you can just look over slides again after class and understand. His tests were easy, just like his practice exams. Gives a TON of extra credit, and weekly homeworks. He was really nice and cared about our class, made changes to the class based off our suggestions.

He was a great professor. Lectures were quite fast but understandable with how much we had to cover. He was very receptive to his students and adapted the course accordingly to better accommodate his students. This is something I haven't seen many professors do. I appreciate him putting aside any ego and putting our needs first.
Professor Bauer and Cuncic were like Shaq and Kobe MSU got gems in these two.

He is the co-lecturer with prof Bauer. He teaches stuff really well in lectures. He will explain questions with great detail and I really enjoy attending his class. Sometimes he will even put corresponding hw questions on presentation slides. Turns out I believe this is a better way of teaching since we now truly understand how this question works.

This class is not hard but you do need to make sure you go through the lectures and review before exams because the exams are not open note. Her lectures are kind of boring but make sure to pay attention bc it will be on the exams and homework. The final exam is not cumulative it just a regular exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On exams be prepared to be tested on calculations as well as definitions and fill in the blank. If you go to lectures you should have no problem in this class. Cuppules is an amazing professor who prepares you for hw and exams extremely well with class lectures, I would recommend making flashcards for definitions, take notes

Overall, a great class and professor. Everything you need to know she teaches you in lecture, the book is a nice addition but not necessary. The exams are a little challenging and require knowledge from lectures and homework, but overall, pretty fair. Attendance/participation not really required as she has recorded lectures on D2L. HWK once a week.

Nice lady! The notes she gives are clear and the homework is totally manageable and actually helps with the exams. The lectures could stand to be a little more interesting, but overall a good class, and an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Cupples is fantastic. All information on exams and homework is gone over in class. Lectures can be a little boring, but overall she is a good professor and prepares you well for exams. As long as you go to class this is an easy A.

One of the best professors I've had. She is extremely kind and her lectures are great. The homework follows the lecture examples and the tests are very similar to the homework. If you show up and pay attention, you'll be fine.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER!!!! I missed class once, and you're allowed to miss three, and i will be lucky to 1.5 this class. It's so hard, she is TERRIBLE and extremely unhelpful. She expects you to memorize all the material and then decides to not test you on the "performance objectives" that she tells you to know. Avoid her at all costs!!!!

She is a really good professor! The homework is actually helpful and never took me more than 20 or 30 minutes. She does expect participation from everyone, but makes it super easy to contribute. Sometimes the lectures can feel a little repetitive, but overall I loved her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved Cynthia! I'm taking her again next semester and looking forward to it!
she is amazing and personable. she is very understanding about everything and willing to be flexible if needed.
I LOVED this professor! She is amazing at what she does, super caring and understanding! Light course work, allows students to revise there mistakes, 10/10 would recommend!

She is my favorite professor I have ever had. Gives you a chance to correct mistakes that you may have made on your quizzes. She is there to help you at all times and is super understanding if you need an extension on a project. Absolutely amazing. Highly recommend taking a class with her if you can!!!!!

She was an amazing teacher. She is also very big on working with people in groups. So, if you do take her class work with people you enjoy talking to and participate. Otherwise, the class is going to go slow, and you will not want to go to class. Get the textbook, you don't really need it for homework, but you will need it for papers.

Cyndi was an amazing prof to have for TE 301 (it made me choose 406 for some reason). You have reading guides due every week but the reading is actually pretty interesting. She is also super helpful if you communicate with her and gives you a lot of class time to work on projects.
One of my favorite profs. I loved this woman! She inspired me in many ways.
Huge class. Feels small. Usually a combo of activities in class. Really interesting activities. More interactive than most classes with 15 students.
Do the extra credit (very easy), go to class, get an A.
If you have to take ISS 300-level class, TAKE Professor Gabriel's section. It is the best.
I really enjoyed the class and the teacher. I learned so much :)

I love the way this class was organized.  We didn't just read from one text book.  It was interesting.  We read from several books (usually only 2-10 pages a time for hw), watched several short YouTube clips and if you attend class each day (very little participation required) you can easily understand and pass this class. Super interesting!

She is extremely confusing. Everything is thrown onto the syllabus including due dates (which are changed verbally but not on the syllabus) so any time there is an assignment you have to dig through the entire syllabus. For a university requirement class the workload is a lot (if you actually do everything).  Conclusion: unorganized

For a class with more than 200 people I can't believe how "small" she makes this class feel. I got to know other students. I love her lecture style. Some students want more "textbook"-style, but I prefer the way she has an organization structure to lecture but just talks without notes.

unlike the other rater i loved our project because she gave us time in class to work on it. it was actually quite easy. and interesting. she gave us a lot of creative freedom with the project. and i thought the discussions were really interesting, but i didn't love listening to the rest of the students so much.

There's too much for just 350 characters, but I will say be prepared for your final to be a big group project. She is very unclear with what she wants, didn't know how to use D2L so I had no idea where I stood in the class. Her class was interesting in the beginning but quickly becomes extremely dull. I'd say the only plus is there was only 1 exam.
Went to FLorence on study abroad with her. EXCELLENT teacher and travel companion!
Great teacher!
wow, she is such a powerful force of nature...the best prof i have had yet!!!!!!

He is an overall good professor, his morning classes were a bit brutal and boring. But he was very passionate in teaching, and provides some extra credit that helps a lot. Plus, he drops your lowest test score. Tests are very, very hard though all true or false.

For a 8 am class tries to keep it pretty interesting. VERY passionate about subject matter. Go to lectures because material not in books will be on the exams. Take notes, read the books, and save exams and you'll be fine. Seven Open Book/Open Note True-False exams & no homework.

Cy is a good teacher his class isn't that hard if you go. You are allowed to use your notes and the books on the exams.  His class is not mandatory to attend but I recommend you do it makes it a lot easier to pass the exams, which are all true false including the final.

I love this class! I think he's a really good professor and he makes class interesting. Unlike many other professors, he relates class to the real world, which makes it easy to understand. Yes, the notes are a little difficult to understand and his test wording is complicated but if you go to class you should be fine.

Do not buy the book. It will be a waste of your money and reading does not help to understand the material. Make sure you go to class often because you will need the notes for the open exams. He is very boring, nice guy, but very boring. His topics are not that interesting either, unless you are really in to native Hawaiians.

The required textbook was edited by him and has several typos.  His lectures are loud and obnoxious. He's rude. The tests are all true/false, watch out for the wording.  While attendance is optional, he adds a lot of stuff in the lectures that you can't get from the book.  My advice, do not take a class with this prof.

He is a very funny teacher, which makes you want to come to class. His exams are hard to understand but they are all 25 questions true or false. The take home final is worth 100 points, if you get together with a group of people you can work on it together. The in class final is 75 questions true or false. 50 50!
do not take this class! the true and false questions are a paragraph long with words that incomprehensible. His notes don't make sense. It is impossible!

The teacher is all over the place in his lesson. He lost my final exam, would not accept responsibility for it and passed me only when i told him im going to the umbudsman to report him. Monotonous and droning, his students learn nothing and suffer for a semester in his class.

Good gosh. I have never had such an easy class. The tests are all true/false!! Honestly! How can you fail?? He gives you a take-home final for god's sake! If you don't understand him, I suggest expanding your vocab. He *does* use some higher level language, but no more than is expected of college students. Too bad he's retiring soon.
TESTS ARE IMPOSSIBLE...I WOULD ADVISE YOU NOT TO TAKE THIS CLASS W/ THIS TEACHER!!!
Worst prof I've ever had. Just loves the sound of his crazy voice.
Go to class, read the books.  The final review is a lifesaver.  Do it FULL OUT.

This class isn't too bad, as long as you read the 2 books, and actually go to the class. He has some pretty cool stories, but you hear them over and over, as well as have to understand how they relate to what your doing on your own.
Tests are hard to understand.

He seems like a very nice guy, but he repeats all of his stories a million times. Plus, his stories never seem to relate to the topic. They are so long that by the time he is done, I cant remember what he was talking about. However I do have to say that the class is really not hard. If you read the book and come to class, you should have no problem
Really cool, but uses huge vocab

To everyone claiming that Cy is "soo hard" ...welcome to college. You cannot expect your professors to spoon-feed you answers to future exams in lectures, or be able to find those answers verbatim in your texts. Cy gives you the proper tools to make the larger inferences yourself. If you can't succeed at this, it's not him, it's YOU.
This class is hard, get out if u can. He is a nice guy but man are the tests hard. I would not recommend this class to anyone.

Nice guy.  Tests are hard even though you can use your notes, books and dicitonary!  When you read the books you think you understand until you take an exam.  He talks a lot to get his point across but I wish he would make his point and get on to the next topic before my attention is totally lost.
if you like hawaii, baseball, or cy's mother then take cy's class. this was the most annoying class i took because you never feel like you are answering any question right. switch out of this class

Nice guy, hard tests. He allows open note and anything else you want to use for the exams, but it's sort of useless. I enjoyed his lectured but my GPA didn't enjoy this exams. I suggest switching out if you can.

Class is aweful, I study forever for the exams and still dont do well. Guy is extreamly hard to understand and will screw you on the exams. SWITCH OUT OF THIS CLASS. I have 4. in every class but in his and have a 2.0

he repeats himself like 50 times, he is obsessed with stating tremendously large exaggerative vocab words, it would be understandable if he talked like that on the regular, but i guess if you feel because you are an prof, you have to be extraordinarily hard on purpose, but not all profs can do that.  Its a fine line between not being cont...

easy class. no homework involved except reading. exams werent too difficult if you simply attended class and gotten a few key ideas. open note exams- but i didnt really use the notes all that much. save the tests for the final exam. bring a dictionary to the tests.
Terrible Professor....His lectures are so boring and repetative its sickening. The exams are worded so difficultly, they are almost impossible to understand.
His test are nearly impossible to understand, switch out if you can. His an interesting person to listen to, but sucks at teaching.

I do not fail classes, but so far I am failing his class. He is the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. His vocab is so hard and no one understands what he says and he will NOT help you. I study so hard for this class and it doesn't help at all. If you can, SWITCH OUT OF HIM NOW! I'm not the only one that feels this way.
No Comments
He tries to make the lectures interesting but its a 2 hour lecture hall at 8am so I tend to nod off a bit. And all exams are open notes.  :)
Excellent professor.  Very passionate about the subject matter.  Will let you argue for points on the exams.  Very understanding about issues outside of the classroom.
No Comments

a little long winded but he realy love his subject and enjoys teaching it.  Also realy likes to make sure his students understand material.  do the reading, go to most classes and TAKE NOTES because his exams are OPEN NOTES!
Horrbile teacher. Tests are unreadable and question are ridiculous. Rubbish.
Very interesting class.  Tests are pretty easy if you went to class.  He let's you argue for points on the test, which is nice.
Very informative.  Makes a few outrageous claims, but at least they are interesting.
He is very passionate.  Uses difficult language on tests to trick you.  Pretty fair
Should keep up to date on current more's
No Comments
He sucks!  Unless his mother is covered on the exams in the future, you fail!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
HAWAII. thats all you need to know.
Went to about 3 lectures and didn't touch the books... still managed a 2.0.
Read the books adn you'll do fine on the exams.  The class was easy.
This man is a hypocrite
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Great guy, getting tired of the same stories.  Hard tests, but worth it

She was nice and helpful when needed, but overall a poor teacher and grader. Instructions for lab write-ups were inconsistent and scattered, making them hard to follow. She graded everything at the end, so I didn't know I was doing things wrong and got low scores. Group work grading was unfair since everyone shared the same grade.

She was great. She was there to help whenever and was easy to acess during office hours and email! The ULA's do a lot but she is always there making sure they are correct and help out whenever needed. My only complaint is the grades came in very late and sudden at the end of the semester.
Dr. Davis was very kind and she is good at explain where mistakes were made and how to fix them.

Your experience will vary greatly depending on your ULA's and lab partners, but Dr. Davis herself was accessible inside and outside of class which was helpful. Assignments are fairly easy as long as you follow the rubric exactly and communicate with ULA about the exact expectations and what they specifically want to see.

Professor Davis is one of the best lab professors I have had at MSU. She's okay at explaining things and may take a moment to articulate her thoughts but she makes sure you understand what's happening and is willing to help at any point during the lab. Overall, I would highly recommend her to anyone taking this class!

Course is a lab so it will be ran by ULAs. Be hopeful that you have amazing ULAs that you can ask for help with. Dr. Davis would have multiple sections at once & rarely appeared in my section. When she did appear, she asked questions but would make it more confusing. She is such a nice and kind professor although her teaching is another story.

Dr. Davis was a good lab instructor! From what I've heard, most labs are ran by LAs. Although Dr. Davis is present, most instruction will come from the LAs. She always has very accessible office hours and is there to answer questions.

Dr. Davis was not present sometimes but when she was she repeated the same things the LAs went over with us for so long and would cold call students. She wastes time and slows you down a little. I found the lab to overall be fine but due to the LAs for the most part. Wouldn't suggest her unless you have to.

Just like in my previous semester, Dr. Davis was rarely active in the lab. When she was there, my interactions with her were neutral. The difficulty of the lab is based solely on your group and ULA's.

LB155 lab and she was awful! My ULA's were great and led the lab. she was rarely in lab, when she was there she created mass confusion and chaos. The ULA's would tell us how to do something then we would do it, then Davis would come around and tell us it was wrong, but it would be right. Was told by ULA "she doesn't know what shes doing"

It is a lab so it is run by ULA's. As long as you have good ULA's you should be fine. Dr. Davis is barely present as she is in between multiple labs simultaneously. She will pop in randomly and ask tricky questions and get irritated if you don't know the answer. Most of the time Dr. Davis and the ULA's aren't on the same page so its confusing.

It is a lab, so it was mainly up to the ULAs. Mine were fine, but I know plenty people with differing experiences. Dr. Davis likes to sneak up on you while you work, but once you get past that, she's fine. She's helpful where it counts, in my opinion. That said, I probably wouldn't choose her as a lab prof again.

Dr Davis was rarely in the classroom. The ULA's and her did not communicate well between material and what is happening in the class. The lab did not contain a lot of actual experiments. Sometimes when asked what to do Dr Davis and the ULA's gave different answers to what we had to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was pretty awful. My ULA Mithil Penta was just straight up mean, and did not help whatsoever. The ULA's grade and run everything, and they are harsh with it. There is VERY little support from the teaching team let along Dr. Davis herself. It was pretty confusing and overall lots could be done to make the course better.

Beware to never know what you are doing in lab at all times. Me and my group met for our final project that was never explained to us and was due tomorrow. Terrible course and a waste of time and money. If you are being placed into College Algebra or a MTH 103, please just go into trig with chem 1 and lab so can skip whatever this is.

Absolutely terrible prof, taught two sections at once but never came in our secfion. TAs ran the course but told us the wrong information or Dr. Davis would come in and tell us something completely different from what the TAs

This professor is by far the worst professor I think I will ever have, and I am only a first year student. She does not give clear instructions at all, gives students assignments with no clear due date. Do not take this prof. even if you have to, if the class is required you are better off waiting for her to retire. Also she burped in my face.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I rarely see Dr. Davis, but my experiences with her have been average. The problem with this lab is that it all depends on the ULAs you get. Also, the lab feels like you are being dropped into a situation without much help or preparation.

She's really not bad. Doesn't do much, but I think that's true of all chem lab profs. It's really all down to your ULAs. Davis wasn't the most helpful, but she wasn't actively bad, and she was pretty nice.

Chem lab is a disorganized mess no matter who your professor is - I think Saraha gets much better reviews but my friends with Saraha had the same confusing assignments. What really matters is who your ULAs are. Class itself isn't hard, just disorganized.

Professor isn't involved in a lot of the labs, the ULA's mostly run them. The ULA's and professor can sometimes give confusing answers/feedback. Prepare to spend a lot of time outside of class with your lab group to work on assignments. Assignments and content aren't too hard though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Davis didn't involve herself often. LAs didn't seem to understand Davis's expectations but tried their best regardless. Assignments were sometimes confusing and very hard to find in D2L. Course is organized poorly. Davis answers questions with more questions and is not helpful. Lots of group work, so your group is large factor in your grade.

Barely saw her the whole semester. I got lucky with good LAs and a great group but it's clear that this class would've been much harder without those. Grades and points for the semester are clearly spelled out in the syllabus which I did like. I don't recommend her even though it wasn't bad for me as it's clearly a gamble on other factors.
Get ready to teach yourself literally every thing you need to know to pass.

In this lab, she was not present much, as the ULAs run the labs with her assisting as needed. The lab is just a hard class overall, so she did not necessarily make it more difficult. She always had good input during labs and made sure we were on the right track even though she was not there very often because she was going between the two labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Here's the deal, when you take chemistry lab through Lyman Briggs, you will not interact heavily with the professor. Your learning assistants are the people grading your assignments, so you really just want to make a good impression on them. Dr Davis is very nice, but not heavily reachable. Do your work in this class and you will 4.0

Do not take any classes! She is extremely disorganized, doesn't respond to emails, and she will only make you more confused. My entire experience in this class has been terrible the only good thing where the LA's since they were the only helpful part of this class. If you take lab with Davis get prepared  to be stressed out and permanently clueless
She made my day:)

I do not recommend taking this course with her. Everything and I mean EVERYTHING was disorganized. From homework not being posted in time, to typos on tests, to errors on the lectures, you name it. If you email her, you probably will not get a response, just keep that in mind. Several grading mistakes. Hardest class I have taken at LBC.
Dr. Davis is almost always late for class, she hardly gives any instruction for anything, and she is very disorganized.

She was one of the worst professors I've ever had. She didn't update any of the worksheets and so the flash didn't work; the pacing was too fast; she basically didn't teach at all; you are your own teacher, which should never happen in a lab; and to put the nail in the coffin your TAs are your only hope, so pray that you get a good one.

This online lab was awful. You do more work trying to figure out what lab assignments are asking (because of poor wording and various mistakes) than completing the lab itself. Dr. Davis herself is uninterested in the welfare of her students. She provided no instruction the entire semester. Take the normal chemistry lab.

She does care about the students and their grades and stuff, you just have to reach out. A very sweet professor and I think she made the best of the fully online lab. Some modules were hard but if you asked, the prof and the LA's are willing to help however they can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You teach yourself everything in this class. EVERYTHING. You want to do well? Get used to putting in 7-10 hours in a one credit class on a weekly basis. And depending on how poorly she paces the course each week, you may find yourself with an upwards of 12+ hours of busywork to do. So yeah, you're in for a treat if you end up with her.

Dr. Davis has good intentions, but failed to deliver on them in any of the time I spent in her class. She is very vague with her instruction and expectations. She has not taught a single thing herself and the entire class is led and taught by the LAs. Do not take LB171 L with her unless you are ready to teach yourself entirely.

Kind person, but she handled this course terribly. The workload is ridiculous, and the instructions on how to complete assignments are vague. To make things worse, none of the material covered in this class will benefit you in LB171 / Chemistry. Expect a lot of situations that make you want to rip your hair out. Pray that you don't get her.

Dr. Davis is a pretty good lab prof. I will say that 171L can be a little overwhelming at first and the profs throw you into it. However, Dr. Davis does care about her students. Be ready to work hard in this class, it is not the easiest. Really make sure you know what you are doing with labs, this gets a better chance for a 4.0.

Dr. Davis herself was a very nice lady, but the class was not up to par. The directions that were given weren't very clear and I had to rely on LAs for help most of time, but even then they too would be confused on what was going on.

Her lectures can be confusing/hard to follow as her english is not amazing. However, she is very kind and wants everyone to do well. Is very helpful in office hours and her exams are fair (and comparatively easy to other briggs exams). If you study, do the homework, and occasionally read the textbook you should be able to handle the class fine.

I do not know how to grade Dr. Davis because she had never stepped foot in the classroom the entire semester. I've met her and she is very kind. The class itself is more work than all of my classes combined. It is very unorganized and the teachers and LA's are very vague on what they expect. A pro is that there is an enormous curve at the end.

This lab was taught by TA's who didn't know what was going on (and the class being at 8am didn't help at all) The few times Dr. Davis did walk in, everyone would go rigid and pretend to do something because she's so intimidating. But if you get to know her, she's super sweet, just really intimidating and never there to help.

The class is taught totally by LAs and the labs are like group projects. I hated lab more than anything and I had a 4.0 in AP Chemistry in high school. The class is a bit of a necessary evil, and Professor Davis responds to emails really quickly if you have questions, but the class is trouble.

Class is taught by LAs. This makes it confusing, because others taking your class, but not in your section will confuse you as to what you need for each class period, lab report, etc. Generally, it was very difficult to figure out what we needed to bring to lab, though the LA and TA worked very hard to try and help us.

Class is taught by LA's instead of professor, which complicates the entire process. Overall, lab reports are daunting and brutal, so is the class. In hindsight, I should have avoided this class, for many reasons.

I urge you not to take this class if you have had difficulty with chemistry in H.S., the understanding partI got an 4.0 in chem. in H.S., and I loved science (I have 2.0 in her class now, maybe I can getr a 2.5..ruined my GPA). I just urge you LBS students to just take the university chemistry class and lab..the labs in 171L are 8-13pages.BE WARNED

I really enjoyed Professor Das Gupta; she makes sure you understand the content and even gives visual aids. Her midterm was open-note, and she even let us redo our first essay after she graded it and left comments. Her lectures are filled with examples that help us understand the content; just be ready to participate, but her office hours help!
Tons of reading and really rude. Hard to understand with her accent and always makes mistakes when speaking. wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor was amazing! I was out for a month due to illness, and she was extremely accommodating and helpful with me and had great feedback. There's a lot of reading and work, but it's worth it and I definitely feel like I learned a lot.

Professor Das Gupta was an incredible professor. She gives great feedback and is a very approachable person. One of the nicest people within the James Madison College. If you have the chance to take her class, take it.

201 is all lecture based, and Das Gupta did an amazing job. Her lectures were fascinating and very informative. All exams and papers were easy and fit the content. Das Gupta put together an amazing team of lecturers, and the topics were diverse. From the U.S. to India, from Brazil to Syria, Das Gupta covered interesting stuff and did a great job.

Das Gupta is the best teacher I have ever had here at MSU so far, and will probably sustain that role for the years coming. She is not only good at teaching and making sure we understand what is happening in class, she cares about her students and their well-being. Would 1000% recommend taking any class you can with her.

Professor Das Gupta is an outstanding professor. She makes an effort to get to know each of her students personally. She has a way of explaining tough concepts in concise, clear ways. She offers great feedback on essays and goes the extra mile to meet with students outside of class. I'd highly recommend taking this class with SDG.

When subbed in for Prof. Elmo, my grade went from bad to good. She was so accessible outside of class and willing to help. When asking for feedback, she went through my paper step by step with me over what she thought I could improve on, it was amazingly helpful when it came down to polishing the draft of my essay. Overall, super caring and helpful

Gupta is a wonderful teacher and person! She came in for Elemo the second half of the semester and the vast difference between those two teachers is insane. I felt more comfortable participating in this class and as if my opinions mattered and she did very well at teaching us the material and to improve our understanding.

As one of my first professors for the major I am pursuing, I was inspired by her and this class. She is very intelligent and wants us to understand these concepts and how applicable they are to our lives. She will make you a better reader and writer. She makes an interdisciplinary study very intriguing and inspiring.

Professor Das Gupta is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. She's tough but it motivates you to work hard and do your best. She does an amazing job at taking complicated theorhetical framework and making it accessible to students. I also think the case studies she chooses are extremely relevant to her work and the CCP major.

Professor DeVeaux is a good professor. At times it didn't feel like we had a clear rubric to follow specifically for the Group project. But he was an overall good professor offers support when you need it

Professor DeVeaux has been one of the best professors I have ever had during my time at MSU. He cares so deeply for his students by structuring his course in a way that is both digestible and challenging. His lectures are so well prepared and very interesting. It truly reinforced my passion for Marketing and Market Research as a career.

Professor DeVeaux prepares you for the future. There are a good amount of homework and reading assignments, but they are all relevant to the following lectures. The course is very structured on D2L in order to reduce stress and confusion when navigating the course website. He is an incredible lecturer and an even better person. Enjoy his courses.
Great professor, wants you to succeed and give you the materials to help you.
Great professor, cares about his students
The Second half of the semester is much heavier than the first. His expectations only get higher as the course continues. He is very kind though and gives helpful feedback.

The group project course is extremely valuable. Professor DeVeaux is always accessible outside of class for extra help. He expects top work but helps you get there. He is very genuine, caring, and personable and makes a clear effort to be a professor, mentor, and friend. Would recommend taking this course & any other course with Professor DeVeaux!
Great professor, truly cares about his students! Learned a lot from him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing prof!! genuinely cares about his students
The most genuine professor I have ever had!

Professor DeVeaux is an awesome instructor. It's very refreshing to have a professor with who you can make a connection that's not a student-professor relationship. You can be "friends" with this professor and very casual. He gives great critical feedback on all assignments and expects a lot and treats you like a peer on equal terms.
