I took this class online and it was all so easy to follow. Everything is in D2L, Weekly quizzes+PackBack but super easy to do. TAKE ONE OF HIS CLASSES!

Great professor! I'm usually hesitant about online classes, but Professor Timke made is super easy to stay on track with the course. Everything is laid out perfectly on d2l. We just had to watch the lecture plus materials, then do a packback and quiz weekly. I would recommend this class with Prof Timke!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! I had him for PR260, which was online this semester. Even though it was online, he made sure to make the lectures engaging as possible. The content was very diverse and I learned a lot. The exams were easy and followed what was discussed in the lecture videos, which I really appreciated. Would 100% recommend to anyone!
Honestly cannot say enough good things about professor Timke. TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU CAN. Very clear and concise on expectations, cares about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super easy class! The prof is amazing and I would 100% take another class of his. He taught a lot of lessons with personal experience which was awesome. Lots of guest speakers.

Professor Timke is the BEST!!!! He is a great professor, his classes are super interesting, and an overall great and cool guy. He is super understanding and accommodating. I highly recommend. My favorite professor at MSU by far!

PR 260: Amazing person and professor. So kind and makes the course interesting, although you don't need to take heavy notes to get a good grade. The projects are engaging and fun and as long as you try, you'll get a good grade. No sweat class. If you need this PR requirement, it's Timke every time.

Was a very nice professor and seemed to be very understanding. Course had weekly quizzes that you were able to retake as many times as needed to get a grade you were happy with.
Only had 2 homework projects which were graded hard but fair, and had only 3 scheduled exams including the final

Best ADV professor in MSU. Great guy and is willing to help his students succeed in class and in life. He is enthusiastic about what he is teaching and makes learning about advertising actually fun unlike other professors. Overall great guy 10/10.
I loved him. He was a great professor and you could tell he loves to teach:) Definitely recommend taking a class with him! You will learn as well as enjoy being with such a nice professor!

He has done so many things with his life (which he will share), and he is extremely engaging to listen to. Be ready to do an extensive amount of reading. If you don't do readings, the class will be difficult for you. There are 4 "pop quizzes," but he always hints heavily at them. At first, you may not like him, but I promise he will grow on you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the best professors you'll have. His ability to engage students with the material and lead thoughtful conversations is unmatched. He expects a lot from you, but you'll get out what you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: IAH 203 is SUPER reading heavy. I mean having 3-4 readings per week, each of which was at least 30 pages long. Don't try skipping them either, as they're just as important as in-class lectures. Each essay required at least 1 citation from three separate sources. Murphy was very passionate about the subject, making class lectures nice to attend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: yikes brotha
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I have taken so far. Funny but also gets the point across. It is lecture-heavy but in a good way. I would absolutely take it again.

This guy is a joke, my TA absolutely SLASHED my final course participation grade because I only attended one office hour and when I talked with prof Murphy about it he was no help. The participation grade might as well be called how often did you talk to me

Dr. Murphy is incredibly passionate about his work, his students, and the topic of Latin America in general. What other professor would show up in a banana suit to drive home a point about bananas? He's wickedly funny and I enjoyed his lectures (which you need go to if you want to do well on the papers)! Show up, read the books and you'll be fine.
One of the worst professors. He's vague with feedback on papers and his grading is very subjective, unfortunately hes the only professor for this course.
An IAH should be an easy 4.0 and this one is not because the professor and TAs think their class is more important than it is
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: After a month of spotty and slow communication regarding my grade, I ended with almost no understanding of it. I was blindsided by my grade and both my TA and professor dodged many of my question and continued to repeat the same thing, I got the grade I deserved without giving evidence of why they marked me down.

This course should be reviewed for the way grades are determined. One portion of the rubric highlights Attendance and Participation and details the required amount of participation for the course. This grade is discretionary, so the instructor is able to (and will) use a 30% chunk of the grade to give you the grade they want to give you.

Its really all about the TA you get, this class is basically just how well you do on the essays. I never did the readings, went to class a lot in the beginning but then stopped about halfway through the semester and still 4.0, extra credit is given at the end of the semester and its really a grade booster.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: I liked this class, you definitely need to show up to lectures, as far as the reading goes you only really need to read enough to write your papers and do the small pop quizzes they give. Professor Murphy was hilarious though and his lectures were well structured. Seems like a great guy and really cares about what he is teaching, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hands down, best professor I had at Michigan State.  He demands a lot from you, but you end up being a better student for it. You're missing outif you don't take at least one of his classes.
This class was interesting. though i had it at 830 i only missed two and still got a 4.0. going to the recitations was important to further understand and also get help on papers
Great!
I LOVED THIS CLASS.  Edward is extremely helpful, I enjoyed his lectures and did not miss a class.  He is extremely helpful, clear, and very hot.
No Comments
The professor is nice and helpful

I actually DESPISE going to this class every single week. She does not respond to emails, she is extremely hard to understand, and she often makes mistakes in her own problems. She urges the class to ask questions, but then she makes you feel stupid when you do and questions you about your understanding. This is the worst part of my week.

I only went to this professor for the first few months of the semester but during that time she was not very open to help students. She was hard to understand and often made students feel stupid if they were to ask a question. She discouraged students from asking questions but also did not throughly explain the content.

Very sloppy method of teaching, you will be provided hours of videos of him speaking into the webcam with no slides. Your webcam videos will be supplemented with History channel documentaries. The discussion questions are odd to say the least. Overall Philip has a very lazy and poor method of teaching.

He was very knowledgable about the subject which I really appreciated! There was quite a bit of reading and the exams were pretty difficult, but I feel like I learned a lot, and he is a very caring person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Effiong is an awesome guy and knows so much information about Africa. He almost knows too much information. He says that the exams are very simple but they can get pretty challenging. They are easy for him because he knows so much. Graded on four exams and a very easy presentation that you get 15% of your grade for just doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Effiong was very difficult. While I appreciate his expertise, he expected us to memorize very specific information about the course reading. It was difficult to succeed on tests. You had to work very hard for it for a simple IAH course.
Best professor ever. she is very cooperative and gives short straightforward exams. She actually made me love math.
very knowledgeble
Amazing!
Hard to understand.  Hated the class.  Won't explain things if asked, just goes through her notes and expects you to keep up.  I still have problems with calc to this day because of this class.
Awesome prof. The only person who could make me excited for 8am lectures.

Super chill guy, moves very fast in lectures. New slideshow every lecture, but posts them on D2L so you can go back to them if you miss something or just want to study. Super helpful and wants to support your learning. Definitely recommend him if you ever have a chance to pick.

This professor is great, his lectures and labs are engaging and hands-on, and is available outside of class. You must study heavily for this course though, just going to lecture and lab is not enough. Tests are very difficult but not impossible to score well on, especially since he curves. End of semester project helps to study for the final exam!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The in class portion was engaging and a great class. The one thing that I didn't appreciate was turning something in even one day late resulted in a 0. No grace period and very strict on the late policy
10/10 Professor and Academic advisor!!
Zoology goat. Class is super digestible and easy to follow, just make sure to take notes and do the San Diego Zoo modules.
Dr. R is very approachable and willing to help you if you put forth the effort. Sometimes organization is lacking but overall shes a lovely teacher to have.

this is my favorite prof EVER! i've had her twice and will have her again. she is amazing. this class is all guest speakers (which i love). attendance is taken in the form of asking a question in class or posting to a discussion board. such an easy class, and i learned such incredible, inspirational things! i recommend all zoology majors take this.
Her and the TA were awesome. They gave insightful feedback on the project which really helped my grade. Few exams that are easy if you pay attention and the recitation is required but very easy.

LOVE LOVE LOVE this professor. She is so sweet and understanding! Very helpful when you need questions answered, and I love the way she structures her class. She is very passionate and caring for her students!

This professor has always been there when I reach out even when it is general advice about courses and life direction. This is by far one of the best overall professors at Michigan state University. EVER!

The class is easy, but it's a lot of work. You can definitely feel that this class is condensed if you take in the summer. There are no exams and the quizzes are not weighted that much, but you get a ton of attempts on them. The class is steered more towards discussions and scientific writing, so if you're not an exam person I would take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed being a student in BS 182H in Fall 2021! I hadn't taken a biology course since my freshman year of high school, and I was relieved by her ability to teach to all levels of knowledge. The course is flipped-classroom which was tedious for the amount of studying required outside of class, but I easily earned a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All of the lectures were given by guest speakers from different areas of the nation. There are participation points for each lecture that can be earned by asking the guest a question or by writing a reflection. 10 modules from the SDZ are given and lecture topics align with the modules. Just show up, do the work, and pay attention to pass with a 4.

Professor is suuuuper disorganized. The class itself isn't hard, but the grading is looking for specific answers from in-class questions so you have to study her materials not just your notes. Also class is flipped where lecture is done outside of class and then there's in class work based on it.

She's a great professor and knows/loves what she's teaching. Class is easy to follow as long as you watch lectures and complete ICQ's. Exams can be a little tricky but not anything you cant handle as an honors student.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Eila Roberts has a poor class setup as she has lecture videos for students to watch outside of the set lecture period. She assigns in-class assignments during the lecture period and assumes you know the information. During lecture time, she will tend to not answer questions. The "quizzes" are 20-38 questions long and will not release them to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Roberts is a great professor and was very accommodating with the online format due to COVID. Her class was flipped, so that we learned out of lecture and applied our learning during lecture. Her tests were very fair, and she tweaked the format after the first one since it didn't go very well online. We did use a required textbook.

Very passionate and amazing lecturer! The class is very difficult where the content from the quizzes and in class dont seem to always fully line up. I would recommend reading the textbook as it has lots of useful information. Wileyplus is definitely a must even though it seems optional. The labs are very fun but dont help learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very kind and upbeat professor. I enjoyed the labs in this class as they were rather easy. TAs were very helpful as well and led you in the right direction for the lab reports and quizzes. I will say though that the exams progressively got harder and I felt as if what we learned didn't always reflect what we were tested on and were weirdly worded.

Okay so the class is hard, test averages are 60 although the content isn't hard to master. Prof. Eisenlohr is really cool tho. She is passionate about her subject and clearly wants her students to learn. She is really funny and is easy to have casual conversations with. She is also very stylish and always has her hair up in flattering hairstyles.

Eisenlohr was a good professor, she wants her students to learn and answers emails fast. However the quizzes are very difficult and they make up most of your grade, the lectures and notes are base level compared to what's on the quizzes. The labs were very interesting and attendance is mandatory or your report/quiz won't be graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher she knows what she is talking about and knows a lot about subject. Did best to keep students engaged in online environment. Beware Exams are harder than they appear. She doesn't give study guides and lectures are base level and exams ask much more in-depth questions. Use the textbook and you'll be fine

Solid Prof. It takes work, but if you show up to class and prepare for the quizzes, you will get a decent grade. Be sure to do optional assigned problems, and review lecture slides before quizzes. Ms. Eisenlohr was very organized, held engaging labs, and clearly explained all material.

I really enjoyed this class and Prof. Eisenlohr. She is very organized and knows what she is doing. The quizzes aren't that bad as long as you actually study for them (and maybe attend office hours) the labs were very engaging and very related to the rest of the class. I also found the material very interesting. The textbook is very helpful too.

Yeah she can be helpful at times, but lectures are useless. All she does is read off the slides with barely any class engagement. Quizzes are 50% of the grade and are all free response, and grading is very strict. Final is brutal and over content that she least covers. Can be rude at times as well and treats students as kids sometimes. Get ready.

Dr. Roraback was awesome! She was super understanding towards students and would always answer questions clearly. She doesn't give much homework, but when she does the material is always interesting. She prepared students for exams and was overall such an amazing prof. I recommend anyone who's taking IAH to take it with her!
She is very caring of her students, appreciates participation and very lenient on reading assignments! I would definitely recommend, not a harsh grader.

One of my favorite professors I have had! She is very sweet and is caring towards her students. Though attendance is mandatory, she understands things happen and is very lenient. The readings weekly are pretty long, but if you skim them and know enough to engage in conversation you will be fine. Exams are easy if you study with the guide provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sweet professor, boring class. Barely did any of the readings unless it came to the exams but still passed the class with a 4.0. Two papers which are extremely easy and two exams which are exactly like the study guide. She does not grade harshly at all and is really understanding and caring towards her students. Easy 4.0, take her for any IAH class

She is the sweetest professor I've had and my absolute favorite so far. The work isn't necessarily difficult, but it can be tedious at times. If you do a small portion of the readings and skim through a few chapters of your textbook you'll do fine. She gives you a detailed midterm study guide a week before the test, and there's no final exam.
This is a super easy honors course to take. Just do the readings, even though there's a lot, and you won't even need to study for the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall Prof Roraback is a nice lady. I appreciate the somewhat easy A but a little work was required. She didnt seem to spread out the assignments nicely. Nothing for the first few weeks and then you were given 6 at once. Stressful near the end but she is very lenient with the due dates. Quality professor for a filler requirement class.

This class is an easy and enjoyable 4.0. Dr. Roraback is one of the sweetest profs I have ever had. She really cares about her students. There are before-class readings, so you have to review them so you can follow along and participate in class discussion. No final, just a paper, and one midterm. Speak up and participate in class discussion.

Such a sweet professor but her lectures are long and very boring (fell asleep a few times this semester). She takes attendance but you have 4 excused absences. I read maybe 1 thing she assigned this semester and still got a 4.0. Midterm and final exam study guides are the same as the questions provided on exams. I would recommend her!

One paper about yourself, an exam where she gives you the concepts and page numbers that you need to know and a group project on creativity. class thats relevant and interesting too, loved it
Great professor! Class is kind of boring, but she is very caring and a good teacher. Her class was an easy A and not much homework or exams.

Allowed 4 skips during the semester. Assigns readings after every class. 4 hw assignments during the semester and if you do them you get 100% on them. Midterm and final are incredibly easy, she gives a study guide and theexam is the study guide. There is a final group project that is easy. Super nice and chill teacher. Class is boring, but easy 4.0

Wants students to do well! One of the easiest classes I have taken. Class consisted of short assignments, midterm, group project, and final. There was required readings which I didn't do, and still got 99/100 on midterm. Go to class and participate in discussions and it will be easiest class ever. Prof Roraback is such a sweetheart!
Very tough and complex professor. Using sophisticated language isn't helping at all, it's very distracting and a lack of guidelines to help students isn't helping too.

If you participate every class at least once, you will receive A+ 
Very boring class and prof(3 hours with her feel like an entire month), 6ist at times(iykyk), jealous if you show extreme knowledge(she feels challenged) but good grader overall.

reviews.comment: The guidelines say not to claim the professor shows preferential treatment but it seems true. She cares but needs to work on her interpersonal communication.

Took McCallum on study abroad. Ridiculously difficult experience re: student/teacher relations. not a bad person, just unequipped for the support and communication required. conversed with students about change but told us she was "incapable" of scheduling more effectively (despite taking us across the globe?). made several students uncomfortable.

I took McCallum on WGS study abroad. Do not take her class. She is unhelpful, unsympathetic, and otherwise a terrible professor. She is combative towards students who don't know the answer that she wants and has a hard time learning from her mistakes. She preaches holistic learning but I am not sure she knows what that is or how to implement it.

1 frequent cold calling. 'I don't know' was never an acceptable answer. 2 After mid-semester eval, she said many of us reported we felt we were "struggling" to keep up. She thought this was a positive!? 3 Assignments were due at 11pm not 11:59 which was inconvenient at best. Might have said something had she not been so unapproachable.

She's intelligent and takes no prisoners, but she remains my most memorable and most inspiring teacher. As a recent graduate, I find myself remembering her the most. Lots of reading, lots of thinking. You WILL grow as a reader and writer, and while you'll hate it at the beginning, you will (at the very least) respect her in the end.

reviews.comment: If you genuinely want to grow as a thinker, take Prof. McCallum's class. It is brutal, challenging, and worth it.
Pretty much forced to go to lectures, where she goes on about total nonsense things... like space. Nothing means what you think it does with her. Do not recommend her for an IAH prof.

This lady is a nutcase. Don't take this class with her if you have a choice. She rambles about god knows what. But, if you do take it, go to your TA's for help with the papers. The grading is really hard. Participate in discussion. Read the books. This final is going to suck.

If you want to not know what is going on for literally the whole semester, sign up for this class. She rants and rants during lecture. It is impossible to judge what she or the TAs want for the essays.
This class was pretty all right. Be ready to do some reading and serious interpretation, but I'd definitely recommend it.

Intro to English class made extremely difficult and boring due to the fact that each class was spent dissecting a line or maybe a paragraph of 1 poem or story or chapter in a book. Had to perform a play at the end and was only penalized if didn't memorize part - what part of English is that?

This professor is the best I ever had! Yes, she's hard. But her comments are written concisely and are simply written to encourage you to  think deeper, and to become the best student you can! Isn't that what college is all about? If it was a park walk the

This professor is quite brilliant, and yes, sometimes that means that some students don't quite follow along. By no means does she teach an easy class. But it's not impossible either - I've had her for 2 classes and I got a 4.0 in both. I'd suggest her for anyone who wants a challenge.

There are no words to describe how craptacular this woman is and I feel really bad saying that. I highly encourage her to leave university required classrooms and only teach to students with applicable majors.

Wow.  This prof is totally heinous.  The entire class is just a forum for her to rant about her own brilliance.  I have no idea what she (or her TAs) look for in writing assignments, and she chooses way boring books.  I DON'T CARE WHAT KIND OF SPACE I AM SITTING IN, thanks.

Not a really hard class but its nowhere close to easy. All the books we read are about lesbians and dont make any sense. I wrote a paper and talked about symbolism with a very good reason and she writes "the author of the book is very anti-symbolist. good paper overall" and gives me a 2.5.

For sure the worst professor that I've ever had! She yells at students who leave the class to go to the bathroom and threw keys at her TAs! She writes these in-depth, lengthy thesis (which I am convinced half is NOT  from the English language) then reads word for word from it. Horrid.
Horrible

He has three eye clickers throughout the class period and the most boring lectures you can imagine. Easy 4.0 though if you show up, do the quizzes that are easy...

Class itself is very easy, listening to him talk for nearly 2 hours is hard. "Guest speakers" every Friday are either videos of CEOs from the early 2000s or someone from the HB school. As a non-HB major, don't take this class. Most of the answers are self explanatory but he never answered an email or mine or will reverse missed quizzes.

reviews.comment: You don't need to study for this class at all, i guessed in all the of my exams and never got below a 75%, because a majority is what you're taught is basic common sense. I used this class mainly for doing homework for other classes and shopping. Elsworth reads directly off the slides which are almost exact copy-pastes of the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have to attend his lectures every Friday as he takes attendance. They're super boring and just a guest speaker but you can do other work during them as they're not relevant to coursework. The homework is easy and quick and the exams repeat homework questions so they're not bad either. It's an annoying class but it's not difficult.

You have to go to his lectures every Friday. They're super boring but you can just do other work during the class because the lectures don't really have anything to do with the homework/exams. Homework was super easy, exams weren't bad and have same questions as the homework. It's an annoying class but not hard.

Love Elsworth, VERY nice but every class = 25 slides of paragraphs. Nothing bolded or highlighted that you NEED to know on the test + no study guide. He gives 100s on projects, papers but sadly the tests make up most of your grade and it's hard to do well on them. I would say to take notes but it's not even worth it. You will have a hundred pages.

Powerpoint slides contained multiple paragraphs and he just reads straight from them. The exams are extremely difficult because the multiple choice answers all seem like the correct answer. You have to take his class for HB major at MSU, which is horrible. Studying for the exams are impossible, but he does offer a lot of extra credit.

Elsworth wasn't the best. His weekly Friday classes would always be a random guest speaker talking about their experience in HB instead of him actually teaching the class, so unfortunately, his classes are pretty pointless. The class was easy; your only homework you'll have is a weekly quiz on D2L and Pearson Revel, excluding the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is the easiest thing I've done in my life, definitely recommend easy A. Although the professor him self is pretty boring and just reads off slides in his lectures but it's only once a week so it's fine.

He is just very bland and copy/paste directly from the slides. Lecture content is just him reading off purchased slides. Exams just repeat the quiz questions. Content is so basic, just filled with busy work. Stay away if you can. He's been here about 30 years, but his slides and lecture content has barely changed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself was really easy all you needed to do was read one chapter and take an online quiz each week. The lectures are pretty boring and aren't covered in the quizzes or exams.

The amount of reading for this class is ridiculous. You have to pay for the textbook to be able to do your work and 100-page long slide shows you have to go through. He teaches nothing in class at all and also his class is points-based so make sure you do everything even the extra credit. This class was easy though!

I just received my final grade for this class and I am in complete shock. I got a 1.5 on the 4.0 scale for inexplicable reasons. I got a 48/50 on the midterm, I did almost every weekly quiz and attended every single class but somehow my grade appears as a 1.5 on sis? This teacher is extremely boring with almost zero personality,would not recommend
Easily the worst professor I have had in msu, shouts at people if they leave 5 minutes early, makes you buy a physical iClicker despite there being an app for it and he is very boring.

Be prepared for so much reading, like I'm talking 15 to 20 pages of a (dry) textbook, along with slideshows a week. You have two quizzes per week that you have to take, and missing even one can tank your grade. He does a lot of iClicker questions, and also has a lot of guest speakers. Textbooks are expensive and unneeded as you can guess a lot.

Just to sum it up - one subject that he covered contained 63 slides. All with long paragraphs with soooo much content. Its like he breaks up 10 page essays into slides and reads them to you in class. Its horrible. It also makes it hard to study for exams, because there is so much content to read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super boring and pointless lectures. He seems to have no idea what the rest of the HB curriculum entails because he covered topics that I mastered in pre-req's. He takes the entire class period for each lecture and you will have to rush to finish his exams in time so never expect to get out early. Avoid him if you have any respect for your time.

God he is so horrid.  The most cold and closed off professor I've had.  He just rambles on and on for what seems like years and you walk out feeling like you've just wasted 80 minutes of your life.  He always goes off on tangents that don't even relate to what we're doing in class.  Avoid at all costs if you can

I took professor Elsworth's HB 100 and HB 207 courses. The first thing you should know is that the content covered is awful. It is a totally unnecessary class and I really did not learn much, but is required for Hospitality Students. As for prof's teaching its okay. He seems like a really knowledgeable person, but lectures are extremely dry.
lots of reading but easy class. weekly lectures and quizzes. gives 2 bonus quizzes. interesting class. quizzes are easy as long as you do the reading and reading assignment.

I went to this class once. The online access is $100, but you do not need to buy the textbook if you don't want to, everything is on Quizlet. Elsworth is super boring, but every week is a quiz, module, and guest speaker quiz. Takes about half an hour a week. Honestly, if he unlocked everything at once you could finish the entire class in a week.

I had a good experience with prof Elsworth, the class was 100% asynchronous and he had a very detailed weekly schedule put out every week. She literally was my favorite professor ever, she used iClicker for attendance but you were allowed a few days to miss and still get a 4.0. Slay Brandy

Prof Ellison was remarkable and probably the best prof I had in the semester. We had lots of fun classes and museum visits. Assignments were not that tough and could be easily managed. I recommend taking her class.
I took Brandy for my seminar aboard and I loved the class the entire time. She was so caring and helpful for anything we needed help with. I would 100% take her class again.

Dr. Ellison is great! However, I took asynch in summertime (which I would not recommend). I missed a quiz once and she let me make it up by just writing a half page paper on any article! Great professor who actually cares for the well being of her students. I missed an online module one week and she reached out to me through email making sure I was well. Easy class along as you keep up with online assignments.

So much reading and listening to podcasts. The professor told us at one point that the workload should take you 16 hours to complete. When class complained and asked for it to open sooner her response was pretty much I don't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Profesor Ellison is very easy going and understanding. Her projects are fun and interesting and allow you to be creative. Easy class and chill Prof, however, a stupid amount of busy work, like way to much for this class. I on average have about 10-15 things due just for that class, while it is easy the sheer amount is what is insane, especially with heavier class loads.

Extremely chill and likable professor, I couldnt recommend her enough. The group projects are fine and easy if you have a decent group. Lectures were pretty interesting. She constantly gives opportunities for feedback so her class is always improving. Great class for first-year students.
Very laid back and did not have anxiety when going to her class. This course was not stressful at all, it was more of a breather class from all of my other ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take Prof. Ellison, do it. She is one of the best professors I have had and she is very personable. She is so caring of her students and her class is extremely interesting.

reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: So I took this class completely online and it's a really easy course with a really easy professor. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Heavy workload, reading heavy and very short powerpoints. Workload is repetitive and mostly busywork. Course format is difficult to follow. Laid out week by week in D2L but each week has some info for week before and after. Discussion board requirements are difficult to follow with two different charts to use to find when and what to post.

Don't waste your time, and money. Ellison apparently thinks making students read WaPo articles, and watch YouTube is teaching. I get that ISS classes are just mandatory courses in ideology, but this one was a waste of everyone's time.

Professor Ellington did a good job given the online format of the past semester. The lectures could have been more detailed, but aside from that I have no real complaints. She assigns a fair amount of work, but as long as you do it all you shouldn't have a problem.
Beware of discussion boards. Professor Ellison is super nice, but she definitely gave the appropriate amount of work for a 4 credit class, don't expect it to be light.
I found the class to be pretty fun and the professor is very receptive with questions and will provide you with feedback really quick. The quizzes get kinda annoying but they arent bad

The class sounds interesting but I found myself dozing off. The mini quizzes every Monday where you have to answer five questions got old real fast, even though I listened to the assigned podcasts and read the assigned reading I didn't do well on them until the class went online. Pray you have good teammates for the group projects.

Every Monday, there are 5 points quizzes. The material gets confused and can't even find it in the readings. If you do bad on these, like get 3 out of 5 everytime, you will be in bad situation. I hope her quizzes are more easy and not this confusing...

She is a very good professor. Not only is her class very interesting, but she keeps the lectures alive. Class was boring, nothing serious. Just remember to read the online assignments for the weekly quizzes cuz I always forgot.  No exams at all, just a project and presentation :).

reviews.comment: Boring class, pretty much just group work, no final exam.

Professor Engram was disrespectful and handled the school shooting awfully. He was often disrespectful to students in class. He has been one of my least favorite professors during my time at MSU.

Dr. Engram was a pretty good professor, The discussion posts are graded are very strictly and he won't tell you your grade until the end of the year. He does offer volunteering for extra credit which was very helpful.

Although the nature of this course preaches empathy, his actions fail to embody his teaching.

Dr. Engram weighs discussion posts very heavily and gives you absolutely no idea of your standing in the category until final grades are released and you have no way of changing them. At the start of this course, I enjoyed Dr. Engram's. But after a while, I saw that he was extremely difficult, discouraging, and rude. I love the message he speaks on in the class and overall the class material was fine but due to his irrational expectations for students especially after we had all gone through a MASS SHOOTING, it's a no for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Engram is exactly what the kind of professor you fear getting in a course like this. He presents his agenda and is not interested in allowing class discussion on topics causing the class to be silent. He will then take your participation points away. Classic tyrant professor not pleasant to be in his class at all despite interesting topic

This professor is not understanding in the slightest, makes it very difficult to get good grades on things like participation! Take any other ISS class if you don't want to absolutely stress about grades.

I thought a lot of the content he spoke about in class was about his personal opinions not necessarily content from the book. The tests had all content from the book and readings so I was able to study, I just don't agree with his teaching style. I also felt it was hard to give my opinion because if it didn't align with his, it would be a problem.

I wish I could give him a zero. Though many may have negative things to say after the msu shooting, Dr.Engram is by far one of the professors I respect the most. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

Seems to care about student success and therefore makes very organized lecture slides that break down material in a succinct and clear manner. Definitely one of your best bets for an econ professor.

This professor deserves a rating higher than 3.2; her class is tough, but it's a college class, and you can't expect an easy A. If you put in just a little more than the minimum amount of work, you'll be fine. She is a very kind professor who you can tell is passionate about history.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lectures can be boring sometimes and she sometimes talks very fast so it is hard to keep up. You will not pass if you do not show up. She is a great professor and if you like foreign relations you will love this class. I though the papers were actually kinda fun. The quizees are kinda hard, DO THE READINGS. great professor!

When it comes to lectures, the slides give no information and the lectures are reliant on her talking about what is being discussed. She gives multiple readings, some literally being whole books that are 300 pages. When it comes to writing papers, her criteria is horrible and does not explain anything. Just terrible all around to be honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She graded way too hard when her instructions and rubrics were not at all specific. Way too difficult to figure out what she was asking for. A majority of students did an assignment wrong because she lacked the ability to instruct and she gives until the end of the day to redo it. Horrible all the way around

I would take this professor again in a heartbeat. I actually tried to see if she is teaching any other courses that apply to my major and was very upset that she didn't. A lot of reading, but that is expected. Two short group presentations that are very relaxed and both exams were take-home essays. Attendance was not required as long as you read.

Can't believe she doesn't have 5 stars. She was reading-heavy (expected for a 300 class), and her lectures could have been more entertaining, but she's an amazing professor. Due dates and assignments are incredibly reasonable. Genuinely happy to answer any question. In my top 3 for best educators I've had at MSU. Didn't take attendance either!

Professor Conroy-Krutz was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about her class. There was a lot of reading but that is to be expected from a History class. People on here complaining about her lectures want everything handed to them on a silver platter. If you do the readings and listen/participate during lecture, you will learn a lot.

Disagree with most of the reviews on here--she is great! Lectures are engaging, she knows her stuff, and most of the work in the class gets graded relatively easily as long as it's clear that you read the material and learned something from the lectures. She goes fast because there's a lot to cover, but it's not hard to follow or keep up. Big fan!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: She's an amazing professor! Her power points are a little vague, but all of your grades are from essays that you write, anyway. Lectures are really helpful for writing your essays. You do need to know a fair amount of U.S. history, but this is a 300 level history class, so it's obviously not a blow-off class. I learned so much valuable information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Her power points are very vague. She talks way to fast for me to take notes and there is no slowing her down because she is alway behind her schedule. She gives a final exam as an in class essay exam in which you have only a commonplace book with quotes, for your notes. STAY AWAY unless you are in need of boring lecture.

This teacher seemed like she expected you to know the material prior to you attending the class. Her notes are just an outline and you literally have to take notes based on what she says in class. She goes too fast and it is really frustrating. She also expects you to read like 4-5 books during the course. STAY AWAY!!!

A very hard grader. If some people in class do not prepare she punishes the whole class by not explaining the materials. The amount of reading is unreasonable. PowerPoint’s are useless.  rambles, very philosophical,taking notes is hard. course is not organized. Responds to emails very late. Doesn’t acknowledge student’s progress and participation.

Katz cares a lot about her students and what they take away from her classes. Second time having her and I'd recommend with my dying breaths tbh. You'll enjoy the class a lot more if you're engaged and participate in discussions, and her study guides make it very easy to excel on the exams given out. Very helpful with papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's a good professor; knows exactly what she's talking about. However, if you plan on doing at least 5-10 hours of reading a week, this would be the class for you. The reading blocks were very excessive (4 days before class, having 30 pages to read. And 2 days in between classes, having 60 pages to read).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Very good and entertaining professor; provides multiple ways to succeed and cares deeply about the students and the topics covered.

Multiple writing assignments handwritten in class, but a very lenient drop policy allows you to miss classes a couple of times. Exams are strictly based on study guides provided (not many surprise questions).
Nice professor willing to help
The lectures help significantly, if you go and actively participate in class it is not only enjoyable but also engaging and easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: She is the best prof ever! so sweet and loves what she does and her students. Lectures are very interesting, and assignments are easy. Would take again 1000x over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Katz is my favorite professor at MSU. She's kind, funny, and genuinely cares that her students have fun doing philosophy. Her grading is super clear in the syllabus. Make sure you're doing the readings and taking notes. If you can do the basics for this class, you'll be fine. Couldn't recommend her more.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Katz was funny and thorough at the same time. Tests were based entirely on the study guides, so if you fill those out it's incentive to do the readings and be prepared for the tests at the same time. Class itself was easy, though it was more philosophy than anticipated. I enjoyed it a lot, despite wanting more of the sci-fi aspect.

Katz was the best professor I have had so far. She is very passionate about philosophy and is very clear. She manages to be very interactive in such a big lecture. The study guide and the exams are close to identical, so make sure that you stay on top of that and ATTEND CLASS. You definitely won't pass if you don't come to lecture and take notes.

There is a lot of reading to endure in this class if you want to do well, but it's interesting. She goes over the readings the next day & explains it all very well, but if you miss a lecture you have to get notes from someone else as she leaves the slides pretty bare. She provides EC & is easy to reach outside of class & provides great feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was a very kind professor. Her lectures were very clear, and she made philosophy pretty interesting for a stem major. you can tell she is very passionate about Philosophy, and she's very experienced. Exams are completely based on the study guides, so if you don't get an A that's on you. Loved her class, highly recommend for IAH

Very sweet & passionate about what she teaches. If I ever had questions outside of class she was very helpful & timely over email. If you show up to class & engage you should do well, the slides dont always have all the info.Use office hours to your advantage (for any prof). I just wish there would've been a clear study guide for exams.
You will do well if you go to class and engage with the content. Dr. Pomeranz is a good professor and clarifies any confusion if you ask. I learned a lot in this class and enjoyed it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Enjoyed this class a lot. I think a lot of people don't understand how important HD is. She was disorganized at times but in general had informative lectures. Lots of readings but I got by without doing most of them. Exams were a little hard to study for but I found that I was pretty prepared just from taking notes and attending

Dr. Pomeranz completely lost the class a month in, maybe 25% came. Lectures are extremely boring and disorganized, you gain absolutely nothing from going. It's supposed to be a writing class, but 2 exams are worth 45% of the grade, in which she gives zero study references. She does not respect your time either and rambles about nonsense. STAY AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For HST 201 our final was a 15 page paper. Prof. Elliott is very nice and caring, she gives great feedback on assignments preparing for the paper. She is very easy to get in contact with and responds to emails pretty quickly. She also made it clear that she is always willing to help and care for her students. Very passionate about her job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Basically half your grade is one paper, but you spent most of the semester just working on it, so it was ok. Elliott is a great speaker, and the class was very entertaining. She would make us work in groups during class sometimes, which was fine but there were some students that made it suck. Clearly very passionate about Russian history.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Elliot was a very understanding proffessor. She did go through lectures pretty quickly but she does post them at the end of units, but just paying attention helps. There are no tests or quizzes, just 3/4 major writing assignments. She is really timely in replies and you can tell she really enjoys teaching this class. Recitations are also fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: So, shes a little rude, and she goes through notes a lot faster than some people are prepared for. But, Her assignments are very easy and clearly detailed. 4 assignments including the final. Compared to MSU's other ISS 210 course this one is MUCH easier. The other having almost weekly tests and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was super easy. Lectures are not mandatory at all due to her slides being posted before the lecture. Recitation is mandatory but overall only 2 papers for the whole course and 1 test and the final exam. Super easy would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 10/10 Professor that I'd recommend to everyone! She's enjoyable and makes her content easy to understand for the class! Her TA, Scott Bullock, is very understanding! As long as you go to lecture, take good notes, go to recitation, and participate you will surely pass with a 4.0!

Professor Elliot lectures every class and then recitation is set up to talk through her lectures and the assigned readings for the week, I found it to be easy because she posts the power points but I would definitely suggest still going to her lectures. There are pop reading quizzes and very few assignments, so try hard and meet the deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Elliott is very knowledgeable and can lecture the full class period. You have to take notes during the presentations as there is nothing written on the slides for you. She does have an accent that can be difficult to listen to for extended time periods. The assignments are reading and essays   and you have to participate in recitations.
